To be developed across approximately 69.52 acres, the park will play a key role in providing integrated facilities for robotics companies, technology start-ups, research institutions and industries,” read an official statement issued by the State government. State Finance Minister Suresh Kumar Khanna said, “The project aims at promoting indigenous robotics manufacturing in the State, accelerating the development of AI-based technologies, and creating a conducive ecosystem for investment and research in the robotics sector. At full scale, the project is expected to generate more than one lakh direct and indirect jobs and contribute an annual GVA of approximately ₹2,000 crores to the State’s economy.” “The PRAGATI Park will be developed in two zones. Eight acres have been earmarked for Zone 1, which will be developed and operated through a SPV constituted under the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model. 64a16fe7ecfacd7b.title: The SIR and its error margin
64a16fe7ecfacd7b.summary: Updated - October 28, 2026 01:07 am IST ‘The Special Intensive Revision exercise has removed more than 13 crore names from the rolls since June 2025. Over a quarter were claimed dead or duplicated, while most were marked as absent or shifted’ | Photo Credit: The Hindu For nearly a month, Indians across the country have courted the ire and might of the state over a question no citizen in a democratic nation should have to ask. Their anger stems from the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise which has removed more than 13 crore names from the rolls since June 2025. Over a quarter were claimed dead or duplicated, while most were marked as absent or shifted. At one booth in Delhi’s Bela Estate, officials cut 728 out of 729 voters , citing address proof discrepancies. Who decided that so many names should come off the rolls and on what basis? While the political answer is being debated on the streets and in Parliament, it is clear that the SIR has changed how a voter’s place on the roll is decided. In 1995, the Supreme Court held that a name already on the roll should be presumed to be there legally. The SIR replaced that presumption with a data-matching exercise. The Election Commission of India (ECI) has relied heavily on software for a public task where a single error costs a citizen their vote. Rolls from the last intensive revision (mostly in 2002) were hastily digitised from Bengali, Kannada, and other regional languages, auto-transliterated by the machine into English, and matched against new enumeration forms. Then a second layer of “logical discrepancies,” such as a parent-child age gap of less than 15 years, was applied. a38b6eb8a319f142.summary: Updated - October 28, 2026 12:46 am IST - Bengaluru D.K. Shivakumar | Photo Credit: File Photo Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Tuesday sought cooperation from MLAs and MLCs from Bengaluru to break what he called the “garbage mafia” in the city, even as the Bengaluru Solid Waste Management Limited (BSWML) is re-tendering 16 of 21 waste management packages. Mr. Shivakumar held an all-party meeting at his official residence, Krishna, to discuss garbage management and development projects in the city. However, R. Ashok, Leader of the Opposition, who recently alleged irregularities in garbage management tenders, didn’t attend the meeting. Mr. Ashok had accused the government of favouring an ineligible company and demanded a high-level probe into the matter. He said that one of the ₹133-crore tenders floated by the GBA had been awarded to a private company despite the firm failing to meet the eligibility criteria. Meanwhile, Tuesday’s meeting saw discussion about the recent cancellation of tenders. Mr. Shivakumar briefed the meeting on the BSWML’s plan to restructure waste management by awarding 33 contracts for waste collection in 27 Assembly constituencies. The move is aimed at increasing the waste collection capacity in the city and ensuring seamless transportation, he said. The new tenders would provide for the collection of up to 9,000 tonnes of waste. GPS tracking would be mandatory for all waste collection vehicles, and only new vehicles would be permitted under the contracts, he said. According to BSWML officials, only five contractors accepted the waste management tenders. Karee Gowda, Chief Executive Officer, BSWML, told The Hindu that the rest have been demanding a nearly 30% premium on the actual contract value. 9c874c8f5b77aa3c.title: Fouled waters: On Rajasthan’s river pollution
9c874c8f5b77aa3c.summary: Updated - October 28, 2026 01:15 am IST The Supreme Court has pulled up, once again, the Rajasthan government over industrial effluents flowing into the Jojari river and the deadly risk it poses for the people depending on it. The problem is decades old — public interest litigation in the Rajasthan High Court alerted State machinery to the problem in 2011 — indicating an oversight by the State bordering on the systematic. The Jojari, the Luni, and the Bandi are seasonal rivers in the State’s arid western region, flowing through Jodhpur, Balotra, and Pali districts. This region has also evolved as a textile-dyeing and steelworking hub, and untreated or insufficiently treated effluents from these factories have run directly into the rivers and soil, endangering the health of around 20 lakh local residents. The region also suffers rampant illegal sand mining in riverbeds. The sewage treatment plants have been able to accommodate only around half of the sewage generated in the three urban centres, according to the State’s submissions to the Court in 2025, even as the Court recorded substantial underutilisation at common effluent treatment plants. The combination is suggestive of industrial sources bypassing treatment facilities, poor connections between the sources and the facilities, and/or insufficient capacity at particular sites or in specific periods. The Court initiated a suo motu writ petition in 2025 and constituted a High-level Ecosystem Oversight Committee chaired by Justice Sangeet Lodha to audit the plants and draft a plan to restore the rivers. Based on the committee’s scathing status reports, Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta banned construction within 100 metres of the rivers’ edges and hazardous industries within 500 m of the present path, or of the flood lines where available. 47b7d989794ec645.title: Asian Champions Trophy: India slams 13 past hapless Bangladesh
47b7d989794ec645.summary: Updated - October 28, 2026 12:17 am IST - Jalandhar Harmanpreet Singh drew first blood for India. | Photo Credit: X@TheHockeyIndia For a city hosting its first-ever international hockey tournament, the result of India’s opening match in the Asian Champions Trophy (ACT) against Bangladesh was the perfect initiation. But less so for coach Craig Fulton and the team’s long-term plans. With local boys among the scorers and India stamping its authority in the 13-0 win on Tuesday, the result ensured the full house had enough reasons to celebrate. Mandeep Singh — among the five players who began on this very ground of the Olympian Surjit Singh Stadium — struck three of those and created as many. Captain Harmanpreet Singh, another local hero, started the rampage in the second minute and India was up by four in the first 15 minutes and six at half-time. Jarmanpreet Singh and Amit Rohidas, in defence, and Nilakanta Sharma, in the middle, were also impressive. Nilakanta even scored against an opponent that barely challenged the Indian might. Nilakanta, later, announced that he will retire at the end of the tournament. The highlight of the day was the drone show featuring the State, its culture, sporting history and legacy and sparkling under the night sky. The results: India 13 (Harmanpreet Singh 2-pc, 44-pc, Mandeep Singh 3, 10, 54, Shilanand Lakra 15, Abhishek 18, Nilakanta Sharma 26, Dilpreet Singh 43-pc, 44, Jugraj Singh 46-pc, Hardik Singh 60, 60) bt Bangladesh 0; Malaysia 5 (Abu Kamal Azrai 4, 14, Akhimullah Anuar 14, Faizal Saari 34-ps, Azimuddin Kamaruddin 35-pc) bt China 4 (Yaqi Wang 11, Moda Ne 12, Benhai Chen 27-pc, 44-pc); Japan 3 (Kentaro Fukuda 14, Ryoma Ooka 36, Kazumasa Matsumoto 52) bt Korea 2 (Han Sangjun 15, Jeong Junseong 59). 833c8524532cb779.title: Fifty years ago | ITDC plan to build hotels abroad
833c8524532cb779.summary: Published - October 28, 2026 03:45 am IST New Delhi, October 27: Indian Tourism Development Corporation, world’s second biggest public sector undertaking of its kind running a chain of hotels, motels, travellers lodges, beach resorts and forest lodges in the country is planning to set up initially about half a dozen ‘Indian restaurants’ at ‘strategic’ places in the world. According to Lt. Gen J.T. Sataravalla, Chairman and Managing Director of ITDC, now that the Corporation has already built up the necessary hotel infrastructure at important tourist centres within the country, it wants to popularise the famous Indian dishes to the foreigners at these restaurants abroad and also attract them to visit India. The location of these Indian restaurants abroad has not yet been finalised but they will be set up at some of the important world capitals. Some of them are likely to be located in the oil-rich Gulf countries. The managers of these restaurants will be specially trained in marketing Indian tourism abroad. The ITDC, which expects to earn Rs 7 crores of foreign exchange during 1975-76, has already entered the field in giving technical assistance abroad in running hotel industry. It is setting up an Indian restaurant at Prague with Czech collaboration. 833c8524532cb779.headline_en: Fifty years ago | ITDC plan to build hotels abroad
833c8524532cb779.raw_facts: Published - October 28, 2026 03:45 am IST New Delhi, October 27: Indian Tourism Development Corporation, world’s second biggest public sector undertaking of its kind running a chain of hotels, motels, travellers lodges, beach resorts and forest lodges in the country is planning to set up initially about half a dozen ‘Indian restaurants’ at ‘strategic’ places in the world. According to Lt. Gen J.T. Sataravalla, Chairman and Managing Director of ITDC, now that the Corporation has already built up the necessary hotel infrastructure at important tourist centres within the country, it wants to popularise the famous Indian dishes to the foreigners at these restaurants abroad and also attract them to visit India. The location of these Indian restaurants abroad has not yet been finalised but they will be set up at some of the important world capitals. Some of them are likely to be located in the oil-rich Gulf countries. The managers of these restaurants will be specially trained in marketing Indian tourism abroad. The ITDC, which expects to earn Rs 7 crores of foreign exchange during 1975-76, has already entered the field in giving technical assistance abroad in running hotel industry. It is setting up an Indian restaurant at Prague with Czech collaboration. Reddy, founder-chairman, Apollo Hospitals Group, on Tuesday stressed the need to take healthcare to the last mile and urged people to make health a priority. Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Limited (AHEL) and Apollo Foundation celebrated the impact of the ‘Total Health’ model in Aragonda, Chittoor district, Andhra Pradesh. The occasion also marked completion of 1,000 total knee replacements at Apollo Hospitals in Aragonda. Taking part in the event, Dr. Reddy said that Total Health has made a significant impact in people’s health. Noting that his intention is to bring healthcare to the people, to the last mile, he said that the hospital at Aragonda has completed 1,000 total knee replacement surgeries without infections. He recalled that, during an earlier tenure of Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu, Apollo took over the management of the District Hospital in Chittoor, which is now a 800-bed facility. District hospitals providing best care for the public will enable last mile healthcare, he added. Dr. Reddy also emphasised on preventive healthcare, urging people to make health a priority and undergo health check-ups. 3d6fcfb9adea7ad0.title: WPL auction: Sneh among biggest names in the fray
3d6fcfb9adea7ad0.summary: Updated - October 28, 2026 12:28 am IST - Kochi: Sneh Rana has been released by Delhi Capitals. | Photo Credit: File photo: K.R. DEEPAK By the time the first name comes up at the WPL’s mini-auction on Wednesday, the third ODI between India and Zimbabwe would have reached somewhere around the halfway mark in Vadodara. India’s middle-order batter Tejal Hasabnis is likely to be curious about what is happening at Grand Hyatt here. She is one of the 146 players who will go under the hammer. In the only chance she got in the Zimbabwe series, she may have lasted only five balls, but last month she had done really well for India-A against the touring Australia-A. So Tejal should interest some of the franchises. There could be even more interest in Sneh Rana, the off-spinning all-rounder released by Delhi Capitals. Sneh is, in fact, among the biggest names at this auction. Others include Australia’s T20 World Cup-winning captain Sophie Molineux, her compatriots Grace Harris and Jess Jonassen, Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu and England opener Sophia Dunkley. Among the capped Indian players are G. Kamalini, Kiran Navgire, Uma Chetry, Taniya Bhatiya, Saika Ishaque, Asha Sobhana, Priya Mishra, Titas Sadhu and Saima Thakor. There are some interesting names among the uncapped Indians, too. Like the 16-year-old Ira Jadhav, who last year smashed an unbeaten 346 off 157 balls for Mumbai against Meghalaya in the Women’s Under-19 One-Day tournament. There are only 27 available slots — including 20 reserved for the Indians. Going into the auction, UP Warriorz could well be a bit more excited, and anxious, than the other four franchises. Warriorz have the biggest purse of ₹3.75 crore. That is a lot more than Gujarat Giants (1.25 crore), Royal Challengers Bengaluru (1.15 crore), Delhi Capitals (1.1 crore) or Mumbai Indians (90 lakh). It would be fascinating to see how Warriorz try to turn the auction into a mega opportunity. Published - October 27, 2026 09:28 pm IST Terms & conditi

3acdfc41d1732b5e.title: India’s ‘balancing act’ risks eroding Russia’s trust
3acdfc41d1732b5e.summary: Updated - October 28, 2026 01:32 am IST ‘India’s public appeal to Russia to end the endless war in Ukraine can be read as a counter-signal to Washington’ | Photo Credit: Reuters The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, on August 31-September 1, 2026, and the BRICS summit in New Delhi on September 12-13, 2026, were remarkable. Iran received considerably more attention and support from members of both the groups, far more than anticipated. More consequential, however, was the shift in India’s stance on the United States-Israel war against Iran and Russia’s war in Ukraine. Traditionally, the SCO and BRICS summits have offered the three major powers — Russia, India and China — an opportunity to demonstrate their mutual solidarity. For Russia, it is a platform from which it can signal to the West that it is not isolated and still has powerful allies. The expansion of the SCO and BRICS under China’s leadership showcases its growing power to the West. For India, the SCO and BRICS have been useful for demonstrating its strategic autonomy. India has sought to remain welcome in both western and non-western forums, from the G-7 to the SCO and BRICS. a840cc2528aeffa9.title: Sreedharan tells Keralam govt. to ‘ignore’ technical panel’s objections over high-speed rail project
a840cc2528aeffa9.summary: Updated - October 28, 2026 12:29 am IST - Kozhikode Technocrat E. Sreedharan addressing the media in Kozhikode on October 27. | Photo Credit: K. Ragesh Technocrat E. Sreedharan has said that the Keralam government should “ignore” and “overrule” the objections raised by the expert committee which studied the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation’s (DMRC) high-speed rail project proposal connecting Thiruvananthapuram and Kannur. He was addressing the media after delivering a talk on the subject organised by the Malabar Chamber of Commerce here on Tuesday (October 27). The expert panel was constituted by the government to examine the technical, financial and environmental aspects of the project. Transport Secretary K. Biju was its convener, and J. Vinayan, C. Veeramani and Sreedhar Radhakrishnan were members representing the subjects railways, finance and environment, respectively. The committee found the DMRC’s report to be “incomplete” and suggested a detailed examination of the technical, financial and environmental feasibility of the project. Replying to a question, Mr. Sreedharan, however, said that the committee had “no expertise” on the subject and that it had only one railway expert. “They did not properly study the proposal. There were no detailed discussions either. They were asked to focus on five core issues, but they looked at only one. I think the government should ignore and overrule the panel’s report and go ahead with the DMRC proposal. The government has no other way,” he said. Asked if the government was sitting over the proposal because of his political links with the BJP, Mr. Sreedharan said he did not think so. d7c98fa1838bef1b.title: Three girls missing in Tiruvannamalai
d7c98fa1838bef1b.summary: Published - October 28, 2026 12:18 am IST - TIRUVANNAMALAI Three schoolgirls were reported missing after they did not return home from school in Thandrampattu village near Chengam town in Tiruvannamalai on Monday. The police said A. Mahalakshmi, 15, A. Maheshwari, 14, and R. Nithya, 13, had left their house after their parents scolded them for not going to school for nearly a month. The police said that as the girls’ parents stayed in Kerala for work as wage labourers, they visited home occasionally. The three children were under the care of Unnamalai, 65, who stayed at a rented house in Thandrampattu village. Two siblings Maheshwari and Maheshwari study in class X and IX respectively at the Government Girls Higher Secondary School, while Nithya is a class VIII student at the Government High School in the village. The police said that the three girls were upset after their parents scolded them over phone for not going to school. Around 4 p.m , they left home in uniforms and did not return. A case was registered by Thandrampattu police. Special teams were formed to find the children and a probe is under way. File photo: AICC via PTI Lok Sabha member from Wayanad and Congress general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) said it took “immense courage, tenacity and the perseverance of a true warrior” to stand against an “onslaught of lies”, a day after her brother and Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi was acquitted in a defamation case by a court in Uttar Pradesh. Responding to Mr. Gandhi’s post on X, in which he wrote “Satyam Shivam Sundaram”, Ms. Vadra accused the government of using “unprecedented resources” to malign her brother. “This government has spent unprecedented resources on a filthy campaign to malign my brother, to defame him and slap bogus cases on him simply for fearlessly telling the truth. It takes immense courage, tenacity and the perseverance of a true warrior to stand against an onslaught of lies, the way he has,” she said. “One by one the chips will fall. The truth will emerge clear and strong. This is just the beginning,” Ms Vadra added. Mr. Gandhi was acquitted by the MP-MLA court in Sultanpur on Monday (October 27, 2026) in a defamation case arising from his remarks against then BJP president Amit Shah in 2018. A day after the court verdict, he invoked a Sanskrit phrase “ Satyam Shivam Sundaram ”, which signifies truth, auspiciousness and beauty. Nagar branch on Tuesday (October 27, 2026). The workshop was attended by 65 students and 30 teachers from 20 schools in Chennai. A press release said Medical Director Vasumathy Vedantham led the hands-on session, during which students enacted various scenarios involving firecracker-related eye injuries and learned first-aid measures. 73dea3f01655703d.title: ACB arrests Mirchowk inspector, home guard in ₹3 lakh bribe case
73dea3f01655703d.summary: Updated - October 28, 2026 12:46 am IST - HYDERABAD Mirchowk Inspector of Police M. Kondal Rao and Home Guard Abid Ali. | Photo Credit: By Arrangement The Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) arrested Mirchowk Inspector of Police and a Home Guard on Tuesday for allegedly demanding ₹6 lakh and accepting a part payment of ₹3 lakh from a complainant in return for closing a case against his father. According to the ACB, City Range-1 officials caught M. Kondal Rao on October 27 after he accepted the bribe through Home Guard Abid Ali. The ₹3 lakh in tainted currency was recovered from the possession of the home guard, the agency said. The ACB said the alleged bribe was demanded in return for doing an official favour, including closing the case registered against the complainant’s father, avoiding coercive action, and providing future support. The agency said the two police personnel had acted improperly and dishonestly to obtain an undue advantage. Both were arrested and are being produced before the Principal Special Judge for SPE and ACB cases at Nampally for judicial remand. The case is under investigation. The ACB has withheld the identity of the complainant for security reasons. The agency urged people facing demands for bribes from public servants to contact its toll-free number, 1064, for action under the law. 5d5376a954452541.title: City faces extreme groundwater depletion with abysmal levels recorded in Bachupally and Ameerpet
5d5376a954452541.summary: Updated - October 28, 2026 12:43 am IST - HYDERABAD Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply & Sewerage Board (HMWSSB) staff filling water into tankers in Banjara Hills, Hyderabad. | Photo Credit: NAGARA GOPAL Bachupally and Ameerpet in the city stand out among all mandals in Telangana in terms of groundwater extraction, by recording abysmal figures of Groundwater Drought Index (GWDI). A large number of other areas in the city too are facing acute groundwater crisis four months ahead of summer, portending a bleak situation. According to figures obtained from the Ground Water department, ‘Extreme Drought’ conditions with regard to groundwater depth are prevailing in at least fourteen mandals in the Core Urban Region (CURE) constituting the State capital. Five more mandals fall under the category of ‘Severe Drought’. The Groundwater Drought index (GWDI) classifies the mandals based on the groundwater levels, into Normal, Mild Drought, Moderate Drought, Severe Drought and Extreme Drought. GWDI is calculated by dividing the difference between historical mean depth to groundwater table below surface and the given month’s depth to ground water table, with the historical maximum depth to groundwater table for the same month. The historical figures are calculated based on the data from previous 10 years. A GWDI greater than -0.15 is considered normal, -0.16 to -0.3 mild drought, -0.31 to -0.45 moderate drought, -0.46 to -0.6 severe drought, and less than -0.6 extreme drought. Bachupally mandal in Medchal-Malkajgiri district has the worst situation in the State with a GWDI of -2.7, displaying extreme among the extreme drought conditions with regard to groundwater levels. Ameerpet is the next worst with a GWDI of -1.7. Ameerpet also recorded the highest depth of groundwater in the State in the month of September, 2026, at 32.07 metres below ground level (m bgl). 07d1fbd059a91b53.title: Mint Explainer: Who qualifies for the Centre’s Diwali bonus, and how much will they get?
07d1fbd059a91b53.summary: This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you. Subscribe to enjoy similar stories. As Diwali approaches, eligible central government employees are awaiting their productivity-linked bonus payments. The Centre has approved a 30-day ad-hoc bonus for the financial year that ended in March 2026 (FY26), which is typically released in October, during the peak festival season. Based on a monthly emolument ceiling of ₹ 7,000, the maximum 30-day payout works out to ₹ 6,908. The government, which had 3.66 million civilian employees as of March 2025, has not disclosed how many are expected to receive the bonus. Mint explains who qualifies for the bonus and how the payout is calculated. The bonus is available to central government employees in Group C and non-gazetted Group B categories, but excludes Group A and Group B gazetted officers. Group A comprises senior government officers, including Indian Administrative Service (IAS) and Indian Police Service (IPS) personnel; Group B covers mid-level staff in supervisory, executive or administrative roles; and Group C includes operational, clerical, and support roles such as assistants and data-entry operators. Eligible employees of the armed forces and central armed police forces are also covered. The order also applies to employees of Union territory administrations that follow the Centre’s pay structure, provided they are not covered by another bonus or ex-gratia scheme. To qualify, employees must have been in service on 31 March 2026 and completed at least six months of continuous service during the accounting year 2025-26. Employees who completed between six months and a full year of eligible service will receive the bonus on a proportionate basis. The eligible period is calculated in months, rounded to the nearest one. Yes, provided they meet specific criteria. b0c1321bf5ee0a6c.title: Two killed in separate road incidents
b0c1321bf5ee0a6c.summary: Published - October 28, 2026 12:39 am IST - TIRUVANNAMALAI A sub-inspector and a school student were killed in two separate incidents in Tiruvannamalai and Ranipet on Tuesday. The police identified the deceased persons as R. Parthiban, 50, a sub-inspector at Vada Vanakkampadi police station near Vandavasi town, and R. Monish, 15, a class X student at Government High School in Banavaram village in Ranipet. Initial inquiry revealed that Parthiban was returning to Vada Vanakkampadi village after completing bandobast duty at a local temple festival when an unidentified vehicle hit the two-wheeler he was riding. The injured policeman was taken to Government Taluk Hospital in Vandavasi town where doctors declared that he was brought dead. In a separate incident, Monish was returning to his house with his sister on a two-wheeler on Banavaram – Nemili Road in Ranipet when a van hit the vehicle. Monish and his sister were badly injured. The Banavaram police rushed the duo to a Government Taluk Hospital in Sholinghur, where Monish succumbed to injuries. A probe is under way. a081c78fd0cc905d.summary: Published - October 28, 2026 12:25 am IST Two history-sheeters escaped from police station on Tuesday evening. 53250e23fe432246.title: HC asks ex-finance secretary to mute ‘defamatory’ remarks against BJP MP Nishikant Dubey in podcast
53250e23fe432246.summary: Updated - October 28, 2026 03:23 am IST - New Delhi BJP MP Nishikant Dubey. File | Photo Credit: ANI The Delhi High Court on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) asked former finance secretary Subhash Garg to have certain allegedly derogatory remarks against BJP MP Nishikant Dubey muted or beeped out of a podcast. TMC MP Mahua Moitra’s counsel also assured that she would remove certain related allegedly defamatory posts on ‘X’. Justice Tushar Rao Gedela issued summons to Mr. Garg and Ms. Moitra in Mr. Dubey’s defamation lawsuit seeking permanent injunction against them from casting aspersions on him, an apology and damages of ₹2 crore, and asked them to file their replies. Even as the counsel for the defendants sought time to file a response, claiming that the lawsuit “did not paint the correct picture”, the court asked if they could restrain themselves from further disseminating the content in the meantime. The court emphasised that it was aware that both the plaintiff and the former finance secretary were persons of repute and the latter should not have used an “intemperate word” in the podcast. “You cannot use a word like this. Suppose someone said ...[that to you] will you take that lightly? ... You cannot use the word. It is absolutely derogatory. You cannot call anybody by that name. Rest of the things it is debatable issue,” the court orally observed during the hearing. After taking instructions, Mr. Garg’s counsel assured that he would contact the podcast host to mute certain allegedly defamatory phrases in the podcast. The BJP leader has alleged that Mr. Garg, in a podcast/interview, made false and malicious imputations against him on September 17, which was published and circulated to the public on YouTube, Facebook and other digital platforms. e62d7728078d2c65.title: Man held for stealing cars near Katpadi railway station
e62d7728078d2c65.summary: Published - October 28, 2026 12:37 am IST - VELLORE A 24-year-old youth was arrested by Katpadi police for stealing cars near a railway station for the past few months. The arrested person was identified as Stephen Raj, a resident of Vellore. The police said that Raj had given an advertisement on social media seeking temporary drivers. Siva, a driver and the victim, had applied for the job. Raj told Siva that he should hire a cab to drop him in Coimbatore and gave ₹20,000 for hiring the vehicle. However, he told Siva to leave the vehicle at the parking lot with the keys. Siva did as he was told but when he returned to the parking lot, he found the car missing. On being informed, Katpadi police registered a case. Special teams analysed CCTV camera footage and nabbed Stephen Raj from his hideout in Vellore. The police also recovered two cars from him. 80911ff1da1fdc61.summary: Beer maker United Breweries Ltd on Tuesday reported a nearly three-fold jump in consolidated net profit to Rs 134.81 crore in the September quarter, primarily driven by premiumisation, cost efficiency and volume growth. The Dutch multinational brewing company Heineken NV-controlled firm had posted a net profit of Rs 46.34 crore in the July-September period a year ago, according to a regulatory filing. UBL's revenue from operations increased 23.7 per cent year-on-year to Rs 4,623 crore in the September quarter of FY27, compared to Rs 3,737.31 crore in the corresponding period a year ago. 0e03b81fde3ac62d.summary: Markets regulator Sebi on Tuesday extended the deadline by six months, till April 27, 2027, for debenture trustees to comply with requirements governing activities that fall outside its regulatory purview. Under Regulation 9C of the Sebi (Debenture Trustees) Regulations, 1993, a debenture trustee holding a valid certificate of registration is required to transfer activities not regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) to separate business units within a prescribed timeline. The provision was introduced through amendments notified on October 27, 2025, to provide clarity on the scope of activities permitted for debenture trustees. Sebi had initially given six months for compliance. The US Department of Defense released 28 PDF files in its latest disclosure , the seventh batch released under an executive order signed by President Donald Trump earlier this year. The documents include a memorandum from the Pentagon's All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) and a statement the agents provided to the FBI . However, the documents do not establish what the object was, how it operated or whether it represented an advanced aircraft, a drone or another phenomenon. The reported observations remain unverified explanations of the object's identity. According to their FBI statement, the agents were alerted to the object by a third agent stationed nearby. They repositioned themselves and spotted a dark object above a ridgeline several miles to the west, against the evening sky after sunset. The agents described it as a substantial, non-reflective, black triangular craft resembling a delta-wing drone. They estimated its wingspan at between 9 and 15 feet, its depth at 6 to 9 feet and its thickness at 1 to 2 feet. The memorandum described the object as having a matte-black, featureless exterior. Investigators said it ascended vertically by approximately 200 to 300 feet without tilting, swaying or wobbling. The agents reported that the ascent took place in complete acoustic silence. Every month the Chief Minister orders a new audit of all buildings, then every month huge bribes are being extracted in the name of audits and inspections,” AAP Delhi president Saurabh Bharadwaj said. Mr. Bharadwaj alleged that the fire and revenue departments have also started “collecting regular bribes” from hotels and restaurants. Mr. Bharadwaj shared on X photographs of Chief Minister Rekha Gupta inspecting the trial run of ‘Namo Yamuna Cruise Safari’ and said the Chief Minister did not have time to meet the relatives of those who died in the latest building collapse incident in Harsh Vihar. “Today, she is laughing and giggling while a ‘boat’ is being called a ‘cruise’. Why don’t you call it Titanic? Reminds me of a photoshoot by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in a fake classroom after 25 years of BJP rule in Gujarat” he said. Meanwhile, Delhi BJP spokesperson Praveen Shankar Kapoor said, “Before making such statements, Saurabh Bharadwaj should have remembered that the concerned Gokalpuri Assembly constituency [under which Harsh Vihar falls] and municipal ward have been represented by AAP MLAs and councillors for several years. According to the police, the crackdown was launched based on information from the district hospital about the deaths of two people on October 15 and 18, whose families alleged that they died after consuming liquor. The Dewas district administration, however, had earlier dismissed new reports and Congress claims, denying any deaths related to spurious liquor while saying that the samples of the two deceased who underwent post-mortem examinations have been sent for forensic tests for clarity. It also said that various liquor samples tested following locals’ allegations were not found to contain poisonous contents. e80568339f935cea.title: Fifty years ago | Foreign bank accounts: 400 cases detected
e80568339f935cea.summary: Published - October 27, 2026 02:40 am IST Madras, October 26: A huge basket of foreign currencies and securities, equivalent to about Rs 30 lakhs, held by Indians in banks abroad have been detected by the Central authorities. Nuclear scientists, engineers, and economists of Karnataka, doctors of Calcutta and East African repatriates in Bombay, account for a big chunk of the over 400 cases that have come to light. The drive launched early this year, gained momentum in recent months and paid rich dividends in August and September, during which a majority of these cases were discovered. Quite a few of the cases, officials say are from Karnataka and the persons involved belong to various professions, who managed to secure employment in West European countries. In West Asia also, the State has contributed a bulk of semi-skilled craftsmen, like tailors and carpenters. Of late, there has been a big spurt in the number of Indians going abroad on assignments from the United Nations and other international agencies, or seeking lucrative positions in West Asian and West European countries. As part of the crackdown on smuggling activity, the Central authorities started enquiries about the various persons who went for employment abroad and returned to India after the tenure of their duties outside but retained their foreign bank accounts. This type of foreign holdings is lapped by foreign exchange racketeers to finance smuggling into India. 62712cb91e80caa1.title: A ready solution to tackle anaemia
62712cb91e80caa1.summary: Updated - October 27, 2026 01:18 am IST ‘At an estimated cost of ₹14-₹20 per person annually, DFS represents one of the most affordable population-level nutrition interventions available’ | Photo Credit: Getty Images/iStockphoto Despite significant economic progress and sustained public health efforts, anaemia — driven significantly by iron deficiency — continues to be one of India’s most pressing public health challenges. Affecting over half of Indian women and almost three-fourths of children, anaemia contributes to maternal mortality, an intergenerational cycle of malnutrition, impaired cognitive development, reduced productivity and substantial economic losses. The Government of India’s 7X7X7 Anaemia Mukt Bharat (AMB) strategy, which was launched recently, rightly recognises the multifactorial nature of anaemia through a comprehensive approach spanning prevention, screening, treatment, dietary diversification and behaviour change. Yet, one proven preventive intervention remains significantly underutilised. That intervention is Double Fortified Salt (DFS) — salt fortified with both iodine and iron. Salt offers an unparalleled opportunity to address iron deficiency. Consumed daily by virtually every household across India, in predictable quantities regardless of income or geography, it is uniquely suited to deliver a preventive nutrition intervention at population scale. DFS also addresses one of the fundamental challenges of anaemia control — sustained compliance. Delivering iron through an everyday food complements interventions such as iron supplementation and dietary diversification, whose effectiveness depends on regular adherence. India already has one of the world’s most successful public health platforms in Universal Salt Iodisation, with around 95% of households consuming iodised salt. Building on this existing infrastructure, DFS is already distributed to an estimated 76 million people across four States through government safety-net programmes. Global a

d5d6d8a6965a1182.title: Maharashtra will prioritise its own interest on Telangana barrage project, says Fadnavis
d5d6d8a6965a1182.summary: Published - October 27, 2026 01:35 am IST - Mumbai Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis told the Telangana delegation that Maharashtra had maintained a policy of resolving issues with the neighbouring States through cooperation. File | Photo Credit: @CMOMaharashtra/X via PTI Maharashtra will prioritise its own interest while co-operating with Telangana for a barrage project, Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said on Monday (October 26, 2026). He met with Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy in Mumbai regarding the proposal to increase the height of Tummidihatti Barrage. The two States have agreed to form a joint committee, comprising the Chief Secretaries and the Secretaries of the Water Resources Departments of both the States. It will examine the technical aspects and the potential area of submergence in Maharashtra. Telangana government has sought Maharashtra’s nod to increase the height of Tummidihatti Barrage from 148 meters to 152 meters. The Tummidihatti Barrage is proposed to be built on the Pranahita River near Tummidihatti village in Koutala mandal of Komaram Bheem Asifabad district in Telangana. It will help meet the long-pending drinking and irrigation demands of north Telangana. The project targets the historically neglected tribal communities in the erstwhile Adilabad district. Telangana has proposed to build the barrage at 150 to 152 metres. In Maharashtra, it will lead to the submergence of 1,000 to 2,300 acres of land, depending on the height of the barrage. Telangana has offered to compensate affected farmers in Maharashtra as per Maharashtra’s land-acquisition and rehabilitation guidelines. Mr. Fadnavis told the Telangana delegation that Maharashtra had maintained a policy of resolving issues with the neighbouring States through cooperation. 237321f83a024ae4.title: Kharge’s remarks on PM reflects desperation: BJP
237321f83a024ae4.summary: Published - October 27, 2026 12:35 am IST - MANGALURU The BJP said on Monday that the language used by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge regarding Prime Minister Narendra Modi at an event held in Patna represents the height of baseness and desperation. It is a true reflection of the Congress mindset, said Satish Kumpala, Dakshina Kannada president of the BJP, in a statement. Such a conduct by Mr. Kharge, who possesses extensive experience in holding key responsibilities in public life, is highly condemnable, Mr. Kumpala said. Such statements from Congress leaders, who are restless due to their lack of power, are contributing to their own downfall. Their arrogant attitude stems from the belief that they alone have the inherent right to rule the nation, he said. Mr. Kumpala demanded that Mr. Kharge apologise for his remarks. In a separate statement, Mangaluru City South MLA D. Vedavyasa Kamath said that Mr. Kharge’s remark is unbecoming of his seniority. The BJP MLA said that the Congress and its leaders, having failed to win the trust of the nation’s people, are clearly in a state of desperation. The language used by Mr. Kharge reflects his own character rather than causing the slightest harm to the dignity of Mr. Modi, he said. It is unacceptable that Mr. Kharge lost his composure during a speech and levelled baseless insults at the Prime Minister’s father. Senior leaders like Mr. Kharge, who possess extensive political experience, ought to speak with responsibility, he said. 5be8a5d997bb6e9a.title: Delhi CM inspects Yamuna cruise trial run ahead of Nov. launch
5be8a5d997bb6e9a.summary: Published - October 27, 2026 12:09 am IST - NEW DELHI Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta poses for a picture with Delhi Minister Kapil Mishra during the trial run of ‘Namo Yamuna Cruise Safari’ at Sonia Vihar, in New Delhi on Monday. | Photo Credit: ANI Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Monday inspected the trial run of Delhi’s first-ever cruise service, ‘Namo Yamuna Cruise Safari’, likely to be launched before Chhath Puja in mid-November, as per a statement from the CM Office. The cruise service, being developed along an approximately six-kilometre waterway between Sonia Vihar and Jagatpur, is intended to offer Delhi residents a unique experience and will open up new tourism as well as employment opportunities in the capital, Ms. Gupta said. According to the statement, the cruise will accommodate 30 passengers on a round trip and is expected to take around 35 to 45 minutes. The trial run is planned to continue for about a week, followed by preparations for a formal launch in the first week of November, it added. The project includes food kiosks, a restaurant, a kids’ zone and other essential public amenities for visitors, the CMO statement said. “The initiative is an important step towards developing an attractive tourism destination for families. While tourism facilities are being developed, equal attention must be paid to keeping the Yamuna clean and protecting the environment,” the CM said. 0724717512953079.title: Beyond Kudankulam’s fence, a cybersecurity challenge
0724717512953079.summary: Updated - October 27, 2026 01:20 am IST ‘An organisation’s security depends not only on its own safeguards but also on those of every other entity that has access to its data’ | Photo Credit: Reuters The data breach involving files related to the Kudankulam nuclear power project in Tamil Nadu, reported on July 15, 2026, indicates that India’s cybersecurity policy for critical infrastructure is behind the perimeter that now extends well beyond the actual sensitive facility. The most consequential breach may never touch the facility at all. It could occur in a rented server in a commercial data centre or even within a contractor’s network which has documents that the contractor is entitled to possess. That, in essence, is what appears to have happened in the case of Kudankulam. And that is why the incident deserves more attention than the reassurances that followed would suggest. In mid-July, the group World Leaks began posting sections of an alleged leak of nearly 19,000 files totalling 14.3 GB relating to Kudankulam on its dark web portal. As reported by Reuters, the material spans the years 2016 to about 2025. It includes engineering drawings, supplier information, inspection records, meeting minutes, and insurance documents. The breach was confirmed by Reliance Infrastructure — it won the engineering, procurement, and construction contract for Kudankulam Units 3 and 4 — and added that the data had been stored on a server by its third-party data centre Yotta. It also said that the government had been notified. Yotta confirmed ransomware activity on its site on May 29, and said that the activity has been contained. By June the attackers were claiming the data and demanding a ransom. The Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL) said that the information was only on documents relating to non-nuclear infrastructure, and unrelated to systems supporting nuclear safety. 2ccb91c74187e6c9.title: Indian Army should stop playing Iqbal’s Sare Jahan Se Achha, says DU V-C
2ccb91c74187e6c9.summary: Published - October 27, 2026 12:15 am IST - NEW DELHI The Indian Army should stop playing Muhammad Iqbal’s Sare Jahan Se Achha in its military bands, Delhi University Vice-Chancellor Yogesh Singh said on Monday. Mr. Singh was speaking at the launch of a book authored by Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) veteran R. Hari, titled ‘The Story of Vande Mataram’. The book, which was translated from Malayalam to English, was launched at an event organised by Prajna Pravah’s Delhi Prant — the regional unit of the intellectual wing of the RSS — in association with Indus Scrolls Press. Addressing the gathering, Mr. Singh questioned what he described as the contrasting attitudes of a “certain section of society” towards Vande Mataram and Iqbal’s Sare Jahan Se Achha . He argued that some people proudly sing Iqbal’s patriotic composition while refusing to sing Vande Mataram . Alleging that Iqbal later advocated ideas associated with Partition, Mr. Singh questioned the continued use of Sare Jahan Se Achha by Indian Army bands. “The Army should stop playing this song in its band,” he added. Former Kerala and Bihar Governor Arif Mohammad Khan, who was the chief guest at the event, contested Mr. Singh’s interpretation. He argued that while Iqbal’s views changed over time, the poet had once deeply loved India. Emphasising that individuals’ opinions can evolve, Mr. Khan offered a different perspective on the poet’s political and intellectual journey. “ Vande Mataram is not merely a patriotic song; it is an enduring symbol of our civilisational identity, our struggle for freedom, and our collective aspiration for national unity,” Mr. Khan said. Meanwhile, Prajna Pravah national convenor J. Nandakumar alleged that Vande Mataram had historically been curtailed to just two stanzas by previous governments. “The Congress cannot claim credit for Vande Mataram ,” he said. He described 2026 as a moment of renewed prominence for the song, suggesting that it is making a strong comeback in public

b95db81f08ebada4.summary: Updated - October 27, 2026 01:11 am IST The National Medical Commission (NMC) has denotified and withdrawn its 2023 Maintenance of Standards of Medical Education Regulations (MSMER ), diminishing the framework of penalties vis-à-vis educational standards and infrastructure at medical colleges. The move is noteworthy as the MSMER provided for fines of up to ₹5 lakh on faculty members and administrators for submitting false information. Fortunately, the Medical Assessment and Rating Board (MARB) retains the power to fine errant institutions up to ₹1 crore under the 2023 Establishment of Medical Institutions, Assessment and Rating Regulations . MSMER was lauded for its intention to crack down on the deep-seated corruption and malpractice in medical colleges, particularly over ‘ghost faculty’ and ‘ghost patients’. The NMC’s justification is that MSMER also introduced a parallel mechanism allowing undergraduate and postgraduate boards to evaluate institutions, stepping on the MARB’s toes. However, why the NMC scrapped MSMER wholesale is unclear. The 2023 Postgraduate Medical Education Regulations remain in force and include a provision to fine individual faculty members at postgraduate medical colleges. Non-compliance among medical colleges is not uncommon and seldom nipped in the bud, even as the number of medical seats swells while the transparency of the medical education system has not improved. Notwithstanding the provision to fine individuals at postgraduate centres, the MARB and the NMC can only penalise institutions, which is harder and risks creating a perverse incentive to accommodate rather than punish, and could mitigate the fear that keeps administrators honest. MSMER also specified timelines to appeal penalties. Although the MARB regulations retain the appeal processes, their 15-day deadline could conflict with the 60-day period under the NMC Act, potentially creating legal disputes that delay penal action. "Teamwork makes us invincible. This is a great honour," de la Fuente said after collecting the award at a ceremony in London. "The secret is to work with very generous players that put the team first. We've got such an amazing pool of talent, the best in the world, so as a coach I have such a great amount of talent to work with. So this is their success," he added. In an age of coaches who were previously star players, 65-year-old de la Fuente stands out as a technician who worked his way up through the national coaching ranks in Spain. After a solid career as a player led to an undistinguished stint in club coaching, he was flicking through the sports pages in 2013 when he saw an advert placed by the Spanish Football Federation for a youth team coach. He applied, got the job with Spain's Under-19s, and 13 years later, some of the players from that squad were part of the teams he has led to victory in the Nations League, Euro 2024 and then the World Cup. De la Fuente insisted from the start in the United States this summer that he had the strongest squad in the tournament, even when they stumbled to a goalless draw against World Cup debutants Cape Verde in their opening match. They built momentum with each match and dispatched one of the pre-tournament favourites, France, in a clinical 2-0 win in the semi-final. In a tight final against Lionel Messi's Argentina in New Jersey, de la Fuente's men kept their cool in the face of muscular tactics from the opposition and Ferran Torres smashed in the winning goal for a 1-0 victory. 4c0671524384074d.summary: Published - October 27, 2026 12:56 am IST ‘In September 2026, Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra, who masterminded Operation Sindoor as the Western Air Command chief, was rewarded with the plum job of running the Ram Janmbhoomi temple’ | Photo Credit: X/@IAF_MCC via PTI Last July, at a seminar in New Delhi on atmanirbharta, the then maintenance chief of the Indian Air Force (IAF), Air Marshal Sanjiv Ghuratia, delivered an address that contained, as one person in the audience reported “more Sanskrit than English or Hindi”. Another attendee wondered who Mr. Ghuratia was speaking to; the entrepreneurs and engineers in the audience or to the Sangh Parivar members who needed a demonstration of his Hindu credentials. For generals, admirals or air marshals looking for post-retirement employment, Hindutva pays. Last month, Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra, who masterminded Operation Sindoor as the Western Air Command chief, was rewarded with the plum job of running the Ram Janmbhoomi temple . Nothing an IAF pilot learns during his career equips him for such a delicate job in such a volatile environment. This Hindutva-isation of the military is not new. On May 13, 2025 at a crucial IAF media briefing on Operation Sindoor, the IAF’s operations chief, Air Marshall A.K. Bharti, invoked the Ramayan. His briefing commenced with militaristic Hindutva overtones, the Shiva Tandava Stotram delivered in rock concert style. Military audiences in New Delhi are no longer surprised when government-affiliated speakers pepper their speeches with Sanskrit shlokas . For no apparent reason, the IAF appears to be more Sanskrit-ised than the other two services. 14db5c7bc03990ff.title: Results of Karnataka Legislative Council polls to be announced today
14db5c7bc03990ff.summary: Published - October 27, 2026 06:15 am IST - Bengaluru Voters show their IDs as they wait in a queue to cast their votes in the North-East Teachers’ Constituency Legislative Council election, in Kalaburagi on October 23 | Photo Credit: ANI Counting of votes polled in four graduates’ and teachers’ constituencies of the Karnataka Legislative Council will get under way on Tuesday morning, and results are expected later in the day. As many as 43 candidates, including three sitting members, are in the fray. Of the total 3.43 lakh voters across four constituencies, 2.01 lakh voters have cast their votes in the elections held on Friday. Prominent among the candidates is five-time MLC and former Deputy Chairman of the Upper House Puttanna, who is contesting on the Congress ticket to retain his seat from the Bangalore Teachers’ constituency. The other three constituencies — Karnataka South East Graduates’, Karnataka West Graduates’ and Karnataka North East Teachers’ — are held by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) currently. Sitting members S.V. Sankanur and Sashil Namoshi are contesting from the West Graduates’ and North East Teachers’, respectively. Mr. Sankanur is being challenged by former MLC Mohan Limbikai. With the BJP sitting member of the South East Graduates’, Chidanand Gowda, opting out of the contest, the BJP has fielded K.M. Suresh against Shashi Hulkuntemutt of the Congress. Currently, the Congress holds a majority in the 75-member Council, as it has 38 members, while National Democratic Alliance partners BJP and Janata Dal (Secular) have 24 and six members, respectively. Five seats, for which the government has to nominate members, are currently vacant. One seat is held by the Chairman, and the other is represented by an Independent. As part of the electoral alliance, the BJP is contesting to retain the three seats, while the JD(S) has fielded its candidate from the Bangalore Teachers’ constituency. The ruling Congress has contested all four seats. Published - Oc

cf1c1bbee86f8823.summary: Published - October 27, 2026 12:28 am IST - PUDUCHERRY The Port Department on Monday hoisted the warning signal No.3 indicating cyclone alert and squally weather for the coast in Puducherry. | Photo Credit: S.S. KUMAR Despite precautionary measures adopted by the administration, several urban areas of Puducherry experienced waterlogging during the recent spell of rain. The rain that lashed Puducherry on Saturday night had led to waterlogging in several low-lying areas of Rainbow Nagar, Krishna Nagar, Venkata Nagar, Balaji Nagar, and adjoining places near these residential colonies. Certain residential areas in Reddiyarpalayam area and main roads, including the Sivaji Statue junction on East Coast Road, also faced inundation for a few hours during the rain. The Irrigation wing of the Public Works Department estimates that the region recorded 9. 7 cm of rainfall between 5. 30 p.m on Saturday and 8. 30 a.m on Sunday. The worst affected places in the rain was Rainbow Nagar with water entering the ground floor of some houses in the 4th, 7th, 9th , and 11 th crosses of the residential colony. “Water started receding only by Sunday evening. As our area is prone to waterlogging, immediately after heavy rain started we moved household items to the first floor. The entire premises of the house and ground floor got filled with slush,” Praseed Thambi, a resident of 4 th Cross Rainbow Nagar said. Vinayakam, a resident of Krishna Nagar Main Road, said the flood mitigation measures have worked in certain places but still lot more needs to be done. “Many streets still face water stagnation. Water enters ground floor of several houses. People are more prepared these days in relocating household items, especially electronic equipment, during heavy rains. But we have to spend money and time for cleaning up the premises,” he said. Anticipating heavy rain, the government had declared holiday for all schools in Puducherry on Monday but the region witnessed a dry spell throughout the day.

1b1b917a9963f85f.title: Minister Vanni Arasu inspects rain affected areas in Kallakurichi
1b1b917a9963f85f.summary: Published - October 27, 2026 12:26 am IST - VILLUPURAM Tamil Nadu Minister for Social Justice Vanni Arasu inspecting rain-affected areas in Kallakurichi district on Monday. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT Minister for Social Justice Vanni Arasu inspected rain-affected areas in Kallakurichi district and directed officials to strengthen precautionary measures. Accompanied by Collector J.E. Padmaja, the Minister visited Porasakurichi and Virugavur villages in Thiyagadurgam block. He said the district administration had taken precautionary measures for the Northeast monsoon. He instructed officials to identify vulnerable areas, monitor preparedness and respond immediately to rain-related problems. They were also asked to compile details of local volunteers and coordinate with them during emergencies. The Minister also directed Health department personnel to monitor all areas to prevent outbreaks of infectious diseases. Officials were told to ensure chlorinated drinking water, uninterrupted electricity supply and prompt delivery of essential services. Calls received at the district control room should be attended to immediately and referred to the departments concerned for action, he said. 67a2deec1075020f.title: Badoni notches up his sixth First Class hundred as Delhi dominates day one
67a2deec1075020f.summary: Updated - October 27, 2026 12:26 am IST - RANCHI On song: Badoni put on a masterclass in facing spin, cutting, driving and sweeping with regal ease. In his previous Ranji Trophy innings, Ayush Badoni amassed a career-best score of 217. In his previous innings against Jharkhand, in the 2024-25 season, he had racked up 205. There was an air of inevitability, then, to the 26-year-old sparkling on day one of Delhi’s Ranji Elite Group-C duel against Jharkhand at the JSCA International Stadium. On a balmy Monday in Jharkhand’s capital, Badoni brought up his sixth First Class hundred and remained unbeaten on 106 to steer the visitor to 309 for five at stumps. As chanceless as Badoni’s ton was, he couldn’t have helped Delhi stage a commendable recovery without the company of Sumit Mathur, who contributed 50 in an unbroken partnership of 128 for the sixth wicket. A moment of fortune fell Mathur’s way as he was called back on 36 despite holing out at long-on because Anukul Roy had overstepped. Other than this lapse, the partnership between Badoni and Mathur struck no false note. On a pitch where all five wickets fell to the tweakers, the Delhi skipper put on a masterclass in facing spin, cutting, driving and sweeping with regal ease. He consumed just 111 deliveries to reach the three-figure milestone. Such authority seemed a distant possibility when Delhi was reduced to 181 for five. In the first session, Priyansh Arya and Sanat Sangwan were undone by off-spinners armed with a newish ball. d460e1da8a95e805.title: Harsh Vihar building cave-in:two bodies pulled out afterovernight rescue operation
d460e1da8a95e805.summary: Published - October 27, 2026 12:14 am IST - NEW DELHI NDRF carries out search and rescue operations following a building collapse in Harsh Vihar on Monday. | Photo Credit: ANI The bodies of a 60-year-old man and his 33-year-old son were recovered from the debris of a building that collapsed in north-east Delhi’s Harsh Vihar on Sunday night, following an overnight rescue operation, police said on Monday. “Preliminary inspection revealed that the ground-floor structure of an old building, which reportedly housed a godown, had collapsed along with the first-floor structure constructed above it,” said a senior police officer. The incident was reported at 6.46 p.m. on Sunday. Two fire brigade vehicles, two ambulances and a crane were deployed at the spot. Civil Defence volunteers and an NDRF team also assisted in the rescue operation. However, some family members alleged that the rescue work was slow and tried to remove the debris themselves. The deceased, Chanderpal and his son, Vijay, worked at the site, the officer said. The police has arrested the owner of the building, Manoj Kumar, under Sections are 290 (negligence during construction) and and 106(1) (death by negligence) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. The bodies were taken to Guru Tegh Bahadur Hospital for postmortem examination, following which they were handed over to the family members. “They were the only breadwinners of the family. We were hoping that they would be rescued alive,” said one of the relatives. An investigation is under way to ascertain the circumstances leading to the collapse, police said. Ministers Kapil Mishra and Ashish Sood also reached the spot late Sunday night to assess the rescue operation. Mr. Mishra said that the illegal construction taking place is the direct cause of these incidents. “The government stands firmly against illegal construction and strict action will be taken against anyone found guilty,” Mr. Mishra said. 4caaea41ea28701f.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday agreed to examine a plea challenging the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Maharashtra. A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued notices to the Centre, Election Commission of India and others on a plea filed by Arun Anandagiri, a chartered accountant and journalist by profession. Senior advocate Arvind Datar, appearing for the petitioner, submitted that voters temporarily relocated during redevelopment in Mumbai and Pune have been deleted as "person not found". He said around 20 million out of the 97.9 million total voters in Maharashtra have been deleted from the draft rolls and another 12.2 million electors have been struck off under "logical discrepancies". The petition stated that till the issue is adjudicated by the top court, the revision exercise in the state should be kept in abeyance and no voter whose name appeared in the pre-SIR list should be excluded or deleted. 52a82861d38f88c2.title: LTCG news: Budget 2027-28 may cut long-term capital gains tax for both domestic and foreign investors, says report
52a82861d38f88c2.summary: The government is considering lowering the long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax from the current 12.5% and allowing foreign investors to calculate capital gains in dollar terms instead of rupees as part of efforts to improve stock market sentiment, The Indian Express reported. The proposals are reportedly under discussion ahead of the Union Budget 2027-28. The potential changes would seek to address concerns among domestic and foreign investors amid a prolonged period of subdued stock market performance. Officials cited two key concerns behind the discussions: weak or negative stock market returns over the past two years and sluggish wage growth, which have weighed on investor sentiment, particularly among the middle class. Earlier this month, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman described the debate surrounding LTCG tax as “healthy” and said she was “keen” to hear different perspectives on the issue. Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy forum, Sitharaman said both domestic and foreign investors had raised questions and shared their views on LTCG tax and the Securities Transaction Tax (STT). The debate on taxation in financial markets and the tax treatment of different asset classes had been widely discussed, she said. Her remarks come amid growing investor scrutiny of India's capital gains tax structure and speculation over possible changes in the upcoming Budget. Retail participation in Indian equity markets increased sharply after the Covid-19 pandemic as investors sought to diversify their portfolios and supplement their regular income. Retail investors are generally defined in this context as individuals holding shares worth up to ₹ 2 lakh. However, the stock market's lacklustre performance over the past two years, combined with limited wage growth in the private sector, has raised concerns about household investment returns and consumption sentiment. 0415035c3ab32dde.title: Monsoon wet spell to pause over T.N.; rain likely to revive on November 1
0415035c3ab32dde.summary: Published - October 27, 2026 05:30 am IST - CHENNAI The Northeast monsoon, which was in its active phase, brought the much-needed rainfall over the State since its onset in mid-October. | Photo Credit: VELANKANNI RAJ B Tamil Nadu is in for a brief hiatus from the monsoon wet spell, with rainfall likely to taper off over most parts of the State from Tuesday. Most parts of the State may begin to experience largely dry weather till November 1 except for isolated rainfall of moderate intensity over the southern and Western Ghats districts. The Northeast monsoon, which was in its active phase, brought the much-needed rainfall over the State since its onset in mid-October. Tamil Nadu has recorded an overall rainfall of 21.5 cm, 58% above the monthly average. The State receives an average of 44 cm of rainfall during the entire season. Officials of the RMC said the intensifying cyclonic storm Arnab is expected to draw moisture-laden winds towards it. It is likely to make landfall between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, close to Yanam, as a very severe cyclonic storm by Wednesday. As the cyclone moves away from the Tamil Nadu region, dry weather would return over the State, bringing only isolated rainfall over south and Western Ghats districts till the month-end. The monsoon is interspersed with dry spells, which may sometimes last longer, said V.R. Durai, head, Regional Weather Forecasting Centre, RMC. With the moisture drawn away from the State, winds would shift from the seasonal northeasterly to dry, westerly or northwesterly winds. The prevailing low pressure area over Bay of Bengal and adjoining south coastal Tamil Nadu would also merge with the intense storm by Tuesday. However, cool winds from the Arabian sea would facilitate cloud cover and sustain rainfall over south Tamil Nadu this week, he said. 6399265726a8c897.title: Woman undergoes treatment for critical brain haemorrhage
6399265726a8c897.summary: Published - October 27, 2026 12:45 am IST - CHENNAI Doctors of Kauvery Hospital, Radial Road, treated a 32-year-old woman who suffered a cardiac arrest while recovering from a minor procedure at a hospital. Following resuscitation, she remained unconscious and had severely compromised cardiac function. Further evaluation, including a CT angiogram scan, revealed a critical brain haemorrhage caused by complex cerebral vascular abnormalities, which also explained the cardiac arrest and poor heart function. A neurosurgical team led by Krish Sridhar, group mentor, Neurosciences and director, Institute of Brain and Spine, performed emergency surgery under advanced cardiac output monitoring. It involved securing a ruptured brain aneurysm and a surgical mechanical thrombectomy to address an obstructed prominent venous channel. She was managed in the neuro intensive care unit and responded well to treatment, a press release said. f4c5e8046f9382c2.title: Centre committed to reducing fiscal deficit, says FM Nirmala Sitharaman
f4c5e8046f9382c2.summary: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Monday said the Centre is committed to reducing the fiscal deficit, as evidenced by the annual budgets, stressing that the national debt will be limited to 50 per cent of the GDP by 2030. Addressing concerns about the national debt, she said that since the post-COVID period, every nation has faced debt challenges. "We are committed to reducing the fiscal deficit, as evidenced by our annual budgets. We have openly stated our goal that by 2030, the national debt will be limited to 50 per cent of the GDP. We are consistently putting in place measures to reduce the Union Government's debt, and international organisations have acknowledged India's disciplined approach to debt management." Sitharaman told reporters here.

3a6d51ce465b6aa4.title: IoB Q2 results: Net profit rises 56% to ₹1,912 cr on higher interest income
3a6d51ce465b6aa4.summary: Indian Overseas Bank (IoB) on Monday reported a 56 per cent growth in net profit at Rs 1,912 crore for the second quarter ended September 30, buoyed by higher interest income. The public sector bank had reported a net profit of Rs 1,226 crore in the July-September quarter of last fiscal 2025-26. Interest income of the bank rose 17 per cent to Rs 9,201 crore during the September quarter of current fiscal, from Rs 7,849 crore in the corresponding quarter of last fiscal. 241467e56986f6fb.title: 32-year-old man arrested for sexually assaulting girl in Ennore
241467e56986f6fb.summary: Published - October 27, 2026 12:35 am IST - Chennai The All Women Police, Ennore, on Monday arrested a 32-year-old man for allegedly sexually assaulting a two-and-a-half-year-old girl from Ennore on two occasions earlier this month. According to the police, on October 23, the girl was taken to the Institute of Child Health and Hospital for Children in Egmore due to health issues. After examining her, the doctor suspected that she might have been sexually assaulted. The Inspector of the All-Women Police Station, Ennore initiated an investigation. A case was registered following a complaint lodged by the girl’s mother under Sections- 5 (Aggravated penetrative sexual assault), 6 (Punishment for aggravated penetrative sexual assault) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act. During the investigation, the police arrested D. Ranjithkumar, 32, a resident of the same locality, on Monday. The investigation revealed that the accused had allegedly taken the girl, who was playing outside, into his house and sexually assaulted her on October 15 and 17. The assaults had severely affected the child’s health, the police said. The accused was subsequently remanded in judicial custody. The girl is currently undergoing treatment in hospital. c71612b24263af58.title: Unusual sighting of greater flamingos at Veeranam lake
c71612b24263af58.summary: Published - October 27, 2026 05:30 am IST - CHENNAI A total of 18 greater flamingos were sighted at the freshwater lake | Photo Credit: J. Pandiyan and team Greater flamingos, usually found in coastal wetlands, have been spotted at Veeranam Lake in Cuddalore district, in a rare occurrence that researchers say could be linked to altered rainfall patterns. A total of 18 greater flamingos were sighted at the freshwater lake, located about 50 km inland from the coast, on October 25 by J. Pandiyan, associate professor and bird researcher at the Department of Zoology and Wildlife Biology, A.V.C. College, Mayiladuthurai, along with his research scholars Saravanakumar and Veerasamy. Prof. Pandiyan said the birds were usually found in coastal habitats such as Point Calimere Wildlife Sanctuary, Muthupettai Lagoon, and Pichavaram mangroves, where they feed in shallow waters. “Usually, greater flamingos migrate from the Gulf of Kutch to the east coast during winter. However, this year due to Super El Niño and severe water deficit, the migration pattern is altered. Cauvery flow has been subpar and rainfall is insufficient. Coastal mudflats are scarce in food resources,” he said. Low rainfall during the Southwest monsoon and reduced Cauvery flows have left coastal mudflats dry and reduced food availability, potentially prompting the birds to explore inland wetlands, he explained. Prof. Pandiyan said the receding water level at Veeranam Lake had created shallow areas suitable for foraging. Evaporation may also have concentrated plankton and other food resources, making the lake a temporary feeding ground for the birds. However, it remains uncertain whether the freshwater habitat can meet the birds’ needs during migration. “We have to monitor the birds continuously to understand how these coastal species use inland wetlands when coastal ecosystems are under stress,” he said. E100 fuel allows vehicles to run on nearly pure ethanol. A senior road transport ministry official said fuel beyond E20 (20 per cent ethanol-blended petrol) and up to E100 is intended only for vehicles designed and certified to use it and will not be applicable for other vehicles. Vehicles that use E20 or normal fuel can't use E85 or E100 fuel. The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) has changed certain vehicle classification thresholds, fuel specifications, and technical references used in emission-related tables and testing provisions. Additionally, the government has raised the vehicle weight limit to 3,500 kg from the previous threshold of 3,000 kg for light petrol and diesel vehicles affected by these changes. c5138b67a17ab757.title: Namo Ghat helipad security breach: UP man poses as fake Army officer during Varanasi air show, arrested
c5138b67a17ab757.summary: A man disguising himself as an Army officer was arrested by the police during the recently concluded Indian Air Force air show, 'Wings over Ganges', at Namo Ghat in Uttar Pradesh's Varanasi, according to a report by Bhaskar English. The man, identified as Arpit Chaturvedi, was roaming in the restricted area on October 24 while claiming to be an Army official. Police became vigilant after receiving information about a suspicious individual, prompting them to question him. After hours of questioning, it was discovered that he was posing as a fake Army officer. Police subsequently registered a First Information Report (FIR) against him under the relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Further investigation revealed that the accused, Arpit Chaturvedi, is a resident of Uttar Pradesh's Azamgarh district. According to a report by Assam Tribune, Sub-Inspector Chandan Kumar was posted at Namo Ghat during the air show and was carrying out his duties alongside Head Constable Hriday Narayan Maurya and Constable Mehboob Alam when they received a tip-off about a man behaving suspiciously near the helipad at Namo Ghat. When the police asked Chaturvedi to show his identity card and other official documents to verify that he was an Army official, he failed to do so, leading to his arrest. The police registered case No. 0189/2026 against him at Adampur Police Station. The case was registered under Sections 204 and 318(4) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. The three-day air show, which featured aerial manoeuvres by the IAF's premier display teams, concluded on October 25. The final day, Sunday, also witnessed the presence of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, Uttar Pradesh Governor Anandiben Patel and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, among others. According to news agency PTI, the show featured fighter aircraft, including the Sukhoi-30 MKI, the indigenous Tejas and LCH Prachand, along with helicopter displays. Three Kiran aircraft flew in

c489f4441c6496c9.title: CCPA imposes ₹1 lakh fine on Britannia over '100% whole wheat bread' claim
c489f4441c6496c9.summary: The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed a penalty of Rs 1 lakh on Britannia Industries Ltd for a misleading advertisement that claimed "100% whole wheat bread" even though the product's declared wheat content is just 62 per cent. In its order dated October 22, the CCPA, headed by Chief Commissioner Nidhi Khare, directed the company to discontinue the advertisement with immediate effect across all print and electronic media, including social media. Britannia has also been asked to submit a compliance report within 15 days. The regulator took suo motu cognisance of the matter after noticing that the packaging of the product declared a wheat content of 62 per cent, despite the "100%" claim in its advertisements. "In the present matter, the product admittedly contains only 62% whole wheat, while the remaining 38% comprises other ingredients, including rice bran and other constituents," the order said. It added that the claim, prefixed with "100%", was prima facie

In its order dated October 22, the CCPA, headed by Chief Commissioner Nidhi Khare, directed the company to discontinue the advertisement with immediate effect across all print and electronic media, including social media. Britannia has also been asked to submit a compliance report within 15 days. The regulator took suo motu cognisance of the matter after noticing that the packaging of the product declared a wheat content of 62 per cent, despite the "100%" claim in its advertisements. "In the present matter, the product admittedly contains only 62% whole wheat, while the remaining 38% comprises other ingredients, including rice bran and other constituents," the order said. It added that the claim, prefixed with "100%", was prima facie

e46b2e44a6364f15.title: A final surge: On Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s triumph in Brazil
e46b2e44a6364f15.summary: Updated - October 27, 2026 01:15 am IST At one point, it seemed almost impossible for Brazil’s 80-year-old President, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, to turn the tide after finishing second to Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round of elections on October 4. In Brazil’s history, no candidate who has finished second in the first round has gone on to win the presidential run-off. Most of the candidates who dropped out after the first round were from the right. Flávio’s Liberal Party cemented its position in both houses of Congress, while right-wing candidates won several provincial elections. But Lula, a former trade unionist and organiser, who lost a finger in an accident as a teenager, was not ready to give up. Lula and his Workers’ Party identified campaign weaknesses, shifted their attention to economic issues, promised growth and welfare, and persuaded more voters to turn out for Sunday’s run-off. Lula won 51.7% of the vote against Flávio’s 48.2%, a greater lead than his victory against Jair Bolsonaro, Flavio’s father, four years ago. Over the weeks, Lula turned the right-wing’s gains in the first round against it, highlighting the threats that a Bolsonaro victory could pose to democracy and civil rights. Flávio’s campaign pledge to free his father — he is serving a 27-year prison sentence for attempting to overturn Lula’s 2022 victory, and impeach Supreme Court judges — only heightened the concerns of voters outside the right wing, who rallied behind a familiar face. Lula unleashed a social media campaign to mobilise younger voters. A WhatsApp channel called ‘Lula’s Army’ with 11 million followers spread his message of continuity. He also announced plans to expand a cash payout scheme for the poor, a new debt relief package and entrepreneur-friendly measures. In the northeast, the Workers’ Party’s stronghold, he gained nearly three million votes and made considerable gains in the working-class neighbourhoods of big cities, including São Paulo.
