29d990236d4e2b58.summary: Updated - October 26, 2026 01:03 am IST Sixteen years after his visit as Poland’s Prime Minister, Donald Tusk’s travel to Delhi and Bengaluru last week was to signal a renewed desire to work closely with India. Mr. Tusk’s visit, two months ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s trip to Brussels to sign the India-European Union (EU) Free Trade Agreement , indicated one part of his agenda. Both sides agreed that it was time to develop trade, currently worth just $6 billion, to double its size by 2030. Mr. Tusk’s last visit to India was in 2017, as President of the European Council for the EU-India summit, and it is fitting that his trip was just as the FTA is finalised and ratified after years of delays. Another area of increased India-Poland collaboration is in technology, AI and defence hardware, critical minerals, renewable and nuclear energy given Poland’s expertise in the last few decades and India’s capacity for scale. As the EU’s sixth largest economy, Poland has officially crossed the $1 trillion GDP (nominal terms) milestone. Its $120-billion-dollar tech economy is also gaining global interest. A large part of Polish machinery and parts is exported to Germany, which in turn has a growing share of Indian imports, and India could consider more trilateral collaborations for manufacturing and mining technology. The two sides agreed to establish a “Defence Industry Dialogue” and explore a dialogue on counter-terrorism cooperation. Finally, the Modi-Tusk talks focused on geopolitics, particularly the ongoing war in Ukraine. 4e56639fd7539d80.summary: Updated - October 26, 2026 12:30 am IST - NEW DELHI The Delhi government is set to introduce Individual Aftercare Plans (IAPs) for teenagers exiting Child Care Institutions (CCIs) at 18, based on their specific circumstances, requirements and rehabilitation needs, under the proposed ‘Aftercare Scheme for Young Persons’, a senior government official said on Sunday. Under the scheme, the eligible beneficiaries will receive up to ₹2 lakh for higher education and ₹60,000 for vocational training. The scheme is likely to be approved by the Delhi Cabinet soon, according to a senior government official. In May, the Women and Child Development Department proposed a budget of ₹3.50 crore for the implementation of the scheme for the current financial year. The government also plans to allocate ₹5 crore from the Chief Minister’s Development Fund to strengthen the juvenile justice system, including the aftercare scheme, the official said. The government is also seeking Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) partnerships to provide mentorship, additional financial resources, and other forms of support. 80d949e9a1642cc2.title: Jantar Mantar to ‘Dilli Chalo’, protest challenges power
80d949e9a1642cc2.summary: Updated - October 26, 2026 01:33 am IST ‘The demonstrations that have gathered momentum since early October mark a significant shift in Opposition politics’ | Photo Credit: AFP Over the past few months, three distinct streams of dissent have emerged in India: the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) -led agitation, actions by left-wing student organisations, and campaigns spearheaded by the Congress and the INDIA bloc. Although these streams have largely evolved independently, their paths have increasingly converged around shared concerns about democracy, dissent, citizens’ rights and the fairness of the political and electoral process. Their significance lies in their capacity to bring disparate grievances and constituencies together in a broader challenge to the government. The first phase of the agitation unfolded at Jantar Mantar in June and July, focusing on education reform, the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET) paper leaks and demands for the (then) Education Minister’s resignation. The CJP played a pivotal role in galvanising public discontent, drawing large numbers of young people into the streets, where they articulated their grievances through a distinctive blend of humour, creativity and youthful energy. This indicated that dissatisfaction with the ruling establishment extended well beyond the established Opposition parties, with the political disaffection of this constituency having been seriously underestimated. The Minister’s eventual resignation gave the movement fresh impetus, demonstrating that sustained public pressure could secure political concessions. 0d9cfd4faa4dca37.title: Free medical camp held for construction workers in Vellore
0d9cfd4faa4dca37.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 11:04 pm IST - VELLORE A medical camp being held for construction workers to commemorate the birthday of G.V. Selvam, vice-president, VIT. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Thalaimurai Peravai, Vellore, in association with Sri Narayani Hospital and Research Centre organised a medical camp for construction workers on Sunday to commemorate the birthday of G.V. Selvam, vice-president, Vellore Institute of Technology (VIT), in recognition of his commitment to social welfare, community development, and public service. According to a press release, G. Ramakrishnan, Politburo Member, Communist Party of India (Marxist), inaugurated the camp in the presence of Mr. Selvam, Katpadi MLA M. Sudhakar, and N. Balaji, director, Sri Narayani Group. In his address, Mr. Selvam highlighted the contribution of construction workers to the infrastructural development of the country. “The medical camp has been organised to emphasise the importance of ensuring the physical and mental well-being of construction workers, who play a vital role in nation-building,” he said. More than 600 workers participated in the day-long camp that provided general medical check-ups, cardiac evaluations, dental check-ups, and orthopaedic assessments, along with Siddha and Ayurveda treatments, the release said. Credit: X/@INCIndia The BJP on Sunday (October 25, 2002) hit out at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge for his remarks against Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The party said it would hold nationwide protests on Monday (October 26, 2026) against the “inappropriate and offensive remarks”. Criticising the “ Modi ka baap bhi jayega [even Modi’s father will go]” comment, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said Mr. Kharge has “torn apart all norms of decorum”. “This is not the first time that the Congress party has used abusive language against Modi ji or his family,” he said, accusing the party of having hurled insults at the Prime Minister’s mother, calling him a “merchant of death”, and mocking his poverty by addressing him as a “chaiwala” in the past. “Under Rahul Gandhi’s leadership, the Congress party keeps crossing the limits of indecency every day,” he said, alleging that repeated electoral defeats over the past 12 years had bred “desperation and frustration” within the party. कांग्रेस अध्यक्ष मल्लिकार्जुन खरगे ने आज पटना में मोदी जी के पिताजी के बारे में अभद्र टिप्पणी कर सारी मर्यादाएँ तार-तार कर दी हैं। यह पहली बार नहीं है, जब कांग्रेस पार्टी ने मोदी जी या उनके परिवार को अपशब्द कहे हों। कभी उनकी पूजनीय माताजी के विषय में अपशब्द कहे, कभी उन्हें 'मौत का सौदागर' कहा, तो कभी 'चायवाला' कहकर उनकी गरीबी का उपहास उड़ाया। राहुल गांधी के नेतृत्व में कांग्रेस पार्टी हर रोज अभद्रता की सीमाएँ पार करती जा रही है। बीते 12 वर्षों में लगातार मिल रही चुनावी हार से कांग्रेस पार्टी में हताशा व निराशा इतनी बढ़ चुकी है कि अब उसके पास न कोई नीति बची है, न कोई मुद्दा, बस गाली-गलौज की राजनीति बची है। जनता के बीच जनाधार खो चुकी कांग्रेस, अब अपने कार्यकर्ताओं में भी आधार खोती जा रही है। जब-जब इन्होंने मो

96977ad862638fe7.title: GVMC elections will be a battle between 'Sale Vizag' and 'Save Vizag': YSRCP leaders

889e3b8e738f2bb3.title: ISKCON unveils 800-kg robotic elephant in Visakhapatnam
889e3b8e738f2bb3.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 11:56 pm IST - VISAKHAPATNAM Devotees gather around Ranga, a fully mechanised elephant, during its ceremonial unveiling as part of ISKCON Visakhapatnam’s Sharad Purnima celebrations at MGM Park on Beach Road on Sunday. | Photo Credit: V. RAJU A moving robotic elephant named Ranga, weighing 800 kg, was unveiled on Sunday at MGM Park on Beach Road in front of a large gathering of devotees during ISKCON Visakhapatnam’s Sharad Purnima celebrations. The organisers described it as the first-of-its-kind in Andhra Pradesh. ISKCON Governing Body chairman Madhusevita Prabhu inaugurated the elephant. Branch president Samba Das Prabhu and Nitai Sevini Mataji led the programme. According to ISKCON, the elephant was brought from Thrissur in Kerala and donated by PETA India. A ‘Nauka Vihar’ (boat festival), Bhajan Clubbing and the ‘Kartika Deepotsavam’ followed ‘sankirtan’ of the Hare Krishna Maha Mantra. CMR Group managing director Mavuri Venkata Ramana, Andhra University former Vice-Chancellor G.S.N. Raju, Simhachalam Devasthanam chief priest G. Srinivasacharyulu, and Pydah Educational Institutions chairman Pydah Krishna Prasad were also present on the ocassion. b7cb5b650b3eebd0.title: 15 candidates in fray for Visakhapatnam Mayor’s post
b7cb5b650b3eebd0.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 11:26 pm IST - VISAKHAPATNAM A total of 15 candidates are contesting for the post of Mayor in the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) general elections–2026, Mayor Election Returning Officer B. Dayanidhi said in a release on Sunday. A total of 29 nominations were received for the GVMC Mayor’s post, of which 8 nominations were rejected, while the remaining 21 nominations were found valid. During the withdrawal of nominations on October 21, six candidates withdrew their nominations, he said. Subsequently, in the notification issued by the Andhra Pradesh State Election Commission on October 22, 2026, it was directed that the final list of candidates contesting for the post of Mayor in the GVMC elections be announced on October 25, 2026. Accordingly, 15 candidates remain in the fray for the Mayor’s post, the Returning Officer stated. Prominent candidates among them include Mukka Sravani from Telugu Desam Party (TDP), Varudu Kalyani from YSRCP (YSRCP), Devara Naga Sunanda Devi from Indian National Congress (INC), K. Keerthana Grace from Bahujan Samaj Party, and Nammi Bhavani from Bharata Chaitanya Yuvajana Party. 175bbc032de8866f.title: Child rights panel seeks report on schoolgirl’s death within two weeks
175bbc032de8866f.summary: Published - October 26, 2026 01:01 am IST - New Delhi Police personnel outside the government school where a 17-year-old student was found with severe burns. | Photo Credit: ANI The Delhi Commission for Protection of Child Rights (DCPCR) on Sunday sought an inquiry report within two weeks from the Directorate of Education over the death of a 17-year-old Class 12 student who was found with severe burns at a government school in east Delhi’s Krishna Nagar on Saturday. The girl was found behind the school’s guard room after school authorities heard cries from the area. She was taken to Dr. Hedgewar Arogya Sansthan, where she was declared dead on arrival. According to police, a water bottle used to carry petrol was recovered from the spot. Taking cognisance of media reports, the commission raised concerns about student safety, questioning how the girl managed to bring an inflammable substance into the school without being noticed. “The content of the news report, if true, are disturbing and raise serious concern on the safety of children inside the school premises. The incident as a whole has resulted in violation of child rights on account of negligence of public servants,” the commission stated in its notice. The commission issued notices to the Directorate of Education, the school principal and the police, seeking action-taken reports within two weeks. Police have seized the school’s CCTV digital video recorder and are examining the footage to reconstruct the sequence of events. ff1a379985d43bb0.title: U.S. immigration restrictions may outlast Trump
ff1a379985d43bb0.summary: Updated - October 26, 2026 01:12 am IST ‘As the bipartisan focus on immigration reform continues, the issue is likely to sustain as a friction point in India-U.S. relations.’ | Photo Credit: AP In its second term, the Donald Trump administration has been active in restricting legal immigration to the United States. The administration’s attempt to impose a $100,000 payment requirement on certain new H-1B petitions, changes to visa renewal procedures, the introduction of a wage-weighted selection system, and the latest suspensions of the Program Electronic Review Management (PERM) process are cases in point, disproportionately impacting Indian immigrants and firms. It is tempting to read these developments as a product of the Trump administration alone, but they reflect deeper political interests that are likely to survive post-Trump. Indian nationals account for 70% of H-1B visa approvals, with one-fifth of the visas going to employees of Indian-origin companies. This means that, as the bipartisan focus on immigration reform continues, the issue is likely to sustain as a friction point in India-U.S. relations. 60625e20732b6626.title: Two feared trapped after building collapse in Delhi's Harsh Vihar
60625e20732b6626.summary: Updated - October 26, 2026 12:51 am IST - New Delhi NDRF personnel at the site after a slab of a house under construction collapsed in Milan Garden in Harsh Vihar area on Sunday. | Photo Credit: - Two men, aged 60 and 36, are suspected to be trapped after roof slabs collapsed during construction in north-east Delhi’s Harsh Vihar on Sunday evening, police said. The collapse occurred in Milan Garden as an additional floor was being built on an old, single-storey house on a 200-square-yard plot, said an officer. A resident said a newly laid slab gave way over an older slab. The Delhi Fire Services received a call at 6.46 p.m. and sent five fire tenders. Teams from the National Disaster Response Force, police, Civil Defence and Delhi Disaster Management Authority joined the rescue efforts. “Two people are suspected to be trapped, but there is no confirmation yet,” Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police Sandeep Lamba said. No casualties had been reported till the time the report went to the press. “Their family members suspect that they are trapped as their mobile phones are not reachable,” the officer said. Some relatives alleged that rescue work was slow and tried to remove the debris themselves. Later in the evening, Ministers Ashish Sood and Kapil Mishra also visited the building collapse site. Police said, the cause of the collapse and the status of construction approvals are yet to be established. 6f7f0097fe010712.title: Wicked surprise: On the northeast monsoon
6f7f0097fe010712.summary: Updated - October 26, 2026 12:48 am IST As India recovers from a monsoon-deficit year , there is both hope and trepidation regarding the prospects for that ‘other monsoon’, or the ‘northeast monsoon’ . While contributing only around a quarter of India’s annual rainfall, it is largely focused on the south-east peninsula regions of Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, coastal Andhra Pradesh, Rayalaseema, south interior Karnataka and Keralam. The southwest monsoon, influenced by a strengthening El Niño , has already left its desiccating mark. Rainfall from June-September was 759.4 mm against 868.6 mm, a 12.6% deficit, the driest in 11 years. This has impacted kharif sowing and is reflected in food inflation. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said that this year, the northeast monsoon rainfall, spanning October to December, would likely be ‘normal’ , meaning in line with a 50-year average and within a 12% error window. Most parts of the country, it said, are expected to receive below-normal rainfall, except some areas of northwest India and southern parts of peninsular India, where rainfall is likely to be normal to above-normal. The wide error window, however, is far less precise than its forecasts for the southwest monsoon with its margin of 5%, and can sometimes make the northeast monsoon the bearer of nasty surprises. For instance, December 1, 2015, saw the city of Chennai deluged by its heaviest rainfall in 24-hours in over a century ; at least 500 lives were lost and 18 lakh people displaced in the State. That year and the present are linked by a common thread: a powerful El Niño. a8dfb0f1c174b461.title: Three North Andhra districts step up cyclone preparedness
a8dfb0f1c174b461.summary: Updated - October 25, 2026 11:42 pm IST - VISAKHAPATNAM Fishermen use an earthmover to haul a boat ashore at Pedda Jalaripeta in Visakhapatnam on Sunday, as a cyclonic storm is forecast over the Bay of Bengal. | Photo Credit: V RAJU The administrations of Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli and Alluri Sitharama Raju (ASR) districts have stepped up preparedness on Sunday by setting up control rooms and readying relief centres, as a deep depression over the Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into a cyclone, according to the India Meteorological Department. Visakhapatnam Collector M. Abhishikth Kishore, reviewing arrangements at a videoconference with Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) Commissioner Ketan Garg said the impact could be as severe as that of Cyclone Montha . He directed officers to remain at their places of work. A control room has been set up at the Collectorate, with others planned to be opened at the GVMC office and at zonal and mandal levels. Officials were instructed to monitor reservoir levels, alert residents living on hill slopes and keep relief centres ready. Mr. Garg said that people had earlier been evacuated from seven areas. The Collector directed officials to arrange for the shifting of those residents again. Tree-cutting machines are to be stationed in advance, while the GVMC and APEPDCL were asked to ensure uninterrupted power supply. Fishing boats on the beach at Pedda Jalaripeta in Visakhapatnam on Sunday, ahead of the forecast cyclonic storm. | Photo Credit: V RAJU Ambulances, medical teams and medicines are to be kept ready. Pregnant women nearing delivery are to be moved to hospitals. Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea and, tourists and residents were warned against visiting beaches. Special officers have been appointed for each constituency and mandal. The round-the-clock Collectorate control room can be reached on 0891-2590100 and 0891-2590102, said Special Deputy Collector and District Project Manager

8c1ac680ad45562b.title: Harmanpreet, Deepti on fire as India seals emphatic series win against Zimbabwe
8c1ac680ad45562b.summary: Updated - October 26, 2026 12:21 am IST - VADODARA Harmanpreet and Deepti put the Zimbabwe attack to the sword. | Photo Credit: BCCI Picture this. Harmanpreet Kaur and Deepti Sharma scored centuries to power India to a big win. Now ask yourself: which of the two blazed her way to triple figures? If your gut said Harmanpreet, it failed you. On a sweltering Sunday at the BCA Stadium in Kotambi, the second ODI against Zimbabwe turned the script on its head. A restrained Harmanpreet played the artisan while Deepti played destroyer, with their record-breaking 153-run fifth-wicket stand laying the foundation of India’s 121-run win and unassailable 2-0 lead. India was stuttering at 19 for two in the third over — Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma both undone by Nomvelo Sibanda’s short-ball ploy — when Harmanpreet joined Pratika Rawal. Pratika, fresh from a hundred in the first ODI, and Harmanpreet added 124 off 118 balls. The former looked set for another ton when Nyasha Gwanzura deceived her with a change of pace. Tejal Hasabnis followed soon after. But Harmanpreet remained unfazed, aided by a fearless Deepti who arrived as if stepping in for a net session. As many as 32 of the pair’s first 47 runs came through Deepti’s audacious shots on the leg-side while Harmanpreet whipped out a catalogue of puritanical drives and cuts on the off-side. When the century came, celebrations oddly didn’t. Neither did tears, like the 91 she scored in the third T20I had drawn out of her. Deepti, too, eventually braved a slowdown to reach her second ODI century in the final over — nine years after her first — helping India set an intimidating 329-run target. Modester Mupachikwa’s sprightly start, despite losing Loryn Phiri early, gave Zimbabwe hope. With support from Chipo Mugeri-Tiripano, the Lady Chevrons got to 100 in just 19 overs, helped by India’s worrying inability to take wickets, especially the seamers. Sayali Satghare finally succeeded in breaching Mugeri-Tiripano’s defence. Left-ar

96cfa179ef2c8f3f.title: APSCHE to hold State-level AISHE workshop for university nodal officers in Vijayawada on October 26
96cfa179ef2c8f3f.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 11:36 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA The Andhra Pradesh State Council of Higher Education (APSCHE) will organise a State-level workshop on the All India Survey on Higher Education (AISHE) for university nodal officers from Andhra Pradesh on Monday (October 26, 2026), in collaboration with the Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education, Government of India. A statement issued on Sunday (October 25) said the workshop will be held at Hotel Fortune Murali Park in Vijayawada. Principal Secretary, Higher Education Department (FAC), Andhra Pradesh J. Syamala Rao, will be the chief guest, while AISHE resource persons from New Delhi N.M. Biswas, Assistant Director; Shubhda Sharma, Senior Statistical Officer and Shivam Pandey, Programmer, will conduct expert sessions. The workshop aims to facilitate interaction between university nodal officers and AISHE experts, address issues related to the survey and improve coordination in implementing AISHE-related activities across higher education institutions in the State. 7868fb24235ac08c.title: How Tamil Nadu CM Vijay got rare praise from Modi govt: Big step he took on aviation fuel
7868fb24235ac08c.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay has earned rare praise from the Centre after his TVK government slashed the Value Added Tax (VAT) on aviation turbine fuel (ATF). The move comes as a massive relief to the aviation sector, which is currently battling surging global crude prices. The decision drew swift applause from Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu, highlighting a moment of collaborative governance between the state and the Modi government. Taking to X, the Union Minister lauded the TVK government's intervention. “Appreciate the Tamil Nadu government's decision to reduce VAT on Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF), a welcome step for the aviation sector. Thank you, Chief Minister Vijay, for this initiative,” the Union Minister tweeted. Naidu underlined that coordination between the Centre and states is critical to keeping the aviation sector viable. “Making air travel more affordable requires the Centre and States to work together. Our shared priority must always be the passengers,” he said. Because ATF falls outside the GST regime, state governments are free to levy their own VAT rates. Through three gazette notifications issued on Friday, the Vijay government implemented steep tax cuts that will remain in force for one year, until 31 October 2027. Tamil Nadu’s interventions include: Tamil Nadu Industries Minister Virudhai Magal Keerthana termed the decision a “decisive step” toward making air travel accessible and keeping regional airports competitive. “Lower operating costs can encourage airlines to introduce new routes, increase flight frequencies and expand operations beyond Chennai. We are building an aviation ecosystem that connects more regions, unlocks economic potential and powers Tamil Nadu's next phase of growth,” Keerthana tweeted. The relief arrives at a critical juncture for Indian carriers. Fuel traditionally accounts for about 30-40% of an airline's operating costs, but this has recently risen to about 55-60%. 45c3a1ff3a7ccf7d.title: A Korean cultural evening in Hyderabad, with a distinctly Telangana touch
45c3a1ff3a7ccf7d.summary: Updated - October 26, 2026 12:32 am IST - HYDERABAD Atti classic vocal crossover performance at the 'K Harmony Festa' at Shilpakala Vedika in Hyderabad on Sunday. | Photo Credit: SIDDHANT THAKUR What happens when the rhythms of Korean culture meet the beats of Telangana’s traditional drums? At Shilpakala Vedika here on Sunday, the answer unfolded through a lively mix of music, dance, martial arts and cultural exchange, as Korea Culture Day 2026 brought the traditions of two countries together on one stage. From afternoon, stalls selling Korean products drew curious visitors, with crowds gathering around them to explore a slice of Korean culture. As the evening approached, the buzz moved towards the auditorium, where hundreds of people began assembling from 5 p.m., eager to witness the performances lined up for the occasion. Inside, the anticipation gave way to a celebration that travelled between two cultures, from the precision and power of Korean martial arts to the vigorous movements of Telangana’s traditional dances. The programme began around 5.30 p.m. with an address by Lee Seong-ho, Ambassador of the Republic of Korea to India, who welcomed the audience to Hyderabad and spoke of the cultural ties that the event hoped to strengthen. Drawing a connection between Diwali, India’s festival of lights, and Chuseok, Korea’s harvest festival, Mr. Lee spoke about the shared values underlying celebrations in both countries: family, togetherness, gratitude and hope for the future. Though the traditions may differ, he said, the emotions they evoke are remarkably similar. Cultural exchanges, he added, help people discover just how much they have in common. 08a71a25e47f3b55.title: Universities urged to embrace continuous learning and innovation in AI era
08a71a25e47f3b55.summary: Published - October 26, 2026 12:02 am IST - VIJAYAWADA Universities must move beyond incremental changes and embrace continuous learning, experimentation and innovation to keep pace with the exponential growth of artificial intelligence (AI), said Soumitra Dutta, advisor to the SRM Group. Delivering the keynote address at a symposium on ‘Advancing Management Knowledge in the AI Era: Research Frontiers and Future’ organised by the Paari School of Business (PSB) at SRM University-A.P., he highlighted the close links between engineering advancements and modern digital ecosystems. He also stressed the need for developing countries such as India to strengthen their technological capabilities and research networks to participate effectively in global innovation, particularly as computing infrastructure remains concentrated in a few wealthy economies. The symposium, themed ‘Reimagining Management through AI’, brought together academics and researchers to examine the impact of artificial intelligence on management practices, economic models, organisational transformation and global business. During a chat on human capital, leadership and organisational transformation, Allan Bird of the Goa Institute of Management and Michael Stevens of Weber State University explored the implications of AI for organisational strategy and decision-making. They discussed globalisation in terms of ease of communication, systemic interdependence and operational complexity. The speakers emphasised the importance of cognitive engagement and independent thinking, cautioning against excessive dependence on automated tools. Ashay Kadam, dean of PSB, said the business school was integrating AI into its curriculum and departmental workflows while conducting faculty development programmes to improve the use of AI in teaching and research. These initiatives were aimed at preparing students for changing industry requirements and advancing the institution’s ambition to become AI-native. Ranjit Thapa, Dean

bd3712139e3eba79.title: A hundred years ago | The Indian civil service
bd3712139e3eba79.summary: Published - October 26, 2026 02:30 am IST Simla, October 25: The following Press Communique is issued: In accordance with the recommendation of the Lee Commission, direct recruits to the Indian Civil Service are now being selected in equal numbers from Europeans and Indians. For the purpose of calculation, London examination of one year and Allahabad examination and nominations of the next year are taken together as forming one year. In the year 1925-26, i.e. London examination of 1926 and Allahabad examination and nominations of 1925, numbers actually recruited were 20 Europeans and 22 Indians. These figures are being adjusted in the year 1926-27 by recruiting 29 Europeans and 27 Indians. The London examination of 1926 has yielded 19 Europeans and 11 Indians. This leaves 16 Indians to be recruited in India in 1927 through examination and nomination. Nine of these vacancies are definitely offered for open competition of the Allahabad examination to be held in January next, while the remaining seven are for the present held in reserve to be filled by nomination. 28a22a0c151a66f9.title: Polio awareness campaign held at five Metro Rail stations in Chennai

9f8c115d4f239e60.title: Officials urged to remain alert as severe cyclone approaches
9f8c115d4f239e60.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 11:46 pm IST - MACHILIPATNAM NTR District Collector G. Lakshmisha reviewing cyclone preparedness in Vijayawada. | Photo Credit: G.N. RAO Krishna District Collector D.K. Balaji has directed officials to remain alert for the cyclone and take steps to prevent human and property loss. Mr. Balaji, who reviewed cyclone preparedness with the district and mandal-level officials, instructed them to be available at the posted places and take measures for supply of drinking water and other essentials. Meanwhile, Andhra Pradesh Central Power Distribution Corporation Limited (APCPDCL) CMD P. Pulla Reddy said leaves of officials and staff were cancelled in wake of the cyclonic storm. He also asked the field staff to caution the public against touching snapped electric cables. Control Rooms have been set up in all districts under CPDCL, Mr. Pulla Reddy said. Eluru District Collector K. Vetri Selvi has directed the officials to be alert and asked the Irrigation department engineers to take measures to prevent damage to canal and tank bunds. Villagers were requested not to venture into rivers and canals and move on the bunds as the impact of the cyclone would be heavy. Control Rooms have been set up at Eluru Collectorate with helpline numbers 18002331077, 08812-224519 and 9491041419, and public are requested to contact and alert the officers in emergency, the Collector said. NTR District Collector G. Lakshmisha reviewed the preparedness for the severe cyclone with the officials of Revenue, Irrigation, A.P. Transco, Medical and Health, Fire and other departments. He directed the Tahsildars to shift people staying in vulnerable areas to safer locations. A control room has been set up the Collectorate with the helpline number 91549 70454 in Vijayawada, Mr. Lakshmisha said. He appealed to the public not to take shelter in dilapidated buildings, under the trees, electric poles and hoardings during the event of the cyclone. Published - October 25, 2026 11:46 p

51fcfc8ac02b49b9.title: Uttar Pradesh CEO orders reverification of all forms submitted through computer operators
51fcfc8ac02b49b9.summary: Published - October 26, 2026 12:25 am IST - New Delhi: Uttar Pradesh CEO Navdeep Rinwa directed that errors identified during the investigation of complaints received regarding the electoral rolls through various political parties and social media platforms should not be repeated. (Representational image) | Photo Credit: Getty Images/iStockphoto Amid controversy over errors found in the electoral rolls published after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) of Uttar Pradesh on Sunday (October 25, 2026) ordered reverification of all entries made by computer operators since the publication of post-SIR final electoral rolls on April 10 and directed that any future digital applications be filed only by Booth Level Officers (BLOs) and not by outsourced computer operators. “Under no circumstances should the feeding of physical application forms be handled by computer assistants. It must also be ensured that all physical forms received are digitised exclusively by the BLO through the BLO App. Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) must review all pending Form-6, Form-7, and Form-8 applications on a daily basis and ensure their prompt disposal strictly as per rules. Proper custody and preservation of all physically received forms must be ensured”, an official statement said. 3f13679c1ef2880d.title: Tamil Nadu Governor Arlekar calls for efforts to cultivate reading habit among children
3f13679c1ef2880d.summary: Updated - October 25, 2026 11:42 pm IST - Coimbatore Tamil Nadu Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar (centre) launching a book at the fifth edition of the Western Ghats Lit Fest in Coimbatore city on Sunday. | Photo Credit: SIVA SARAVANAN S. Tamil Nadu Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar on Sunday (October 25, 2026) called for efforts to cultivate reading habit among children, stressing that publishing books alone was not enough without creating a readership. “Books have to be there, books are to be published in abundant number, but at the same time we have to create readership,” he said at the fifth edition of the Western Ghats Lit Fest 2026, organised by The Verandah Club in Coimbatore city. Recounting his interactions with school students in Himachal Pradesh, Mr. Arlekar said some cited Physics and Geography textbooks when asked whether they read books. He also recalled that teachers at a school in Shimla were unaware of a book exhibition in the city, highlighting the need to encourage reading beyond the curriculum. He urged literary festivals to produce tangible outcomes rather than remain platforms for intellectual discussions. Referring to the cultural, linguistic, literary and ecological links between different parts of the country, Mr. Arlekar said these connections formed the basis of a united Bharat, and stressed on the need to preserve and rejuvenate these bonds. Citing the idea of ‘Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat’, he said people should develop a sense of belonging to the region in which they lived, irrespective of where they originally came from. He said literature and cultural exchanges could help strengthen this sense of national unity. He cited the Kashi Tamil Sangamam and historical links between Maharashtra and Thanjavur as examples of the country’s inter-connected heritage. 140c8de5aa4318c7.title: Vellore Corporation desilts waterbodies in 49 areas prone to waterlogging
140c8de5aa4318c7.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 11:12 pm IST - VELLORE Vellore Corporation Commissioner A. Catherine Saranya inspects desilting of water channels and storm-water drains in the town. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement With the onset of the Northeast monsoon, Vellore Corporation has identified 49 areas, mostly in Old Town, which are prone to waterlogging. Water channels have been desilted in these areas to prevent water stagnation during the monsoon. Corporation officials said that areas such as Kansalpet, Kaspa, Shenbakkam, Ambedkar Nagar, Thedir Nagar, and Konavattam are identified as flood-prone areas in Old Town. “Most of the identified spots in Old Town are low-lying areas. Desilting of storm-water drains and key water channels have been done to ensure free flow of excess rainwater into the river,” A. Catherine Saranya, Commissioner, Vellore Corporation, told The Hindu. Corporation officials said that as part of monsoon-preparedness measures, special teams led by a sanitary inspector have been deployed in identified areas prone to waterlogging in town. Surveillance teams will also patrol waterbodies to prevent dumping of waste that could choke the flow of rainwater in these water channels. Key water channels such as Nicholson, Thorapadi, and Pandian canals have been desilted to a distance of 64 km in the town. Among these water channels, Nicholson canal is the oldest waterbody and runs upto nine km. Built by the British in the 1890s, the canal discharges excess rainwater from nearby hillocks such as Pinchamandai, Kurumalai, Nechimedu, Pallakollai, and Vellakalmalai to the Palar River. Along with Corporation Commissioner Ms. Saranya, Collector P.S. Leena Alex inspected rain-related works in town. Ms. Alex also directed civic officials to take up road repair works and remove garbage, especially in congested spots such as markets and bus termini. 09328191bd1a24cb.title: Man jumps from terrace in bid to escape from police, dies
09328191bd1a24cb.summary: Published - October 26, 2026 12:02 am IST - Chennai A 42-year-old man working in the Commercial Taxes Office in Chengalpattu, who sustained injuries while trying to escape the police and was admitted to the Rajiv Gandhi Government Hospital, died on Sunday. The city police said R. Rajapandian, a resident of Kathirvedu, was working as an Office Assistant at the Commercial Taxes Department in Chengalpattu district. In July this year, a woman filed a sexual harassment complaint against Rajapandian, based on which a case was registered against him. The accused failed to appear before the court despite a warrant being issued against him, due to which the Puzhal police initiated proceedings against him. When a team of police officials from the Puzhal station visited his house on Friday, he tried to escape by jumping from the terrace on the third floor of the building. He sustained serious injuries and was admitted to the Rajiv Gandhi Government Hospital for treatment. However, he died on Sunday. 42bfa8999ca8c338.summary: Updated - October 25, 2026 11:53 pm IST - Chennai Officials of the Narcotics Intelligence Bureau (NIB) arrested three persons for selling high-end narcotics in Saligramam on Saturday. A senior official of the city police said they received a tip-off about a group of youth involved in consuming and selling methamphetamine. Acting on this, a police team apprehended three youth who were seen moving around suspiciously in Dhanalakshmi Colony. The police recovered 7 g of methamphetamine from them. In another incident, the Vanagaram police arrested an online delivery worker, Manjay Patel from Thiruverkadu, for selling prohibited tobacco products at his home. Three kg of tobacco, along with a grinder and a mobile phone, were seized from the accused. e6a0b3edb920cbae.title: Denso Iris reigns supreme
e6a0b3edb920cbae.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 11:35 pm IST - BENGALURU The best part about Denso Iris (Japan) is that it does not rely solely on its foreign imports, unlike most teams in the FIBA Women’s Basketball League Asia at the Sree Kanteerava Indoor Stadium here. Instead, it thrives on collective effort, with every player contributing and the foreigners complementing the team’s overall game. On Sunday, in the final against favourite Sichuan Yuanda Meile (China), Iris underlined the strength of that approach. Iris’s commanding 81-63 victory over the Chinese side was a powerful vindication of its philosophy. Sichuan, heavily dependent on American Chennedy Carter and Australian Sara Blicavs, struggled to find its attacking rhythm. Carter was disqualified early in the second quarter after picking up two technical fouls, while Blicavs was not at her best. With Iris’s defence denying it the space to operate freely, Sichuan found it increasingly difficult to raise the tempo. Iris’ disciplined approach and sustained intensity were reflected in the way it built its advantage quarter after quarter, moving from 24-20 after the first quarter to 43-36 at half-time before sealing an 81-63 victory. Maki Takada, a three-time Olympian at 37 years was a striking example of experience triumphing over age. Neither exceptionally quick nor overly aggressive, the veteran centre relied on composure, sound positioning to finish as the game’s top scorer with 23 points, including seven two-pointers and a three-pointer. G. Parameshwar, Deputy Chief Minister of Karnataka, gave away the prizes. The results: Final: Denso Iris (Japan) 81 (Maki Takada 23, Haruna Kasagi 15, Mai Kawai 13) bt Sichuan Yuanda Meile (China) 63 (Sara Blicavs 18, Gao Song 12, Chennedy Carter 11). Third place: Cathay Life Tigers (Chinese Taipei) 73 (Shelbynal Cheyanne Cheslek 24, Penina Davidson 20) bt KB Stars (South Korea) 68 (Yunjeong Na 22, Yeeun Heo 18, Yunha Song 15). 83561d0577b6a453.title: Food Safety Department destroys 922 kg of food items in raids: CMO
83561d0577b6a453.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 11:46 pm IST During a special drive at Mori Gate Khoya Mandi, the department destroyed around 370 kg of k hoya. | Photo Credit: KAMAL NARANG The Food Safety Department destroyed about 922 kg of food items during surprise inspections ahead of the festival season, the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO) stated on Sunday. Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said no compromise on public health or the purity of food products would be tolerated. “During festivals, when demand for sweets and other food items rises, greater vigilance and responsibility are essential to ensure food safety,” she said. Ms. Gupta said sweets are an integral part of traditions, faith and mutual affection, making their purity a matter of public health as well as a legal obligation. During a special drive at Mori Gate Khoya Mandi, the department destroyed around 370 kg of k hoya and 150 kg of c hhena found to be “spoiled and emitting a foul smell”, according to the CMO. Three samples of k hoya were also collected for laboratory testing. In west Delhi’s Nihal Vihar, officials inspected unlicensed units manufacturing sweets and destroyed around 402 kg of food items, including 265 kg of r asgullas, 45 kg of c hhena, 80 kg of milk cake and 12 kg of grated coconut. “The teams also collected 14 samples for testing, including six of c hhena, two each of milk cake and r asgullas, and one each of m otichoor laddoos, a tta laddoos, r asbhari and paneer,” an official statement said. The department said the inspections were conducted on a holiday, with teams deployed simultaneously in different lanes to prevent establishments from being alerted in advance. 51f9f424086d64f5.title: Two persons arrested in Ranipet for stealing two-wheelers
51f9f424086d64f5.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 11:08 pm IST - RANIPET Two persons were arrested by Thimiri police on Sunday for stealing two-wheelers in Vellore, Ranipet, and Tiruvannamalai districts. The arrested persons were identified as M. Dhanasekaran, 48, and R. Arumugam, 42. They are residents of Ranipet. The police recovered 12 two-wheelers from them. Initial inquiry revealed that the duo stole parked two-wheelers at temple festivals, hospitals, banks, markets, and government offices. Based on complaints from affected persons, Ranipet Superintendent of Police P. Sibin formed special teams to nab the duo. The police intercepted the duo during a surprise vehicle check. Stolen two-wheelers were kept in a godown before they were sold at cheap rates without documents. Each stolen two-wheeler was sold at a price of ₹5,000 to ₹10,000. A case was registered and later they were lodged at Central Prison in Vellore. A probe is under way. eb9e437d19555c49.title: India's heatwave tag flags global adaptation finance gap ahead of COP31
eb9e437d19555c49.summary: As India officially recognised heatwaves as natural disasters nearly three months ahead of the UN climate change conference (COP31) in Turkiye, officials and experts have pointed out that the move exposes a stark reality of a global climate finance system that pushes vulnerable nations to pay for immediate climate survival entirely on their own. "This task would have been much simpler if we had a good amount of international assistance that allowed us to access funds for various heat adaptation measures," Krishna S Vatsa, National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) member and Head of the Department, told PTI Videos in an interview. Stressing that the resources available for adaptation are "inadequate and unpredictable", Vatsa emphasised the need to improve access to the right kinds of technologies, including those required for efficient cooling. 15136289bbe20b8c.title: Fifty years ago | Chinese herb medicine cures cancer
15136289bbe20b8c.summary: Published - October 26, 2026 02:05 am IST Tokyo, October 25: A Chinese herb medicine preparation claimed to be remarkably effective against cancer has been developed by scientists at Osaka University and Kink University’s Oriental Medicine Research Institute. The preparation, composed of about 30 kinds of herbal medicines, produces comparatively little of the adverse effects generally noted in cancer-arresting drugs. Patients suffering from breast, abdominal, rectal and uterine cancer showed marked improvement when given the herb medicine, the researchers said. The preparation is based on recipes listed in an ancient book of Chinese medicine and said to be effective for breast and skin cancer. The formula was worked out after performing animal tests for a three-year period. Experiments had been conducted since 1974 on advanced cancer cases treated at the hospitals attached to the two universities. Nine out of 13 cases administered the preparation made good progress and one person was able to resume a normal life even though rectal cancer had recurred and spread. bdbfd11e85293053.title: Delhi’s longest cycling track planned along Yamuna: Route details, opening date, cost and purpose
bdbfd11e85293053.summary: The Delhi Development Authority (DDA) is planning to develop a 24-km cycling track along the Yamuna riverbank , which could become the national capital’s longest cycling track. The proposed route will run from the Old Railway Bridge near Wazirabad to National Highway 24 near Sarai Kale Khan, forming part of a wider plan to improve public access to the riverfront. The DDA has floated a tender for the first phase of the project, with the overall estimated construction cost pegged at around ₹ 16 crore, PTI cited an official as saying. The project is part of the DDA’s broader vision under the approved Master Plans of Delhi 2047 to strengthen the connection between the river and residents through green spaces, cycling routes, walking trails and recreational facilities. The proposed cycling track will stretch along the western bank of the Yamuna, connecting areas from the Old Railway Bridge near Wazirabad to National Highway 24 near Sarai Kale Khan. The route forms part of a larger 52-km Yamuna corridor planned to be developed in three phases. The first phase will cover the stretch from the Old Railway Bridge near Wazirabad to National Highway 24. A public greenway measuring between 75 metres and 100 metres in width is planned along the riverbank. It will include cycling and walking trails, along with spaces for passive recreational activities. The bank's cost-to-income ratio stood at 50.38 per cent in the first half of the current fiscal year, down from 53.3 per cent in September 2025, as it focuses on rationalising expenses and maximising profitability, he told PTI in an interview. "We are aiming to go below 50 per cent this financial year. That is the first target we have set for ourselves. In the next two years, by 2028-29, we should be somewhere around 45 per cent," he said. Chandra said the bank was working on two key areas -- rationalisation of expenses and maximisation of profits-- while sensitising its various units about the importance of improving operational efficiency. 35f3097a2554a437.title: Bhavani devotees throng Kanaka Durga temple atop Indrakeeladri
35f3097a2554a437.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 11:49 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA Sri Durga Malleswara Swamy Varla Devasthanam, abode of Goddess Kanaka Durga, atop Indrakeeladri, witnessed a massive influx of Bhavani devotees and general pilgrims from the early hours of Sunday (October 25, 2026), with thousands arriving from far-flung places to conclude their Bhavani Deeksha. The hill shrine was filled with devotees dressed in red, while chants of “Jai Bhavani” reverberated across the temple premises, creating a spiritually charged atmosphere. The rush began early in the morning, with devotees arriving from both the Ghat Road and Kanaka Durga Nagar routes. The queues grew crowded as the number of pilgrims continued to swell. In view of the heavy rush, the temple administration introduced several measures to regulate the crowd and facilitate faster darshan for Bhavani devotees and general pilgrims. As part of these arrangements, Antaralaya Darshan, which allows devotees to enter the inner sanctum, was completely suspended from the morning. Later, following the offering of Maha Nivedana to the presiding deity at noon, the temple authorities cancelled all categories of special-entry darshan tickets as well. Consequently, only free Sarva Darshan was being permitted, allowing devotees waiting in the queues to have the darshan of Sri Kanaka Durga Devi without purchasing special-entry tickets. The move was aimed at improving the flow of pilgrims and providing greater access to ordinary devotees amid the unprecedented rush. Temple officials were closely monitoring arrangements to ensure uninterrupted distribution of drinking water to pilgrims waiting in the queues and to prevent inconvenience during the prolonged waiting periods. Temple Executive Officer V.K. Seena Naik appealed to the devotees to cooperate with the temple staff and security personnel, maintain discipline and follow the prescribed arrangements to ensure a smooth and orderly darshan of the Goddess. Published - October 25, 2026 11:49 p

She felt it wasn't right to cast a ballot in a place she no longer lived. But now, after seeing the far right gain power, Natra, 61, said she believed she had no choice. Ahead of Israel's election on Tuesday - the first since the 2023 Hamas-led attacks and ensuing wars in the region - Natra spent thousands of dollars to travel nearly 6,000 miles from Toronto to Tel Aviv to be in the country and vote, she said. Israeli law generally requires citizens to vote in person in the country, with narrow exceptions for diplomats and certain official emissaries abroad. Natra said she plans to cast her ballot for parties not aligned with the current government led by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. 222f9fc71a1d9a00.title: Sukhoi, Tejas, Prachand headline IAF's grand air show in Varanasi
222f9fc71a1d9a00.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday attended the Indian Air Force's air show 'Wings over Ganges' at Namo Ghat in Varanasi and witnessed a display of aerial manoeuvres by the IAF's premier display teams. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, Uttar Pradesh Governor Anandiben Patel and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath accompanied Modi on the final day of the three-day air show held to commemorate the 94th anniversary of the Indian Air Force. According to Air Force officials, the show features fighter aircraft, including the Sukhoi-30 MKI, indigenous Tejas and LCH Prachand, along with helicopter displays. Three Kiran aircraft flew in a 'V' formation, creating a spectacle in the colours of the national flag, while Mi-17 helicopters carrying the tricolour participated in the Omkar formation. The Surya Kiran aerobatic team showcased precision flying and coordinated manoeuvres, while the Sarang helicopter display team enthralled spectators with its aerial stunts. Modi's presence at the event .

7b5a154b830be4c5.title: Gunmen open fire at church during funeral in Jordan, killing 7, injuring 40
7b5a154b830be4c5.summary: Gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a church in Jordan on Friday, killing seven people and wounding 40 others, authorities said. The shooting took place at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, about 180 kilometres (110 miles) south of the capital, Amman. Footage broadcast on Jordanian state television showed two gunmen who appear to be holding pistols approaching the church and firing shots. A third man who appears to be holding a semiautomatic rifle then approaches and opens fire, and all three then run toward the church. Video footage taken by witnesses shows broken glass and pools of blood on the floor of the church. Dorgham Halasa, who was among the mourners inside the church, said intense gunfire erupted 15 minutes after the funeral had started, and then people started running. "It was a weird situation, and heavy gunfire," Halasa said. He did not see the gunmen, but said other people reported seeing four of them. The Associated Press could not independently verify the number

b8b8014b8ecf7b27.title: Aung San Suu Kyi speaks to son after five years in detention in Myanmar
b8b8014b8ecf7b27.summary: The son of Myanmar's former leader Aung San Suu Kyi said Friday that when he finally got to speak with his mother, who has spent more than five years in detention in the Southeast Asian country, it seemed in some ways like not much time had passed at all. "She sounds like herself, and still sounds strong," said Kim Aris, adding that her voice was a bit croaky, like she had a cold. Myanmar's military government on Thursday allowed Aris a 20-minute phone call with his 81-year-old mother, one of the world's most famous political prisoners. He spoke from Myanmar's embassy in London to Suu Kyi in her country's capital, Naypyitaw, where she's serving an 18-year sentence under house arrest. Suu Kyi has been detained since February 2021, when Myanmar's army ousted her elected government. Held mostly incommunicado, she's serving an 18-year prison term on charges that supporters and rights groups say are bogus and politically inspired. It's not the first time she has been kept as a prisoner -

2759c8ffd56e2f7a.summary: Rescuers combed through a remote area in the Chinese region of Tibet on Friday after a magnitude 7 earthquake killed at least 16 people, injured 76 and collapsed hundreds of homes, according to Chinese state media. The disaster struck Nagqu, a city north of Tibet's capital Lhasa that is some 4,800 metres (15,748 feet) above sea level, on Thursday. At least 339 homes collapsed, and officials told journalists they were concerned about further building collapses from aftershocks, as well as casualties from rockslides. China's national broadcaster CCTV aired footage on Friday showing collapsed houses and shattered stone walls in Nagqu. More than 12,000 residents in the region were evacuated, with additional shelters under construction, China's official news agency Xinhua reported. No one was reported missing in Baqen County in Nagqu, where the earthquake struck. Search and rescue efforts are complicated by the geography and low temperatures, officials said. 7ab5c6c7938a4e2b.title: Tree falls near school in Ashok Nagar; a lucky escape for students
7ab5c6c7938a4e2b.summary: Updated - October 25, 2026 02:25 am IST Sixth Avenue in Ashok Nagar following the rains in October 2026. Photo: special arrangement A tree near Sixth Avenue (near the entrance of GRT school) in Ashok Nagar fell on October 21. As luck would have it, it was a holiday for the school on account of the rains. This road comes under the purview of Ward 135 in Zone 10 (Kodambakkam). Earlier, on October 18, another tree had fallen, and this was on 86th Street in Ashok Nagar. In this incident, a bike was damaged. From time to time, a road is dug up several times for various works including stormwater drain construction, laying water pipes, sewage pipes and telecommunication cables. This could damage the roots of trees, and as a result, they get uprooted. Hence, the Parks Department of the Greater Chennai Corporation should take necessary measures without any delay and prevent the occurrence of untoward incidents. 1ca9ef8d9f92f32d.title: Ashoke Sen becomes first Indian physicist to win 2026 Oskar Klein Medal
1ca9ef8d9f92f32d.summary: Indian physicist Ashoke Sen has been awarded the 2026 Oskar Klein Medal, becoming the first Indian physicist to receive the honour. Sen, an ICTS-Infosys Madhava Chair professor at the International Centre for Theoretical Sciences (ICTS)-Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR), Bengaluru, is widely regarded as an architect of modern string theory. The theory postulates that the elementary constituents of matter are tiny one-dimensional, string-like objects instead of point particles. It thus tries to put forth a unifying description for matter and forces between them. Established in 1988 and named after the Swedish theoretical physicist Oskar Klein, the medal is awarded annually by Stockholm University and the Nobel Committee for Physics of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences. Honouring the memory of Klein, the organising committee of the Oskar Klein Memorial Lectures every year invites a distinguished researcher to give a memorial lecture and to receive the Klein medal. 4d68a1f200d353d5.title: AU Small Finance Bank Q2FY27 result: Net profit jumps 53% to ₹858 crore
4d68a1f200d353d5.summary: AU Small Finance Bank on Saturday reported a 53 per cent surge in net profit at Rs 858 crore for the second quarter ended September 30, 2026 on the back of improvement in interest income. The lender had earned a net profit of Rs 561 crore in the year-ago period. Total income rose to Rs 6,382 crore in the quarter under review from Rs 5,224 crore in the same period a year ago, AU Small Finance Bank said in a regulatory filing. Interest income increased to Rs 5,612 crore as against Rs 4,511 crore in the corresponding second quarter of the previous year. Net interest income of the bank improved to Rs 2,820 crore in the July-September quarter, from Rs 2,144 crore in the September quarter of 2025, registering a growth of 32 per cent. Net interest margin increased to 5.8 per cent from 5.5 per cent at the end of September 2025. Asset quality of the bank also improved with gross non-performing assets (NPAs) rising to 1.99 per cent of gross advances at the end of the September quarter 2026

feb45a02f9c05114.title: Protests great mechanism for governments to perform better: Wangchuk
feb45a02f9c05114.summary: Climate activist and educationist Sonam Wangchuk on Saturday said protests are a great mechanism for governments to perform better and cited the unrest in Sri Lanka and Bangladesh as examples of what could happen if they are disallowed. Speaking at the IPF Festival here, he said nations all around the world happily permit protests, and that too right in front of Parliament. In fact in all the countries the front of parliament is the face of the protest, Wangchuk claimed. He said in countries like the United Kingdom, Norway and Sweden, protests are allowed right in front of parliament. "In India, it was far from Parliament.. 2c154bb19c3f4ee2.summary: A 5.3-magnitude earthquake struck China's Qinghai province on Saturday, two days after a powerful 7.0-magnitude temblor in neighbouring Tibet left 16 people dead and 76 others injured. The latest quake jolted Zadoi County in northwest China's Qinghai Province at 4:39 pm (Beijing Time), according to the China Earthquake Networks Centre (CENC). The epicentre, at a depth of 10 kilometres, was monitored at 32.54 degrees north latitude and 93.97 degrees east longitude, the centre said. There were no immediate reports of casualties or damage from Saturday's earthquake. The fragile Tibetan Plateau is prone to powerful earthquakes as it lies in a region where the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates collide, generating significant seismic activity. 9243627e57fe77bd.title: CJP seeks impartial probe into Chorabagan stampede that killed 19 in Bengal
9243627e57fe77bd.summary: CJP's West Bengal unit on Saturday demanded an impartial probe into the Chorabagan stampede that claimed 19 lives and called for accountability for any negligence established during the investigation. The party organised a condolence programme and a press conference to pay tribute to the victims and express solidarity with the affected families. Addressing the press conference, a Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) member called for safety audits, trained personnel, emergency evacuation plans and better coordination among emergency services. In a statement, CJP coordinator Prakriti Sahu outlined the party's demands, including timely financial assistance and medical support for the affected families and injured, stronger safety guidelines for major public gatherings and festival pandals across the state, and regular public updates on the investigation and relief measures. The party said it would submit its demands in writing to the relevant authorities and seek details of the action taken.

b2bf9ac9c1ddb5b7.title: Centre extends Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh's tenure by one year
b2bf9ac9c1ddb5b7.summary: The Centre has extended the tenure of Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh by one year, till October 31, 2027, according to an official order issued on Saturday. The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC) approved the extension of Singh, a 1989-batch IAS officer of the Kerala cadre, beyond his scheduled tenure ending on October 31, 2026. "The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet has approved extension in the service of Rajesh Kumar Singh, IAS (KL:89) as Secretary, Department of Defence, Ministry of Defence, for a period of one year beyond 31.10.2026, i.e. up to 31.10.2027 or until further orders whichever is earlier," the order issued by the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) read. The extension was granted in relaxation of the provisions of Fundamental Rule 56(d) and Rule 16(1A) of the All India Services (Death-cum-Retirement Benefits) Rules, 1958, the order said.

They said that the pathway was also completely closed after a resident on the pathway erected fencing on one portion of the stretch. As a result, residents had to take a detour of three km to reach Ramdass Nagar and surrounding areas. 5790de2cc52c3644.title: Healthcare challenges require collaborative, technology-ledsolutions, says Health Secretary
5790de2cc52c3644.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 01:00 am IST - CHENNAI Health Secretary Darez Ahamed presents the Lifetime Achievement Award to R.V. Ramani, founder and managing trustee, Sankara Eye Foundation. Sathish Devadoss, convener, CII TN Healthcare Panel, and C. Devarajan, chairman, CII, T.N., are also seen. | Photo Credit: S.R. RAGHUNATHAN While the Tamil Nadu public health system is one of the best in the country, demonstrating great achievements in maternal and child health care, challenges such as the growing burden of non-communicable diseases require innovative, technology-led solutions. This is where, perhaps, a partnership with the private sector and industry could help, Tamil Nadu Health Secretary Darez Ahamed said. He was speaking at TN MedClave, 2026, of the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) on the theme ‘Intelligent Healthcare: From Innovation to Implementation’, held on Saturday. Noting that hypertension, diabetes, cancer and mental health were some of the big emerging challenges in the healthcare sector, Dr. Ahamed said cardiac issues were one of the leading causes of morbidity and mortality in the State and it was here — in ensuring that interventions reached people on time — that innovation could play a role, but this had to co-exist with implementation. Tracing patients across the health system and ensuring continuity of care for chronic diseases were other issues that needed tackling. The State had proved it could deliver quality care at scale, he added. He said the government was willing to partner to tackle these challenges jointly with the private sector and implored the conclave to take on these challenges, come up with solutions collaboratively, and importantly, evaluate progress in the future. A Lifetime Achievement Award was presented to R.V. Ramani, founder and managing trustee, Sankara Eye Foundation. Dr. Ramani highlighted the importance of evaluating progress in healthcare, the need for strong human resources, and making healthcare accessible

abacc3a3acc5ce80.title: H.E.L.P. conference held at Coimbatore hospital
abacc3a3acc5ce80.summary: Updated - October 24, 2026 11:50 pm IST - Coimbatore Health & Environment Leadership Platform (H.E.L.P.) Tamil Nadu Chapter Conference 2026 was held on Saturday (October 24) at Ganga Medical Centre & Hospitals, Coimbatore. Sustainability has become a buzzword across industries, but it is now the need of the hour—particularly in healthcare, where energy consumption, water use, waste generation and climate-related risks have a direct bearing on responsible and resilient service delivery. Guided by the theme ‘Strategic Leadership for Sustainable Healthcare’, the conference aimed at encouraging healthcare institutions to move beyond awareness and adopt practical, measurable sustainability initiatives. Welcome address was by Rama Rajasekaran, director-Ganga Hospitals, president - H.E.L.P Tamil Nadu Chapter. The session included a ceremonial lamp lighting, followed by the inaugural address delivered by Alexander Thomas, chairman of H.E.L.P., Public Health Foundation of India (PHFI). A. Lingiah, medical director- Yashoda Hospitals, regional lead – H.E.L.P South Zone, delivered the special address, highlighting the significance of leadership and collective action in advancing sustainable healthcare. The speakers included Chandan Khanna, India project manager, Healthcare Without Harm, who spoke on the business case for sustainable healthcare; Vinod, chairperson, Healthcare Engineers Forum and head consultant at VBG Consulting Engineers, Kochi, who spoke on hospital utilities and carbon footprint; Chandran Vinoth Kumar, chairperson, Supply Chain Leaders Forum, CAHO, who spoke on green procurement; Krishna Murthy, director, DAK Healthcare Consultancy, Chennai, who spoke on Green OT challenges and implementation; Vanitha Mohan, chairperson, Pricol Holdings Private Ltd. and managing trustee, Siruthuli, who spoke on water conservation and leadership; Ashwini Dokka, associate counsellor, IGBC- Green Commercial, who spoke on green hospital building standards; and Ramesh Babu, medic

36a2b971107368f8.title: We only tried to make Thirumavalavan the Chief Minister, says Dhinakaran
36a2b971107368f8.summary: Published - October 24, 2026 11:47 pm IST - CHENNAI AMMK general secretary T.T.V. Dhinakaran. | Photo Credit: R. ASHOK T.T.V. Dhinakaran, general secretary of the Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam (AMMK), said the AIADMK and the DMK never attempted to form a government together, and instead, efforts were made to make VCK president Thol. Thirumavalavan the Chief Minister. Speaking to reporters in Sivagangai, Mr. Dhinakaran said they initiated this move because the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) did not have the support of enough MLAs. “Speaking as someone who was part of that alliance, no effort was ever made for the AIADMK and the DMK to join hands and form a government. The TVK only had 107 MLAs. [DMK president] M.K. Stalin had made it clear that the DMK would not attempt to come to power. Therefore, we tried to form a government led by the AIADMK. At that time, I addressed [Chief Minister] Vijay and said if you were unable to form the government, please extend support so that we, the common people, could form it. However, the Left parties refused their support, stating that backing [AIADMK general secretary] Edappadi K. Palaniswami would be tantamount to supporting the BJP. Following this, all of us, including EPS [Mr. Palaniswami], made efforts to make Thirumavalavan the Chief Minister,” he said. Mr. Dhinakaran further clarified that this initiative was not to prevent the TVK from forming the government, but rather to stop their MLAs from being poached. He asserted that the DMK and the AIADMK could never align under any circumstances. Responding to another query, he said those grieving Mr. Palaniswami’s inability to bring the AIADMK back to power should convey their views directly to him in person rather than airing them publicly, adding that the AMMK and the AIADMK would continue working together. Speaking to reporters in Sivagangai, Mr. Dhinakaran said they initiated this move because the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) did not have the support of enough MLAs. “Speaking as someone who was part of that alliance, no effort was ever made for the AIADMK and the DMK to join hands and form a government. The TVK only had 107 MLAs. [DMK president] M.K. Stalin had made it clear that the DMK would not attempt to come to power. Therefore, we tried to form a government led by the AIADMK. At that time, I addressed [Chief Minister] Vijay and said if you were unable to form the government, please extend support so that we, the common people, could form it. e6e541e1ce3a90d5.title: SRM Medical College holds national geriatric summit
e6e541e1ce3a90d5.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 01:01 am IST - CHENNAI SRM Medical College Hospital and Research Centre, through its Department of Community Medicine, organised ‘Age Well India’, a National Geriatric Summit. Centered on the theme ‘From Prevention to Policy: Building Healthier Ageing Systems’, the summit aims to bring greater attention to the healthcare needs of older adults and the importance of strengthening systems that support healthy ageing. Binod Kumar Patro, director, National Institute of Health and Family Welfare, New Delhi and V.S. Natarajan, founder and chairman, Dr. V.S. Natarajan Geriatric Foundation, participated. Dr. Patro said that geriatric care must be integrated into primary healthcare, with a focus on prevention, rehabilitation, and dignified care for older persons. Dr. Natarajan raised the need to strengthen geriatric services, rehabilitation centres, and train more geriatricians to ensure that older people live with dignity, independence, and quality of life. R. Jayanthi, dean (Medical), SRM Medical College Hospital and Research was present, a press release said. 7de24362ec31c379.title: Tiruvannamalai Corporation sets up 10 temporary shelters for families in Arunachala Hills
7de24362ec31c379.summary: Published - October 24, 2026 11:59 pm IST - TIRUVANNAMALAI Collector Vandhana Garg held an inspection in Tiruvannamalai town to assess rain-preparedness on Saturday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement With the onset of the Northeast monsoon, Tiruvannamalai Corporation has set up at least 10 temporary shelters, mostly community centres, to accommodate families in Arunachala Hills. Corporation officials said that along with the Forest Department, local police and revenue officials, civic officials have identified at least 1,400 vulnerable families - those residing in the upper portion of the hills. “Adequate shelters have been arranged during emergencies. Most of these accommodations are located at least 500 metres away from the hills to ensure safety of relocated families,” K. Balasubramanian, Commissioner, Tiruvannamalai Corporation, told The Hindu. At present, over 6,000 families are living in small settlements in the hills. Of this, the Revenue Department has identified 1,535 illegal settlements, mostly houses and commercial establishments. Around 140 illegal settlements fall under the Corporation limits. Demolition of these illegal structures will prevent landslides in the hills during monsoon. On December 1, 2024, seven persons, including children died after heavy rain triggered a landslide. A total of 576 acres of land in the hills are encroached upon, with most of them being houses. Along with civic officials, Collector Vandhana Garg inspected Mada Streets around Arunachaleswarar temple, a bus terminus, Girivalam Path, and a market in town to assess rain preparedness. Sudden showers for the past few days have inundated key stretches in the town. Shops on Mada Streets were stagnated with knee-deep water. “With Karthigai Deepam festival, the town should be prepared to handle the monsoon, especially by preventing water stagnation ,” said R. de85488919f9cd0a.title: Corporation RDCs inspect drain cleaning across Chennai
de85488919f9cd0a.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 12:58 am IST - Chennai GCC Region Deputy Commissioner (Central) H.R. Kaushik inspecting the precautionary arrangements for the Northeast monsoon in Kodambakkam Zone on Saturday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement While the city braces for more rain, the Regional Deputy Commissioners (RDCs) of the three regions of Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) inspected pumping stations, stormwater drains, canals and subways, reviewed ongoing drain works and checked arrangements for National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) personnel deployed for rescue operations on Saturday (October 24). RDC (North) Swetha Suman inspected basic facilities and food supplies for NDRF personnel stationed at the Chief Minister’s Marriage Hall on Anna Pillai Street in Royapuram for rescue operations during the monsoon. RDC (Central) H.R. Kaushik inspected a motor pump-equipped pumping station on Duraisamy Road and the Parangusapuram subway in Kodambakkam Zone, besides Nandanam Canal and the children’s playground area on Puthuth theru in West Saidapet. He also reviewed precautionary measures at a Tamil Nadu Urban Habitat Development Board residential area on Pachaiyappa Veerasamy Street in Ward 97. He inspected desilting of stormwater drains on Railway Border Road and ongoing drain works on Aziz Nagar Street in West Mambalam. Officials were asked to expedite the works and maintain continuous surveillance of canals and subways. RDC (South) Aftab Rasool inspected integrated stormwater drain works on Old Mahabalipuram Road in Ward 178, Adyar Zone, and reviewed precautionary measures in other parts of the southern region. MLAs, zonal officers and officials were present. 0e8b07ea362666d3.title: Association questions DPH over gag order for govt. doctors
0e8b07ea362666d3.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 01:00 am IST - CHENNAI The Service Doctors and Post Graduates Association (SDPGA) has questioned the Director of Public Health (DPH) and Preventive Medicine for issuing a gag order on government doctors. The DPH had recently issued a circular stating that the employees of the directorate should not criticise the policies, schemes, and actions of the Central or State governments in public, through media, or at public meetings. The association asked in a statement issued whether the DPH had passed the gag order to prevent government doctors from questioning him on social media about Government Order (G.O.) 354, relating to pay and promotions. The G.O., issued in 2009, contains a clause for review in 2012, and thereafter every five years. But it was not reviewed in 2017 and 2022. In January 2023, an order was issued by the Additional Chief Secretary (Health), appointing the DPH as head of the committee to review the G.O., but it was not done, the association said. The SDPGA sought clarification from the DPH on whether the services of government doctors were regularised on the completion of one year. It said there were delays exceeding five years, forcing women doctors to struggle to obtain maternity leave benefits. It also flagged the delays in promotions for doctors due to administrative inefficiencies. The association said that when such delays continue to affect doctors, passing gag orders was unacceptable. It urged the Health Minister and Health Secretary to review G.O. 354 and fill all vacant pay band-4 posts on a war footing. 438c5041672ff967.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 01:05 am IST Security personnel keeping vigil outside Jamia Millia Islamia. Jamia Millia Islamia (JMI) on Saturday shifted all classes online and said the campus gates, libraries and canteens would remain closed until further notice to ensure “student safety” amid an ongoing protest demanding the restoration of student union elections. The decision followed a failed attempt by the administration to “persuade” the protesters to call off their agitation, the university said in a statement. The protesting students and the All India Students’ Association (AISA) alleged that the university staff tried to forcibly remove them from the protest site on Saturday afternoon while police deployment outside the campus increased. The university said the decision to move classes online with immediate effect was a precautionary measure taken in view of the prevailing situation and to ensure the safety and security of students. In a notice issued on Saturday, the office of the Dean of Students’ Welfare directed students to follow their online class schedules and avoid visiting the campus until further notice. Several students have been on a hunger strike since October 12, demanding the restoration of student union elections, which were last held in 2006 before the union was dissolved following campus violence. JMI had constituted a high-level committee on October 18 to engage with the protesting students and look into their demands. 92a920725b63b3c6.summary: Updated - October 25, 2026 01:04 am IST - Chennai Persons with disabilities are disappointed that a government order for free travel in buses has still not been formulated. Since its announcement in the State Budget in the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly in August, 2026. While women with disabilities are automatically covered under the Vetri Payanam scheme where women and transpersons can travel in State buses for free, men with disabilities have not been included. The announcement made by the Social Welfare and Women Empowerment Minister K. Jegadeshwari expanded it to persons with disabilities and their companions with a UDID card. However, as there has been no G.O. published in this regard, men with disabilities continue to wait to avail themselves of the scheme. Nethrodaya founder C. Govindakrishnan said, “The G.O. for free bus travel for persons with disabilities has not been issued even after 53 days of the announcement. This inordinate delay has prevented eligible persons with disabilities from availing the free travel in government buses.” Jhansi Rani, State general secretary of Tamil Nadu Association for the Rights of All Types of Differently Abled and Caregivers, said the scheme is important as women with disabilities might be accompanied by male caregivers. “In this regard, they would be made to pay for their travel, increasing their expenses. Further, persons with disabilities are usually not allowed to go out due to the extra financial expenses, the delay in the G.O. to include men with disabilities adds to their reduced travel,” she said. Govindakrishnan pointed out that a proposal to the Welfare of the Differently Abled Department Secretary was forwarded only on September 16.
