aa9f629f06beb7a9.title: BJP says textbooks meet quality norms; AAP seeks lab testing
aa9f629f06beb7a9.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 01:00 am IST Delhi Education Minister Ashish Sood on Saturday said the government followed the prescribed process in procuring NCERT textbooks for schools at ₹28 per copy against ₹55 under the previous dispensation. Responding to Aam Aadmi Party’s (AAP) allegations of “substandard” quality textbooks supplied to students, the Minister said a review has been ordered. AAP challenged Chief Minister Rekha Gupta to send the books to a laboratory for testing. Addressing a press conference, Mr. Sood said, “AAP is alleging a scam to stay relevant and misleading the public. Despite inflation, the BJP government has capped the price of textbooks for government schools that was almost double during the AAP’s tenure.” Following a review, strict penal action will be initiated against those involved in spreading deliberate falsehoods, he added. On Friday, AAP’s Delhi chief Saurabh Bharadwaj alleged irregularities in the BJP government’s school textbook printing and tendering process. He claimed that the quality of the paper used in the textbooks was substandard. In response, Mr. Sood displayed a copy of the tender document and said the government had followed the prescribed process. Challenging Mr. Sood to make public the file in which his department officials have moved for full payment to the vendors, Mr. Bharadwaj said, “The Minister has not answered why these books have very poor printing quality and use cheap 60 GSM paper, while the tender specified standard 80 GSM paper.” Published - October 25, 2026 01:00 am IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscriber Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. d3ef12dcd1709824.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 01:00 am IST Chief Minister Rekha Gupta taking stock of preparations for Chhath Puja at a ghat along the Munak Canal on Saturday. | Photo Credit: PTI Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday inspected the ongoing construction of a Chhath ghat in the Munak Canal area near Prem Bari Bridge. She said the ghat would provide devotees with better facilities to offer prayers and a clean, beautiful and well-organised space ahead of Chhath Puja. Directing officials on site to ensure that the work was completed on time, Ms. Gupta said the government aimed to complete the construction of all such ghats and related development works before Chhath Puja. “Chhath is deeply connected with Delhi’s cultural identity and public faith. A large number of devotees offer prayers to the Sun God and Chhathi Maiya during this sacred festival. The government, therefore, has a responsibility to provide better facilities for devotees and ensure that places of worship remain clean and well-organised.” During the visit, she reviewed the progress of various works and directed officials to ensure proper lighting during the festival, celebrated predominantly by Purvanchalis, people from eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and parts of Jharkhand, living in the national capital. She also issued instructions on waste management . “There must be no accumulation of garbage on roads and footpaths, foul smells or haphazard waste collection under any circumstances. A proper system for waste collection and disposal must be developed,” she added. 648584b7d7a73d75.title: Law and order situation in T.N. is in an extremely dire state, says Palaniswami
648584b7d7a73d75.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 12:22 am IST - CHENNAI AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami. | Photo Credit: E. LAKSHMI NARAYANAN AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami has alleged that the law and order situation in Tamil Nadu was in an extremely dire state. He listed several incidents reflecting the prevailing law and order conditions and questioned the inaction of the government. “Reports that a woman was hacked to death by an unidentified intruder inside her house near Sathankulam, a young boy who sought a lift went missing near Uthangarai in Krishnagiri district, and a student died due to caste discrimination at a government-aided school in Coimbatore are deeply shocking. What action has been taken over the death of a student due to caste discrimination under this regime, which merely invokes ‘social justice’ in its rhetoric?” Mr. Palaniswami asked. Pointing out that the young girl who went missing in Gingee has still not been traced, he asked whether the government had not even suspected that the repeated disappearances of children might be following a pattern. Mr. Palaniswami urged the government to conduct an intensive investigation into the disappearances of children from all angles and demanded stringent action regarding the incidents in Coimbatore and Sathankulam. 6dd8e6d9aea6ab24.title: P.B. Siddhartha College signs MoU with Tech In to enhance students’ employability
6dd8e6d9aea6ab24.summary: Published - October 24, 2026 11:54 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA P.B. Siddhartha College of Arts and Science, Vijayawada, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Tech In Process Private Limited to enhance students’ employability, technical skills and industry exposure. The three-year agreement was signed by college principal Meka Ramesh and Managing Director of Tech In Gubbala Srinivasa Rao on Ssaturday. Director Vemuri Baburao and dean P. Rajesh C. Jampala said the collaboration aims to bridge the gap between academic learning and industry requirements by providing students with practical knowledge and industry-oriented training. Under the MoU, Tech In Process Private Limited will extend technical support and guidance for industry-focused training programmes, student internships, academic and industry projects, resume preparation, conferences, workshops, faculty development programmes, and career guidance and counselling. The partnership may also include mock interviews, aptitude training, soft-skills development and job-readiness programmes to prepare students for employment opportunities and meet the evolving demands of the industry. The initiative is expected to strengthen industry-academia collaboration and provide students with greater exposure to professional practices and workplace expectations. MBA faculty member Rahman, the placement officer, and Computer Science faculty member Kavuru Sridhar participated in the programme. 7395cfa99f03e793.title: Six election officials removed in U.P. after SP flags voter list errors
7395cfa99f03e793.summary: Updated - October 25, 2026 01:02 am IST - LUCKNOW The Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) of Uttar Pradesh on Saturday removed five Booth Level Officers (BLOs) and a computer assistant from election duties following an investigation into voter list discrepancies in Azamgarh. Action has also been initiated against three senior electoral registration officials. The orders come after the Samajwadi Party (SP) held a press conference on October 15, alleging that a voter named ‘Vikas Yadav’ was listed 10 times in the voter list for the Azamgarh assembly constituency (347). Following a detailed probe by the District Election Officer of Azamgarh, authorities found that the name “Vikas Yadav” appeared 13 times in Hindi on the rolls. According to the CEO’s office, one of the entries belongs to a voter of the same name and age from the Chauri Chaura constituency in Gorakhpur district. Deletion proceedings have been initiated for two other duplicate entries. The investigation revealed that the remaining 11 entries actually belong to 11 different individuals living in Azamgarh. Officials have now filled out Form-8 to correct the names and personal details of 10 of these individuals, ensuring only the actual Vikas Yadav remains on the roll under that name. In response to the clerical lapses, the CEO directed the immediate removal of the responsible computer assistant and five BLOs from voter registration work. Authorities have also issued notices regarding the termination of their services. Furthermore, the state election body has ordered charge sheets and departmental action against the then Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) and two Assistant Electoral Registration Officers (AEROs) for negligence and poor supervision. The three senior officials face potential action under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950. 05d719958793295c.title: PSGIM students use management learning for community benefit
05d719958793295c.summary: Updated - October 24, 2026 11:49 pm IST - COIMBATORE During the National Management Week 2026, around 250 students of PSG Institute of Management (PSGIM), Coimbatore, will take management learning beyond the classroom and into the community through initiatives focusing on waste management, rabies awareness, and preventing pollution caused by indiscriminate poster pasting, under the overarching theme of ‘Clean and Safe City’. Observed from October 26 to 31 under the aegis of the Association of Indian Management Schools (AIMS-New Delhi), the initiatives reflect a simple yet meaningful belief: building a better city is a shared responsibility. During the week, students will engage with communities at more than 30 identified waste hotspots across Coimbatore. By promoting waste segregation at source and responsible disposal, they will encourage everyday practices that protect the environment and improve neighbourhoods for everyone. The initiative will also highlight the connection between unmanaged waste and street dogs. Discarded food and other waste can attract dogs to public spaces, increase the risk of conflict and create unhealthy conditions for people and animals. Students will also conduct rabies awareness activities across 30 identified locations in the city in association with the Humane Animal Society (HAS), to promote rabies prevention, safe interactions with street dogs and humane animal care. These activities will reinforce the importance of keeping public spaces free of food waste and other refuse that can attract dogs. Students will also work with NGOs, including Olirum Kovai, on poster-related interventions and community engagement in locations such as Vellalore. Through these efforts, they will contribute to making public spaces cleaner and more welcoming. Through these initiatives, PSGIM aims to nurture future managers who recognise that leadership is defined not only by professional achievements, but also by the willingness to understand community need

8aecefea472c8045.title: Andhra Pradesh braces for very severe cyclonic storm; landfall likely between Bapatla and Vizag on October 28
8aecefea472c8045.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 01:20 am IST - VIJAYAWADA Dark clouds over the Kandula Obul Reddy Reservoir in Prakasam district on Saturday. | Photo Credit: KOMMURI SRINIVAS The cyclonic storm brewing over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a ‘very severe cyclonic storm’, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said. It is likely to be the second highest in terms of intensity. Last year’s Montha was classified as a ‘severe cyclonic storm’. The maximum sustained wind speed associated with a very severe cyclonic storm is likely to be between 118 km per hour and 221 km per hour. During Montha, the wind speed recorded at Machilipatnam was 65 kmph, while the wind speed this time may go up to 130 kmph, weather experts said. According to the IMD bulletin released at 9.30 p.m. on Saturday, the well-marked low-pressure area formed over the east-central and adjoining south-east Bay of Bengal on Saturday morning concentrated into a depression by the evening. The depression lay centred over the same region, which is about 510 km off the coast of Andaman Islands, 820 km off Vishakhapatnam coast, 910 km off Kakinada coast, 1,020 km off Machilipatnam cost and 1,100 km off Bapatla coast. The weather system is likely to intensify into a deep depression and then gradually recurve towards the east-central and adjoining south-east Bay of Bengal on Sunday. It is very likely to intensify further into a cyclonic storm over the east-central and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal by Monday morning, and further intensify into a severe cyclonic storm over west-central Bay of Bengal around October 27. Thereafter, it is likely to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm and reach the west-central Bay of Bengal near the Andhra Pradesh coast around October 28. 1dd7c7fba6d94005.title: Man arrested with 66 kg of firecrackers in Rohini
1dd7c7fba6d94005.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 12:58 am IST - New Delhi Police found that the accused brought the firecrackers for sale without a valid licence. | Photo Credit: SUSHIL KUMAR VERMA A 33-year-old man was arrested for allegedly storing and transporting 66 kg of firecrackers illegally in the Vijay Vihar area of Rohini, police said on Saturday. Police personnel on patrol spotted a three-wheeler parked outside a park on the night of October 20. When questioned, the driver failed to give a satisfactory response, police said. "On checking the vehicle, various types of firecrackers were found inside," a senior police officer said. The driver was identified as Vijender Kumar, a resident of Rampura. 3ef745fde0ee5413.title: My father pushes me to become a better player, says Tagenarine
3ef745fde0ee5413.summary: Updated - October 25, 2026 01:28 am IST - Chennai Tagenarine had a stint at the Super Kings Academy recently. | Photo Credit: AFP Every time Tagenarine Chanderpaul makes his way into the middle, he carries the weight of a surname that is etched in cricket fanatics’ hearts. No day on the pitch passes by without the mention of his father Shivnarine Chanderpaul, a legendary figure in the world game. Unfortunately for the West Indies opener, he has not kicked on in his Test career after entering the international arena with promise. Four years into his journey with the Men in Maroon, Tagenarine has come to terms with the constant comparisons with his dad but is striving to create a name for himself. “Wherever I go, people expect me to perform as good as him. But I cannot be him, I can only be myself,” the 30-year-old told The Hindu recently. “He was a great player, but I just try to be myself. As an individual, I do the best I can.” While Tagenarine wades through challenges, Shivnarine, as both a father and mentor, attempts to make the former’s path easier. “He shares his knowledge and experience to make me a better player. He is a very competitive and serious guy. He keeps pushing me to get better,” said the southpaw. Tagenarine, lucky enough to be taught a masterclass on a regular basis, knows where he is lacking: he has just one ton and two half-centuries in 15 long-format matches (758 runs). “I need to be more consistent, convert starts into big scores. Sometimes, you get comfortable in the middle and get out. But Test cricket is tough... there is no time to relax,” the top-order batter added. His stint at the Super Kings Academy — in the company of West Indies red-ball teammates — may be the launchpad for bigger things ahead. “I always believe in putting in the work, so hopefully I can reap the rewards of it”. 97958a5bcc68fac9.title: Students mark 90th anniversary of Temple Entry Proclamation
97958a5bcc68fac9.summary: Published - October 25, 2026 12:02 am IST - Thiruvananthapuram A copy of the Temple Entry Proclamation being distributed by students of Government Boys Higher Secondary School, Karamana, and ward councillor Karamana Ajith to autorickshaw drivers Students of Government Boys Higher Secondary School, Karamana, marked the 90th anniversary of the historic Temple Entry Proclamation of 1936 by distributing copies of the proclamation in houses and public spaces on Saturday. The Temple Entry Proclamation was issued by Chithira Thirunal Balarama Varma, former king of the erstwhile Travancore kingdom, on November 12, 1936, in the wake of the social reformation under way then. It opened the doors of Hindu temples in the State to marginalised communities and drew the attention of the entire nation to Travancore. A copy of the proclamation in possession of the Archives department was received by students and teachers of the school, and then distributed to houses, residents’ associations, shops and commercial establishments, and libraries for display. Through autorickshaw drivers, the proclamation reached passengers too. The proclamation’s 90th anniversary also saw nonagenarians Gopalakrishnan, a retired income tax official, and his wife Sarojam, who live near the school, being felicitated with the proclamation and a ponnada by class V student Shikha and ward councillor Karama Ajith. At a time when marginalisation was re-emerging, the proclamation taught lessons, head teacher Mini. Y said. Principal Bilu V.B. was present. As part of the year-long celebrations, a proclamation rally from East Fort to Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple, cultural meets with historians, trips to memorials for reformation leaders, quiz, and other events will be organised, PTA representatives said. cde6ab97d8e39e41.summary: The administrations of former US President Joe Biden and current President Donald Trump have repeatedly asked Elon Musk's SpaceX to activate or restrict its Starlink satellite internet service in different countries, highlighting Washington's growing reliance on private technology companies to implement foreign policy objectives, according to a Reuters report citing six former senior US officials. The requests, made before the recent restrictions on Ukraine's military access to SpaceX satellite communications, included disabling Starlink to prevent Iran-backed militias in Yemen and Lebanon from using the service and activating it to provide internet access in Iran and Ukraine, Reuters reported. During Biden's presidency, US officials sought to restrict the service's availability to certain militant groups while also requesting its activation to support internet access in Iran and military communications in Ukraine, four former officials told Reuters . The Trump administration similarly asked Musk, SpaceX's chief executive, to make Starlink available in Iran following US-Israeli strikes in 2025 and 2026. The objective was to strengthen internet connectivity and communications for anti-government protesters, the report said. The recent restrictions on Ukraine's access to SpaceX satellite services have renewed concerns about the relationship between the US government and Musk, whose company operates satellite communication systems considered important to the US military and its allies. The earlier requests by both administrations illustrate how Washington has increasingly depended on a private company to support diplomatic, political and military objectives abroad. The restrictions affecting Ukraine have also caused concern among European officials, some of whom argue that Europe needs to develop independent military satellite communication capabilities. 3c1cb8664e9eed7e.title: Delhi govt begins identifying ineligible old-age pension beneficiaries
3c1cb8664e9eed7e.summary: Delhi government has started a verification drive to identify and weed out ineligible beneficiaries of its old age pension scheme covering around 4.4 lakh senior citizens, officials said on Saturday. The verification process was to begin earlier, but it was halted as permission for Aadhaar authentication of the beneficiaries via a third party was not allowed. Now, the third party is carrying out door-to-door biometric beneficiary verification after receiving permission, said a senior functionary of the Delhi government. "The verification exercise will conclude in three months and we expect to create 20-25 per cent vacancies out of the total 4.4 lakh beneficiaries after weeding out the deceased and duplicate beneficiaries getting other government assistance besides the old age pension," he said. The government currently provides a monthly pension of Rs 2,000 to senior citizens aged between 60 and 69 years, while those aged 70 years and above are entitled to Rs 2,500 per month. Earl

f3e4879ac88cc5d1.title: Coforge Q2 results: Net profit surges 56.5% to ₹588 cr, revenue up 53.6%
f3e4879ac88cc5d1.summary: Coforge posted a 56.5 per cent increase in consolidated profit to Rs 588 crore in the second quarter ended September 30, 2026, driven by AI-led execution of deals, the company said on Friday. The IT firm had posted a net profit of Rs 375.8 crore in the same period a year ago. "Right now the margin uptake that we are seeing is in the existing fixed price projects where AI is getting infused," Coforge Chief Executive Officer and Executive Director, Sudhir Singh, said during the company's earnings call. Coforge signed 8 large deals the highest number signed in a single quarter across North America, Europe and Australia, which led to a total contract value of the new orders of USD 1.04 billion during the reported quarter. The company increased the operational profit margin guidance to 17 per cent for the next year from the range of 15.5 per cent to 16 per cent. Revenue from operations during the reported quarter increased by 53.6 per cent to Rs 6,171 crore from Rs 4,016 crore a year

fcce9943226f9bd1.title: Parvatipuram witnessing rapid progress, says TDP MLA
fcce9943226f9bd1.summary: Updated - October 24, 2026 09:37 pm IST - PARVATIPURAM TDP leader and wife of TDP MLA Bonela Vijaya Chandra taking up door to door campaign in Parvatipuram. | Photo Credit: ARRANGEMENT Telugu Desam Party MLA Bonela Vijaya Chandra on Saturday (October 24, 2026) said that Parvatipuram municipality has been witnessing rapid growth as the State government has sanctioned around ₹162 crore for the development of the civic body, which was established in 1959 and is one of the oldest in the State. Along with TDP leader and his wife, Bonela Anusha, he campaigned for TDP’s candidate for the chairperson post, Belagam Karuna, and for councillors in 36 wards. Speaking to the media, he said that voters are keen to vote for the TDP, JSP, and BJP in the ensuing elections, as the government has taken steps to lay new pipelines from the Thotapalli reservoir to the city, since the old pipes were damaged long ago. He stated that the government has been spending around ₹89 crore on new pipelines and has ensured dedicated water supply to every household in Parvatipuram. Ms. Anusha said there was an overwhelming response from voters to the quick developmental activities in nook and corner of the town. She alleged that the YSRCP government had neglected the town’s development during its tenure. She added that the TDP women’s wing formed special teams to intensify a door-to-door campaign in the next few days. ccac7c2927062ae1.title: KTR urges youth against ignoring AI
ccac7c2927062ae1.summary: Updated - October 24, 2026 09:05 pm IST - HYDERABAD BRS working president K.T. Rama Rao at the inauguration RandomTrees office in Hyderabad. | Photo Credit: Arrangement BRS working president K.T. Rama Rao has urged youth to embrace Artificial Intelligence (AI) as an opportunity for innovation and employment, instead of living in fear of the technology, particularly its impact on jobs. The former IT and Industries Minister, who was inaugurating the India headquarters of data, AI and innovation firm RandomTrees here, said this underscoring the significance of continuous learning, skill development and harnessing emerging technologies. Every technological revolution initially creates apprehensions but eventually opens new avenues for growth, he said, recalling the resistance to introduction of computers in the banking sector. Adapting to change was essential for progress and portraying AI as a ‘monster’ would only create unnecessary fear among people, Mr. Rao said. Highlighting the importance of strengthening Telangana’s technology ecosystem, attracting investments and preparing youth for future employment opportunities, he said the BRS government had taken several initiatives to position Hyderabad as a leading global IT destination and attract global capability centres of multinational companies. He expressed confidence that the city could emerge as a major hub for AI research, data science and technological innovation, a release from his office on Saturday said. With private sector playing a major role in employment generation, the governments should focus on creating a business-friendly environment rather than attempting to provide jobs directly to everyone. Reliable power and water supply, quality infrastructure, efficient transport and ease of doing business were essential to attract investments, Mr. Rao said. 4223785a7993584b.title: Bhatti Vikramarka calls for judicious use of water, electricity amid El Nino concerns
4223785a7993584b.summary: Updated - October 24, 2026 09:02 pm IST - KHAMMAM Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka on Saturday called for collective efforts to conserve water and electricity amid dry weather conditions and rising power demand, urging the Opposition parties to set aside political differences to tackle the emerging El Nino-related challenges. . Addressing the media at Kodumuru in Chintakani mandal of Khammam district, he appealed to the Opposition to rise above political differences, recalling the collective efforts during the COVID-19 pandemic. Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy had reviewed the situation and constituted a Cabinet Sub-Committee to address the challenges, he said. Mr. Vikramarka said peak power demand had risen from 6,648 MW at the time of Telangana’s formation in 2014 to 20,018 MW now. Daily electricity consumption had increased from 245.35 million units in October last year to 335.05 million units this October, a rise of about 37%. He said the expansion of transmission infrastructure and construction of new substations were helping the State manage the growing demand. However, declining reservoir levels were affecting hydropower generation, which normally supplies around 3,500 MW during peak night-time hours. Of the nearly three million agricultural pump sets in the State, around 1.5 million were reportedly facing groundwater shortages. He urged farmers in areas with inadequate groundwater to avoid operating motors to prevent damage to pumps and transformers. The State’s major reservoirs, with a combined capacity of 470.22 TMC, held only 178.60 TMC of water, while nearly 40% of its 44,034 tanks had less than one-fourth of their capacity filled. Mr. Vikramarka said the government would prioritise water conservation while protecting livelihoods of farmers, labourers and rural communities. 0097d0d8d6ff8464.summary: Published - October 24, 2026 09:07 pm IST - Riyadh, Saudi Arabia Smoke rises after an attack by Houthi rebels. File | Photo Credit: AP Yemen’s Houthis said on Saturday (October 24, 2026) they attacked the southern city of Aden, the interim seat of the Saudi-backed government, after accusing Riyadh of killing 16 people in strikes on capital Sanaa and a Red Sea port city. Saudi Arabia and the internationally recognised Yemeni government have come under sustained attack from the Iran-backed Houthis, shifting the focus of the wider West Asia war that erupted with U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran in February. The Saudi-led coalition said earlier on Saturday (October 24) it had intercepted two missiles targeting Saudi cities Taif and Yanbu in the kingdom’s west, before explosions were heard in Aden, the home of the government that Riyadh supports in the years-long civil war. The Houthis quickly claimed the attack, saying they targeted a naval base and military camp overseen by Saudi forces. “Our armed forces targeted Saudi enemy concentrations at the so-called Al-Nasr camp and the naval base in Aden,” Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said. The Houthis’ Al-Masirah outlet earlier reported a series of “Saudi enemy airstrikes” targeting Yemen’s capital Sanaa, including one on a house that killed at least four people and wounded several others. A separate strike at a residential building for cement factory workers in the Sanaa governorate killed six women and one child and wounded three others, the broadcaster said. It later reported “five people, the head of the family, two of his children and his two wives, have been martyred” in a strike on their home in the western port city of Hodeida, blaming it on Saudi Arabia. Yemen’s civil war, pitting the Iran-backed Houthis against the Saudi-supported and internationally recognised government, had been dormant since a ceasefire in 2022, but erupted again in July as the wider West Asia war roiled the region. 5880547296026a16.title: Caste harassment case: deceased student’s parents refuse to accept body demanding arrest of teacher, headmaster
5880547296026a16.summary: Published - October 24, 2026 09:10 pm IST - COIMBATORE The parents and relatives of Akilan, a Class 11 student of a government-aided school in Peelamedu who had ended his life due to alleged harassment over caste and eating habits, staged a sit-in protest demanding the arrest of his teacher, headmaster and other students purportedly involved in abetment. They refused to accept the body of the student. The Peelamedu police had registered a case against the teacher and a few classmates based on a complaint lodged by the deceased student’s mother Kausalyadevi. Two students were arrested after the case was registered. A press release issued by the city police said two students have been arrested in the case, and 30 other students, teachers and other witnesses were questioned. Separate inquiries were also conducted by officials of School Education Department and Child Welfare Committee. The autopsy report will provide more clues. Five special teams have been formed and CCTV camera footage and scientific evidence were being examined. The press release said that a transparent investigation was under way and that spreading of rumours should be avoided. Assistance for overcoming suicidal thoughts is available on the State’s health helpline 104, Tele-MANAS 14416, and Sneha’s Suicide Prevention Helpline 044-24640050 Published - October 24, 2026 09:10 pm IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscriber Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. 398f6c917d9a94cd.title: Five-day inclusive art festival from October 28
398f6c917d9a94cd.summary: Updated - October 24, 2026 09:03 pm IST The fifth edition of Tattva 2026, an inclusive art platform dedicated to celebrating the creativity, talent, and aspirations of artists with disabilities, will be inaugurated on October 28. Initiated by V-Excel Educational Trust, this year the festival brings together 270 plus artists from across Tamil Nadu and Kolkata for five immersive days of artistic expression, mentorship, and public engagement. This is being organised around five thematic pillars — Drishti, Srishti, Anubhav, Vistara, and Ekattva, serving as a catalyst for social inclusion, offering structured workshops, live demonstrations, collaborative murals, a curated art auction, and dedicated sales platforms designed to foster economic independence and livelihood opportunities for participating artists, said a release. In a release, Vasudha Prakash, Founder-Director of V-Excel Educational Trust, said: “This year, we also celebrate the success stories of past participants, reaffirming our core belief that talent flourishes when properly nurtured. Through exhibitions, live demonstrations, and our new art auction, Tattva 2026 connects extraordinary creators with wider audiences.” As part of this year’s celebrations, V-Excel Educational Trust will host a special art auction on October 25 at 5 p.m. at Hotel Savera. The auction will showcase selected artworks created by artists with disabilities, offering art enthusiasts and collectors an opportunity to engage with their work while supporting the artists and their creative journeys. As many as 3,841 aspirants, including 1,651 women and 19 with disabilities, attended the job fair meant to find private placements for unemployed youth. Over 200 companies attended the fair to recruit candidates for various positions, according to an official press release. Minister for Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments S. Ramesh distributed the offer letters to candidates and said that 40,625 candidates, including 684 with disabilities, had been placed through 208 job fairs organised in the State since the TVK government assumed office. Private placement fairs would continue to be held in the districts to find suitable jobs for unemployed youth. Collector Pratik Tayal and other officials participated. a435a348810cc741.title: Forum urges CM to frame rules for Malayalam Language Act
a435a348810cc741.summary: Published - October 24, 2026 09:02 pm IST - Thiruvananthapuram Eminent names from the cultural, literary, and other spheres in Keralam, under the umbrella of the Aikya Malayala Prasthanam, have urged Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan to implement the Malayalam Language Act to coincide with the 70th anniversary of the State’s formation. In a representation, prominent figures such as Adoor Gopalakrishnan, George Onakkoor, V. Madhusoodhanan Nair, C. Radhakrishnan, K. Satchidanandan, M. Mukundan, and N.S. Madhavan have pointed out that though Keralam was formed in 1956 along linguistic lines with Malayalam as its language, it neither had a language policy nor planning. Malayalam was not seen as the foundation of the State’s development nor was it projected with pride. Governments too were responsible for the neglect of Malayalam. This should change. The Malayalam Language Bill that was passed by the State Assembly in October last year became an Act after the Governor gave his assent in March this year. However, only on implementation could the Act be said to have achieved its objective. Seven months after Malayalam was declared the official language of Kerala, the Act was yet to get Rules. This was a matter of concern. On Kerala Piravi day (November 1) this year, Rules for the Malayalam Language Act should be framed and the State government should declare that Act will be implemented effectively, the representation sought. Some of the other signatories include C.V. Balakrishnan, M.N. Karassery, V.N. Murali, K.N. Ganesh, Subhash Chandran, Ezhacherry Ramachandran, P.K. Rajasekharan, Ambikasuthan Mangad, R.V.G. Menon, Alankode Leelakrishnan, Kaleeswaram Raj and M.R. Thampan. Alleging institutional capture and demanding measures to restore the integrity of the electoral process, economist Parakala Prabhakar, who joined the protest, called for the scrapping of the SIR and the reconstitution of the Election Commission of India (ECI). Wherever dissent is expressed and wherever we register our objection to SIR, anywhere in the country, in any village, town, lane or street, that is our Jantar Mantar. 785a4a28291d1789.title: BJP discusses preparations for MLC, GHMC elections
785a4a28291d1789.summary: Updated - October 24, 2026 09:17 pm IST - HYDERABAD State BJP president N. Ramchander Rao, national general secretary Sunil Bansal and other party leaders at a meeting in Hyderabad on Saturday. | Photo Credit: G RAMAKRISHNA The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has discussed preparations for the upcoming Graduates’ MLC elections and Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC) elections at a meeting of its State leaders and office-bearers here on Saturday. The meeting, chaired by State BJP president N. Ramachander Rao at the party’s State office, reviewed the prevailing political situation in Telangana and discussed the party’s organisational activities in nine districts falling within the GHMC limits. Party leaders outlined strategies to secure victory in the Graduates’ MLC elections and called upon cadres to mobilise workers at the booth level and intensify public outreach. The meeting also discussed the BJP’s ‘Loktantra Bachao – Bheedtantra Hatao’ (Save Democracy – Remove Mobocracy) campaign against what the party described as actions undermining democratic values. It was decided to intensify grassroots-level protests against the Congress government’s policies in Telangana. BJP State in-charge Sunil Bansal, co-in-charge Abhay Patil, State organisational general secretary N. Madhukar, State joint organisational general secretary Dashrath, MPs, MLAs, MLCs and presidents of the nine district units attended the meeting. Rekha Sharma was also present. dca4cf39d8031b80.title: Prakasam Collector calls for utmost vigilance in handling polling materials
dca4cf39d8031b80.summary: Published - October 24, 2026 09:12 pm IST - ONGOLE Prakasam District Collector P. Raja Babu and Joint Collector Kalpana Kumari inspect ballot boxes ahead of the Municipal Corporation elections on Saturday. | Photo Credit: KOMMURI SRINIVAS As the State gears up for the local body elections, Prakasam District Collector P. Raja Babu has emphasised the need for utmost vigilance in handling polling materials and in making arrangements for the counting process to ensure that no lapses occur. The Collector, along with Joint Collector Kalpana Kumari, inspected the ballot boxes at RISE Engineering College on the outskirts of Ongole on Saturday. Officials have set up facilities for the distribution and reception of election materials, as well as strong rooms and a counting centre for the local body elections, within the college premises. At the centre, the Collector inspected how the 101 statutory and non-statutory items of equipment required for the elections were being maintained. He instructed the officials to prepare the equipment required for the 224 polling stations in the Municipal Corporation limits. He also inspected the manner in which the barricades were prepared and the necessary arrangements made as per the rules of the Election Commission. 681662735aec5502.title: Sichuan to meet Denso Iris in the final of FIBA-Women’s Basketball League Asia tournament
681662735aec5502.summary: Updated - October 24, 2026 09:13 pm IST - BENGALURU By experience and pedigree, American Chennedy Carter towers above everyone else in the FIBA-Women’s Basketball League Asia. A former WNBA player and the only one in the tournament, the 27-year-old has been one of the top scorers for Sichuan Yuanda Meile (China) in the league at the Sree Kanteerava Indoor Stadium here. Against KB Stars in the semifinals on Saturday, Carter appeared to play every role, switching between guard, shooting guard and even power forward. Carter (31 points), ably supported by Australia’s Sara Blicavs (22) and captain Song Gao (21), powered Sichuan to a 93-74 win over KB Stars, taking the Chinese side into its second final in three WBLA editions—it last won the title in the inaugural edition in 2024. Carter also made her presence felt on the boards, collecting five rebounds and dishing out five assists. Denso Iris (Japan) faced a stiff challenge from Cathay Life Tigers (Chinese Taipei) before emerging triumphant 86-78 in the other semifinal to set up a final against Sichuan on Sunday. Maki Takada, the 37-year-old Olympic medallist and centre, starred for Iris, finishing as its top-scorer with 20 points. Earlier, Indian Railways suffered its third successive defeat to finish sixth and last in the tournament, losing to Akari Sparks (Philippines) 86-56. The results: semifinals: Sichuan Yuanda Meile (China) 93 (Chennedy Carter 31, Sara Blicavs 22, Song Gao 22) bt KB Stars 74 (Yunjeong Na 22, Yunha Song 15, Yaeun Heo 15). Denso Iris 86 (Maki Takada 20, Sokhna Sylla 12, Haruna Kasagi 12, Mnami Yabu 10) bt Cathay Life Tigers 78 (Penina Davidson 30, Shelby Cheyanne Cheslek 14). 5th-6th place match: Akari Sparks 86 (Bre’Amber Shakira Scott 25, Saicha Patricia Grant-Allen 24) bt Indian Railways 56 (Pushpa Senthil Kumar 13, Harima Sundhari Munishkannan 13). b6af02c1ad349ac0.title: Iran president says many struggling for food as war bites
b6af02c1ad349ac0.summary: Updated - October 24, 2026 09:29 pm IST - Tehran Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian attends the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) summit in Turkmenbasy, Turkmenistan. File | Photo Credit: AP Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said on Saturday (October 24, 2026) that many Iranians were struggling to put food on the table, as the economic pressure from the Middle East war with the United States mounts. Washington has in recent weeks dialled back military operations in favour of economic pressure, while Iran's leaders have said peace negotiations will only succeed without pressure and threats from Washington as the conflict remains locked in a stalemate. "There are many people in this society who are struggling to put food on the table because of the war we have found ourselves in, because of the wartime conditions we are living under," Mr. Pezeshkian said in a speech shared on his website. The war began on February 28 when the United States and Israel attacked Iran, killing supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and senior military commanders. eec99c39dbf4cedc.title: Coimbatore NXT pitches for major railway infrastructure push in its meeting with Southern Railway GM
eec99c39dbf4cedc.summary: Published - October 24, 2026 09:33 pm IST - COIMBATORE A delegation of Coimbatore NXT, Railway Task Force, at its high-level meeting here with the General Manager of Southern Railway U. Subba Rao and the Divisional Railway Manager, Salem Division, Panna Lal, on Friday, sought urgent improvements in railway infrastructure, additional train services, enhanced passenger amenities and better suburban connectivity across Coimbatore. Led by Vanitha Mohan, vice-chairman, Kongu Global Forum, the delegates, including Dorairaj, president, Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industry; Naushad, chairman, CII, Coimbatore Zone; Balasubramanian, president, Residents’ Awareness Association of Coimbatore (RAAC); and Dileep who represented the Customs Brokers and Shipping Agents Association, strongly emphasised that the development of Coimbatore Junction, a major revenue-generating railway station in Southern Railway, has been long overdue and must receive immediate attention. The major demands constituted operating Coimbatore–Chennai Vande Bharat Express with more coaches to meet growing passenger demand; introduction of Coimbatore–Tiruvananthapuram Vande Bharat Express; restoration of direct train connectivity to the southern districts of Tamil Nadu that were in place during the metre-gauge era; and rerouting of trains currently bypassing Coimbatore Junction. The delegates also called for upgrade of Coimbatore Junction with additional infrastructure, improved passenger amenities and facilities for simultaneous train operations; expediting the development of Coimbatore South - Podanur Junction; establishing additional island platforms at Coimbatore North Junction and according it a status of terminus; and improvements to platforms and passenger amenities at Irugur, Singanallur, Kinathukadavu, Peelamedu and other suburban stations. They mooted strengthening of circular suburban railway connectivity from Coimbatore to Tiruppur , Pollachi and Palakkad to serve Coimbatore’s growing metropoli

01f26b4112395f20.title: Minister inaugurates bus stand in Chekkanurani
01f26b4112395f20.summary: Published - October 24, 2026 09:45 pm IST - MADURAI Minister for Energy Resources and Law C.T.R. Nirmal Kumar inaugurating the new bus stand at Chekkanurani in Madurai on Saturday. Minister for Energy and Law C.T.R. Nirmal Kumar here on Saturday inaugurated the newly constructed bus terminus built at a cost of ₹8.50 crore under the Integrated Assigned Revenue Scheme in Chekkanurani in Tirumangalam Panchayat Union. Facilities established in the bus terminus included seven bus bays, 27 commercial shops, two restaurants, two waiting rooms for men, two waiting rooms for women and nursing mothers, a transport office, a police office, restroom facilities for both men and women, and 21 vegetable market stalls. Speaking there, he said, as the bus stand work was lagging behind, the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam government expedited the works and completed the works earlier. “Chekkanurani bus stand which connects the nearby villages is very important for the farmers and villagers around. It serves as a hub for the nearby regions,” he added. Recognising the importance of the Usilampatti bus stand, the government has directed the officials to fasten the works carried out there. “Further, we have also heard from the public about further upgradations required in the Chekkanurani bus stand and it will be taken to the Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay for approval,” he noted. Regarding the works carried out in Madurai for upcoming rains, he said, all works which were stagnated for over five years in the previous government have all been kicked off. “In Sellur following an inspection we have ordered the pipe laying works to be expedited and it is expected to be completed in the next five days. Along with this, many other works are also being carried out,” he said. 004a4e33dd48a7c6.title: ISRO Space on Wheels comes to Dindigul Book Festival
004a4e33dd48a7c6.summary: Published - October 24, 2026 09:33 pm IST - DINDIGUL Students at the ISRO Space on Wheels bus at the book exhibition held in Dindigul on Saturday. | Photo Credit: KARTHIKEYAN G Indian Space Research Organisation’s (ISRO) Space on Wheels mobile exhibition bus was stationed on Saturday at the Dindigul Book Festival currently under way on the Anguvilas Higher Secondary School grounds. The main objective was to raise awareness about space science and technology among the public, particularly students. Dindigul Collector Durgamoorthi inaugurated the event. She urged the public, particularly the students to visit the exhibition bus and learn about the key features. The exhibition featured the scale models of India’s premier launch vehicles and missions. The exhibition bus is stationed at the venue for the weekend. The Collector urged the public to attend the book festival and make it a grand success. Apart from the cultural programmes, world cinema was also being screened as part of the festival. A donation box has been placed on the premises for interested people to donate books. A total of 126 book stalls have been set up for this edition of the book festival. Last year’s book festival turned out to be a success with books worth ₹3 crore sold at the event. A total of 126 book stalls were set up last year. A total of 1,02,723 people attended the book festival and 66 people donated 1,157 books. Subsequently, the donated books were given to government schools and libraries. The book festival is jointly organised by the Dindigul district administration, the Directorate of Public Libraries and the Dindigul Ilakkiya Kalam. Adequate arrangements have been made for the smooth conduct of the event. d73cebf1fb6380b7.title: Siruthuli requests Railways to rename Coimbatore-Chennai Superfast Express as ‘Noyyal Express’.
d73cebf1fb6380b7.summary: Updated - October 24, 2026 09:40 pm IST - COIMBATORE Siruthuli, the Coimbatore-based environmental organisation working on water conservation and afforestation, has requested the Southern Railway to rename Train No. 12680 Coimbatore-MGR Chennai Superfast Express as ‘Noyyal Express’. In a representation to Southern Railway General Manager U. Subba Rao, on Friday, managing trustee of Siruthuli Vanitha Mohan said the Noyyal river originating in the Velliangiri Hills of the Western Ghats and flowing to a length of 160 km before joining the Cauvery river was integral to the historic development of Kongu region encompassing Coimbatore, Tiruppur, Erode and Karur districts. The Noyyal river, with its network of streams and irrigation channels sustained agriculture, supported livelihoods, and shaped the region’s cultural heritage. The Indian Railways has recognised the cultural and geographical significance of rivers and natural landmarks through the names of several trains: Vaigai Express, Cauvery Express, and Pothigai Express. Renaming Train No. 12680 Coimbatore-MGR Chennai Superfast Express as ‘Noyyal Express’ will be a meaningful tribute to the Noyyal river and the legacy, and would inspire future generations to protect the invaluable natural resource, Ms. Vanitha Mohan said. In another representation, Siruthuli while thanking the Railways for permitting planting of 62,800 trees on railway lands in and around Coimbatore since 2012, sought consent for extending the afforestation activities, under its Green Guard initiative, to raise 1.62 lakh trees in the open spaces to a cumulative extent of 46.4 acres in Singanallur railway station, Nallampalayam, Kavundampalayam, Podanur, Karamadai railway station, and Coimbatore Railway Station. 28630bd49731fc82.title: Sri Lankan Navy seizes two Indian boats in beedi leaves smuggling bid
28630bd49731fc82.summary: Published - October 24, 2026 09:29 pm IST - THOOTHUKUDI Sri Lankan Navy and the Coast Guard seized two Indian fibre boats and two Sri Lankan local dinghies on Wednesday (October 21) off the coast of Udappuwa, Puttalam while attempting to smuggle a consignment of beedi leaves. According to Sri Lankan Navy’s website, a total of 11 suspects, Indian and Sri Lankan nationals were also apprehended. The interception was made after having spotted two suspicious Indian fibre boats that had entered the Sri Lankan waters, along with two local dinghies. Upon searching the boats, naval and coast guard personnel recovered about 2,400 kg of beedi leaves packed into 60 sacks. Seven Indian nationals aboard the fibre boats and four Sri Lankan suspects on the dinghies were taken into custody in this operation. The suspects, seized boats and beedi leaves were handed over to the customs preventive office for further legal proceedings. 2490f901117886d9.title: SHG members, students participate in nutrition awareness programme at PU
2490f901117886d9.summary: Updated - October 24, 2026 09:23 pm IST - PUDUCHERRY A Nutrition Assessment Camp was held recently at the Pondicherry University as part of the celebrations to mark National Nutrition month and World Food Day 2026. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT Members of self-help groups, community representatives and students participated in a Nutrition Assessment Camp held as part of the celebrations to mark National Nutrition month and World Food Day 2026, at the Pondicherry University recently. Vice-Chancellor P. Prakash Babu inaugurated the programme aimed at spreading awareness on nutrition. The camp, organised by the Department of Food Science and Technology of the university, had on display many value-added food products, including micro-greens, millet-based premixes, minor millet cookies, organic vegetables, honey, edible oils and other locally-produced foods, the University said in a release. The camp provided BMI assessment, blood pressure reading, haemoglobin analysis and random blood glucose testing. In addition, dietary and lifestyle counselling, along with personalised nutrition guidance was provided to the participants to help adopt healthier food habits and improved lifestyle practices, the release added. The event was an opportunity for community groups to popularise their value-added products and promote sustainable food practices, the release said. a598a27a9389ba22.title: Guntur doctor presents research at neurosurgeons’ meet in London
a598a27a9389ba22.summary: Published - October 24, 2026 09:27 pm IST - GUNTUR Dr. Mohana Rao Patibandla, founder and chief neurosurgeon of Dr. Rao’s Hospital, participating in the Society of British Neurological Surgeons centenary meeting in London. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Dr. Mohana Rao Patibandla, founder and chief neurosurgeon of Dr. Rao’s Hospital–International Institute of Neurosciences (IIN), Guntur, presented research on complex craniovertebral junction surgery at the Society of British Neurological Surgeons (SBNS) centenary meeting in London. In a statement on Saturday, Dr. Patibandla said the international scientific meeting was held from October 12 to 16, bringing together neurosurgical experts to discuss advancements in neurological care and surgical techniques. His presentation, titled “Transnasal Endoscopic Odontoidectomy for Failed Posterior Craniovertebral Fusion: Salvage Decompression and Outcomes in 6 Complex Cases,” examined a minimally invasive approach for patients experiencing persistent compression despite previous posterior stabilisation surgery. The craniovertebral junction connects the skull to the upper cervical spine. Compression in this region can threaten brainstem and spinal cord functions. The endoscopic technique enables surgeons to access the odontoid process through the nasal passages to relieve pressure from the front. The research analysed six complex cases, highlighting the importance of individualised surgical planning, careful assessment and evaluation of neurological outcomes. The findings contribute to international discussions on minimally invasive neurosurgery and complex spinal disorders, he added. bbb5f9d88d72b508.title: IRDAI extends distribution reforms feedback timeline to Oct 31
bbb5f9d88d72b508.summary: Published - October 24, 2026 09:50 pm IST - HYDERABAD The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) has extended the last date for submission of comments on its consultation paper on distribution reforms till October 31. The consultation process has received an encouraging response, with over 650 comments received thus far. In view of the significant interest and to facilitate wider participation, the last date for stakeholders and the public to submit feedback and suggestions is being extended, the regulator said on Saturday. Placing its two-part consultation paper on the proposed distribution reforms titled ‘Recalibrating Economics of Insurance Distribution’ in public domain on September 23rd, IRDAI had set October 25 as the deadline. Desirous stakeholders and members of the public are encouraged to utilise the extended timeline and submit their comments and suggestions. The feedback received will help inform the further examination and refinement of the proposed reforms. All other details and terms of the consultation paper remain unchanged, IRDAI said. The insurance regulator is proposing a major overhaul of norms governing insurance distribution, commissions and expenses. It said the objective is to foster a more efficient and inclusive insurance distribution ecosystem. e660a98a5348b5f4.title: Dominant India aims to seal ODI series against Zimbabwe
e660a98a5348b5f4.summary: Updated - October 24, 2026 09:52 pm IST - VADODARA Skipper Smriti Mandhana will be happy with Pratika’s form. The sun will rise in the east. A day has 24 hours. India will beat Zimbabwe. Some certainties are written into the fabric of the universe. This one comes stamped with a scoreboard. None of this is meant as a disrespect. Even the visitor speaks of an upset as a miracle: improbable, yet gloriously welcome should it arrive. But miracles demand fresh legs, and Zimbabwe’s are running on fumes. They come into the second ODI at the BCA Stadium in Kotambi on Sunday carrying the bruises of a nine-wicket loss and the weight of a calendar that has given them little mercy. The Lady Chevrons have been the busiest side in international cricket recently, playing non-stop since September. Niggles have crept up, with Josephine Nkomo and Kelis Ndhlovu missing the 1st ODI. Recovery has been a challenge, with the priority for the camp being the ICC Emerging Nations Trophy, which gets underway in Bangkok in November. India, meanwhile, eyes an unassailable lead but isn’t without its own headaches. The pacers were erratic in the 1st ODI. Nandani Sharma, who made way for debutant Jintimani Kalita, was spotted doing her routines with her left knee in a compression brace. But the bigger issues are the wayward lines India settled into after the PowerPlay and an inability to bowl to set fields, which Zimbabwe smartly capitalised on. Will India be brave and give wicketkeeper Richa Ghosh, whose errors have been piling up, a rest to allow Baroda girl Yastika Bhatia, who graces several billboards around the venue, a spot in the side? Or is there room for both, the way India has managed to embrace Shafali Verma and Pratika Rawal? Coach Amol Muzumdar and captain Smriti Mandhana must weigh rotating players to build depth for the South Africa tour or stick with a winning lineup. Published - October 24, 2026 08:55 pm IST - MYSURU Pramoda Devi Wadiyar of the erstwhile Mysuru royal family speaking to reporters in Mysuru on Saturday. | Photo Credit: M.A. Sriram Pramoda Devi Wadiyar of the erstwhile royal family of Mysuru has said she will issue a statement shortly on the circumstances that led to the cancellation of the traditional Vajra Mushti Kalaga during the Vijayadashami celebrations at the Mysuru palace on Wednesday. Responding to reporters’ queries in Mysuru, Ms. Wadiyar said she was yet to gather complete information about the developments that led to the cancellation of the historic martial tradition. Vajra Mushti Kalaga, an ancient form of martial combat in which wrestlers strike each other on their shaved heads with knuckle-dusters, has traditionally been held ahead of the erstwhile royal family’s private procession on Vijayadashami. The event was, however, cancelled this year after wrestlers alleged that the police had prevented some of them from entering the Mysuru palace premises in time to participate. Meanwhile, Ms. Wadiyar, however, expressed satisfaction over elephant Prashanta successfully carrying the golden howdah and ensuring the smooth completion of the Jamboo Savari. She admitted that she had been anxious about Prashanta carrying the golden howdah. It may be mentioned that it was 54-year-old male elephant Prashanta’s first time performing the task following the retirement of his predecessor, Abhimanyu, upon attaining the age of 60. Published - October 24, 2026 08:56 pm IST - PALAKKAD The Palakkad chapter of the Victims Information, Sensitisation, Welfare and Assistance Society (VISWAS) India will conduct a district-level children’s parliament competition for Class XI and XII students here on November 9. The event will be held in association with the State Bank of India (SBI) as part of the State government’s anti-drug campaign Operation Toofan. The competition will focus on drug use among students. Schools must conduct preliminary rounds and nominate the first prize winner for the district-level final. Students can choose from six topics covering drug prevention, awareness, youth responsibility and the need to protect students from substance abuse. Schools must email the details of their winning students to viswaspkd.programs@gmail.com before November 3, 2026. The final will be held at the Collectorate conference hall at Civil Station here. District Collector Sudheer K. will preside over the function. MLAs and senior police and excise officials will attend. Minister for General Education N. Samsudheen will be the chief guest. The first, second and third-place winners will receive mementoes and certificates. Five students will receive consolation prizes, and all participants will get certificates. For details, contact P. Premnath (9447137244), Rakhi N. (9747010826) or M. Devadasan (9971048234). Updated - October 24, 2026 09:00 pm IST - AMALAPURAM The Konaseema Centre for Migration (KCM) is gearing up to launch a village-level campaign against fake recruitment agents and agencies in Dr. B. R. Ambedkar Konaseema district to prevent locals from being stranded in the Gulf region. The local agents are allegedly active in recruiting people—mostly women—for employment in the Gulf region, where victims are reportedly subjected to physical harassment, assigned work beyond their physical capacities, and stranded without employment. KCM manager Golla Ramesh stated that 284 people stranded in the Gulf region had been repatriated and 128 grievances pertaining to fake agents and agencies are being redressed. In a review meeting with the officials concerned, District Revenue Officer Veerla Subbarao directed the revenue, police, and other officials to launch a campaign against fake agents and agencies and create awareness on the employment opportunities and recruitment procedures. Ravi Prakash held a meeting with representatives of six recognised political parties in Puducherry on Saturday. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT Chief Electoral Officer A.S.P.S. Ravi Prakash held a meeting with representatives of six recognised political parties in Puducherry to brief them on the Special Summary Revision (SSR) exercise being undertaken in the Union Territory. The Election Commission of India has directed the Election Department to undertake the SSR of the photo electoral roll in the Union Territory. The representatives of political parties were informed about the procedural aspects involved in the conduct of the SSR. The instructions given by the ECI were passed on to the representatives of political parties at the meeting held on Friday. Published - October 24, 2026 08:33 pm IST - KOTTAYAM Aroma Chundan, rowed by the Aroma Boat Club, crosses the finish line in the final of the Thazhathangady Boat Race, part of the Champions Boat League, in Kottayam on Saturday. | Photo Credit: VISHNU PRATHAP Aroma Chundan, rowed by the Aroma Boat Club of Paravur in Kollam, raced to victory in the Thazhathangady Boat Race, the Kottayam leg of the Champions Boat League (CBL). Aroma Chundan crossed the finish line in 3 minutes and 21.227 seconds to win the title. Melpadam Chundan, rowed by Pallathuruthy Boat Club, finished second in 3 minutes and 21.802 seconds, followed by Niranam Chundan of Niranam Boat Club in 3 minutes and 21.925 seconds. Veeyapuram, Cheruthana, Arppookara, Punyalan Niranam, Nadubhagam and Thalavady finished fourth to ninth, respectively. In the smaller boat categories, Puthenparambil won in the Iruttukuthi B-grade event, Champion clinched the Veppu B-grade title, Moozhi won in the Churulan category and Munnuthaikkal emerged victorious in the Iruttukuthi A-grade event. Aroma Boat Club will receive ₹5 lakh in prize money for the victory, while Pallathuruthy Boat Club and Niranam Boat Club will receive ₹3 lakh and ₹1 lakh, respectively, for finishing second and third. District Police Chief K.M. Sabu Mathew distributed the prizes at the valedictory function. Earlier in the day, Assembly Speaker Thiruvanchoor Radhakrishnan inaugurated the race at a function presided over by Water Resources and Housing Minister Mons Joseph. .Speaking on the occasion, Mr. Joseph said the Speaker had submitted a proposal for constructing a permanent pavilion for the Thazhathangady boat race. 5e12ef738de05c4e.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Need help with your subscription? Updated - October 24, 2026 08:41 pm IST - TIRUVARUR: Compensation under the the Prime Minister’s crop insurance scheme has been released to farmers who were not able to take up sowing during the kuruvai season in 2026-27 in Tiruvarur district. According to an official release, the Centre has announced that a sum of ₹77.70 crore would be distributed as compensation to farmers in 159 hamlets in Tiruvarur district under the ‘prevented sowing’ clause of the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY). While a sum of ₹12.05 crore would be disbursed to 4,868 farmers in the first phase on October 24, it would be distributed to others in subsequent phases. The amount would be credited directly into the accounts of the beneficiaries. Kuruvai coverage in Tiruvarur district stood at 77,573 hectares last year and dropped by 31,235 hectares this year, the release added. According to an official release, the Centre has announced that a sum of ₹77.70 crore would be distributed as compensation to farmers in 159 hamlets in Tiruvarur district under the ‘prevented sowing’ clause of the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY). MOORTHY The Tamil Nadu Government Aided College Non-Teaching Staff Association organised a seminar here on Saturday in memory of its late president R. Stephenraj. R. Murali, former Principal of The Madura College, who spoke on ‘Changing directions of Higher Education in Tamil Nadu,’ warned that Tamil Nadu’s higher education sector was facing several crises, and the government appeared to be facilitating the expansion of private and foreign universities instead of strengthening public universities and government colleges. Asserting that education is not merely a means of obtaining employment, he described it as a vital public resource that fosters independent thinking, scientific temper, social justice, human rights awareness, and democratic values. Updated - October 24, 2026 08:40 pm IST Preetham R is one of the youngest to be exhibiting his collection. Three years ago, Preetham R stumbled upon a small box stacked with coins in the almirah and fell in love with it. “Although my father had shown me his collection when I was much younger, it was in college that I took a liking to coins,” says the 22-year-old who completed his B.Com. He is one of the youngest who is participating in the three-day coin exhibition conducted by Chennai Coin Club that concludes on October 25. More than 50 numismatics from different states are taking part in this event, and Preetham’s short journey with coins shows that it is never too late to start a hobby. “I started segregating the coins in the box into different types and researching them to develop more interest,” says the resident of Ayanavaram. A one-rupee copper coin was one of his first that he brought home on his own. Today, the youngster has a collection of 1,000 coins, with those minted from 1950 onwards being his specialisation. At the ongoing exhibition, besides selling some of his coins, he hopes to buy some rare ones to add to his collection. For those keen on starting coin collection as a hobby now, he says, it is not just a knowledgeable and a learning experience but a good investment option. Organisers of the Chennai Coin Club exhibition say the three-day event is aimed at raising awareness about counterfeit currency and fake coins that are increasingly doing the rounds. All the participants at the exhibition are experienced numismatics who are showcasing their best collection and share their knowledge. Besides antique coins, historical banknotes and vintage stamps will be showcased. The event will serve as a platform to buy, sell and exchange currencies and coins. Updated - October 24, 2026 08:52 pm IST - TIRUCHI The condition of several roads in Tiruchi has turned from bad to worse after the recent spell of rain. | Photo Credit: M. MOORTHY The wet spell over the past few days has battered many key roads in the city, causing hardship to commuters and motorists. Since the onset of the Northeast monsoon on October 15, Tiruchi has been receiving rainfall. The showers were light until Thursday. However, heavy rain lashed different parts of the city on Friday, and the incessant rainfall has left arterial roads and interior lanes damaged. Uneven road surface and potholes have become a common sight on major stretches, with the top layer eroded at many places. The damaged patches have led to frequent skidding incidents, particularly affecting two-wheeler riders. The roads in Anna Nagar, Karur bypass, Old Madurai Road, West Boulevard Road, Major Saravanan Road and important stretches around Central Bus Stand such as Rockins Road, McDonalds Road, VOC Road, and Williams Road have suffered significant deterioration. Similarly, stretches around Chathiram Bus Stand have also been damaged. Similar issues have cropped up around Gandhi Market, Palakarai, Varaganeri and other areas. With movement of heavy vehicles continuing through the roads, the loose surface material has begun to dislodge, worsening driving conditions. Recently patched up roads too have suffered damage. Motorists say the situation has grown increasingly unsafe, especially during the night. “We encounter many deep potholes and eroded stretches on the roads. They test the patience of motorists. We need to navigate carefully,” says R. Thiruvengadam, a social activist. Published - October 24, 2026 08:39 pm IST - Thiruvananthapuram Vaisakh Chandran. | Photo Credit: File Photo The last two seasons were forgettable for off-spinner Vaisakh Chandran. A finger injury, followed by a shoulder injury, sidelined him. In between, he lost his bowling action and, consequently, his wicket-taking ability. The Ranji Trophy match against Karnataka at the KCA Stadium in Mangalapuram last season was particularly chastening; he was savaged by Karun Nair and R. Smaran, conceding over 100 runs at nearly five runs an over. His shoulder injury then flared up, forcing him to spend the rest of the season in rehabilitation. “I knew something was wrong but I was helpless. I was just going through the motions in the match against Karnataka. The shoulder was hurting as well. I felt a sharp pain on my right shoulder whenever I threw the ball while fielding. I think I over-bowled in the nets. I was told to bowl 30 overs daily during practice by our former coach and I followed it. The pain worsened, forcing me to consult a doctor who advised rest,” During his rehabilitation, he watched the video of the Karnataka match and compared them with old footage and realised his bowling action had changed drastically. “I went back to the drawing board, worked on my action. I also sought the help of Biju George, who pointed out the flaws and helped me to correct them,” he said. “It is a common problem for all bowlers to lose their original action when they play a lot. Every bowler has a specific arm slot from which he delivers the ball comfortably. In Vaisakh’s case his release point and arm path were different from his earlier action. I made slight adjustments to his loading and recoil and things fell into place,” Biju.explained. I was just going through the motions in the match against Karnataka. The shoulder was hurting as well. I felt a sharp pain on my right shoulder whenever I threw the ball while fielding. I think I over-bowled in the nets. I was told to bowl 30 overs daily during practice by our former coach and I followed it. The pain worsened, forcing me to consult a doctor who advised rest,” During his rehabilitation, he watched the video of the Karnataka match and compared them with old footage and realised his bowling action had changed drastically. “I went back to the drawing board, worked on my action. I also sought the help of Biju George, who pointed out the flaws and helped me to correct them,” he said. “It is a common problem for all bowlers to lose their original action when they play a lot. Every bowler has a specific arm slot from which he delivers the ball comfortably. In Vaisakh’s case his release point and arm path were different from his earlier action. I made slight adjustments to his loading and recoil and things fell into place,” Biju.explained. Published - October 24, 2026 08:31 pm IST - HUBBALLI The special drive against use of manja launched by the Hubballi Dharwad Police Commissionerate continued on Saturday. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT The special drive against use of manja launched by the Hubballi Dharwad Police Commissionerate continued on Saturday with more cases being booked taking the total number of cases booked to 16. A day after a 38-year old woman was killed after manja (abrasive kite string) slit her throat in Hubballi, the Police Commissionerate had launched the special drive on Friday. According to the Hubballi Dharwad Police Commissioner, during the special drive, 124 places were inspected and 69 locations where manja was being used were checked. The police had so far removed dangerously hanging manja strings at 63 locations and checked 67 shops where manja was being reportedly sold. While 11 cases including those against sellers, users, and also a parent for allowing a kid to use the abrasive string to fly kite were booked on Friday, five more cases were booked in Bendigeri, Old Hubballi, APMC Navanagar, and Kasabapet police stations on Saturday. On Thursday, lab technician Vidya Manjunath Goudar was killed after the abrasive kite string got entangled around her neck, slitting her throat, while she was riding a two-wheeler. The incident led to backlash and various leaders, including Pralhad Joshi, Basavaraj Horatti, Prasad Abbayya and others, calling for strict action against the sale and use of manja. 555d80f878d4d30a.title: Anniversary of Mysore Chalo observed in city
555d80f878d4d30a.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Need help with your subscription? Updated - October 24, 2026 08:28 pm IST - MYSURU The Mysore Chalo movement, which began on September 1, 1947, played a significant role in the freedom of the Princely State of Mysuru. | Photo Credit: M.A. Sriram The Mysuru District and City Freedom Fighters’ Association commemorated the 80th anniversary of the Mysore Chalo movement at the Freedom Fighters’ Park in Subbarayana Kere on Saturday. Members of the Freedom Fighters’ Association garlanded the statue of Mahatma Gandhi at 10.30 a.m. They later took out a march to Ramaswamy Circle and paid a floral tribute at the memorial of Ramaswamy, who sacrificed his life on September 13, 1947, for the freedom of Mysuru. The Mysore Chalo movement, which began on September 1, 1947, played a significant role in the freedom of the Princely State of Mysuru. While India attained Independence on August 15, 1947, Mysuru hoisted the national flag for the first time on October 24, 1947, marking the beginning of the Independence era. While speaking on the occasion, Yogananda, Working president of the Freedom Fighters’ Association, said, “On October 24, 1947, Jayachamarajendra Wadiyar, the then ruler of the Mysuru State, announced the merger of the Princely State into the Indian Union and declared Independence.” Association Secretary Ravi, Pandith Aradya and others were present on the occasion. Published - October 24, 2026 08:24 pm IST - SIVAGANGA RAMANATHAPURAM: TAMIL NADU: 24 October 2026: Tamil Nadu Ministers paying floral tributes at Maruthu Pandiyar brothers memorial in Tirupattur in Sivaganga district on Saturday. Photo: handout_e_mail / The Hindu. | Photo Credit: HANDOUT_E_MAIL Marking the 225th death anniversary of Maruthu Pandiyar brothers, leaders from various political parties garlanded the statues at the manimandapam in Tirupattur in Sivaganga district on Saturday. The memorial day of the Maruthu Pandiyar brothers was observed as a government event at the manimandapam in Tirupattur, Sivaganga district. District Collector P. Akash hoisted the national flag and garlanded the statues of the Maruthu brothers. District Superintendent of Police Abhishek Gupta, District Revenue Officer Sailendran, and others participated. Minister for Energy Resources and Law C. T. R. Nirmal Kumar, Minister for Natural Resources T. K. Prabhu, Minister for Labour Welfare and Skill Development J. Mohamed Farvas and Minister for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises P. Mathan Raja, paid their respects at the venue. On behalf of DMK, former ministers K. R. Periyakaruppan, R. S. Rajakannappan, T. R. B. Rajaa, MLA Muthuraja, former MLA Tamilarasi, and Town Panchayat President Sengaimaran paid their respects. On behalf of AIADMK, former ministers Dindigul C. Srinivasan, Sellur K. Raju, Gokula Indira, Kamaraj, Manikandan, and former MLAs Rajan Chellappa and Senthilnathan paid their respects. MDMK General Secretary Vaiko, AMMK General Secretary T.T.V. Dhinakaran, BJP District Secretary Pandithurai, Congress National Secretary Mayura Jayakumar, former MLAs Mangudi, among others paid their respects. CPI(M) District Secretary Mohan, Communist Party of India former MLA Gunasekaran, also paid their respects. Published - October 24, 2026 08:24 pm IST

During the the review meeting, Mr. Nanduri said that with the onset of monsoon and widespread rainfall in the district, the district administration has taken immediate precautionary measures to tackle the situation of heavy rain and flooding. More than 5,466 volunteers are ready to assist in rescue operations, he noted. Mr. Nanduri further said that seven relief centres had been kept ready to provide safe shelter to people in the event of heavy rain. Similarly, buildings such as schools and marriage halls had also been identified and kept ready to set up as relief centres, depending on the situation. He also emphasised the need to create awareness among farmers about precautionary measures to protect crops from damage caused by heavy rains. Published - October 24, 2026 08:29 pm IST - Hyderabad Information and Public Relations Minister Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy made it clear that the government would soon give details of the house sites to be allotted to journalists, as promised earlier. In a statement here, he said the modalities were discussed with Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy during his New Delhi visit and the job of identifying the land and giving a blue print was entrusted to a senior officer, who is on the job. Mr. Reddy said that the government was committed to fulfilling the long-pending demand of journalists for house sites and is working towards a permanent solution that will ensure allotments are free from legal complications. Published - October 24, 2026 08:27 pm IST - COIMBATORE The Health Department has confirmed the death of a four-year-old boy from Tiruppur district due to dengue. The child, identified as Tamil from Kungumapalayam village in Palladam Block, was diagnosed with Dengue Shock Syndrome combined with sepsis and Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC), at the Coimbatore Medical College Hospital, where he was referred to by a private clinic. In a press release, Hospital Dean M. Geethanjali said that since the child was admitted with after-effects of two epileptic attacks and low blood-pressure, normal saline bolus, and noradrenaline adrenaline were administered. There was respiratory failure and the child was kept in life-support. Though attempts were made to normalise blood pressure, the child suffered circulatory failure, and despite administering blood products and resuscitative efforts, the child died of cardiac arrest on Friday night, the press release said.
