a30320a748957285.title: HYDRAA operation unearths illegal extraction of water from Sunnam Cheruvu
a30320a748957285.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Need help with your subscription? Updated - October 24, 2026 08:20 pm IST - HYDERABAD Pipelines dropped into Sunnam Cheruvu. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement The Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Protection Agency (HYDRAA) has unearthed several establishments drawing water illegally from Sunnam Cheruvu, Madhapur. In a major operation on Saturday (October 24, 2026), HYDRAA forces removed dozens of pipelines discreetly laid into the lake from several buildings at Borabanda Phase-3 and Navbharat Nagar areas. The large hoses were attached to pump sets in the residential buildings on the other end, and buried under the earth outside to avoid detection. The houses raided revealed massive bore-wells drilled in bedrooms and kitchen areas, a statement from HYDRAA said. Photos and videos shared by the agency showed water sumps and bore-wells dug up beneath cots. Using heavy machinery, HYDRAA forces excavated the pipelines and traced them back to their source points. The operation which began at 6.30 a.m. continued up to evening, with officials removing 15 bore-wells, and unearthing a large number of pipes laid into the lakes. The statement said HYDRAA acted upon complaints from local residents about depleting ground water reserves due to unlawful extraction of water from the lake for supplying to hotels and hostels in Madhapur. The two-day high-level fact-finding mission, scheduled for Monday and Tuesday, October 26 and 27, will be jointly led by former Solapur Commissioner Harish Mangalal Baijal, IPS, and retired Karnataka Forest Service officer Raju, a former IFS officer. Representatives of several human rights organisations will be part of the mission. In a press statement, People’s Watch executive director Henri Tiphagne said three farmers were killed, and another person was injured in the shooting involving Karnataka Forest Department personnel. Identifying the deceased as Anthony Sami, John Rose Peter and Kumar, alias Savariyappan, the statement said the fourth person, Mahimai Das, was reportedly injured and subsequently taken to a hospital. The Forest Department has reportedly maintained that the four men had illegally entered the forest to hunt wildlife and were carrying weapons. According to the department’s account, the men had attempted to fire at forest personnel, who returned fire in self-defence. They maintained that the men were farmers who entered the forest in connection with their livestock, not to hunt wildlife, the statement said. The spirit of Telangana didn’t just travel to Michigan, it bloomed there. The Global Telangana Association (GTA) Detroit Chapter hosted its fourth Bathukamma & Dasara celebrations at the Studio Center with around 1,800 members of the Telugu diaspora gathering for a vibrant display of culture, devotion, and belonging. The venue transformed into a riot of colours as women and young girls arrived adorned in beautiful silk sarees and traditional langa vonis . But the true centerpiece was hundreds of intricately arranged Bathukamma flower mounds, brought by attendees as offerings to Goddess Gowri and mother nature. The air resonated with devotional songs as participants danced in circles around the floral stacks, their synchronized claps and movements creating a mesmerizing spectacle. The festivities opened on a spiritual note with a traditional Shami pooja conducted by the local temple priest. Updated - October 24, 2026 08:09 pm IST - DINDIGUL Farmers in Dindigul district expressed their happiness over the continuous rainfall in the region. They distributed sweets during the farmers grievance redress meeting held at the Dindigul Collectorate on Friday. At the meeting presided over by Dindigul Collector Durgamoorthi, the farmers said residents of Kalanjipatti and Veriyappur were affected by the stone quarry operations. They demanded that the licence should be cancelled. A section of farmers complained that sewage had accumulated in a pond at Avilipatti. They also complained that the inlet channel leading to the Thattankulam tank and the supply channel leading to the Nagayakottai tank had been encroached upon. The Collector said steps would be taken to provide proper drainage facilities in Avilipatti and the encroachments would be removed. A section of farmers demanded that a survey be conducted across the district and adequate compensation be paid to affected farmers. The Collector assured the farmers that steps would be taken to conduct a survey in this regard. Farmers complained that the road from Natham to the foothills of Sirumalai was severely damaged. Ravi Singh, Railways’ hard-hitting willow-wielder, is quite new to the rigours of First Class cricket. The 25-year-old — who has a penchant for striking big in the shorter formats — hasn’t taken long to adjust to the longest discipline, averaging a creditable 58.2 after seven Ranji Trophy innings. Ravi, who works as a ticket collector in Howrah, had to bide his time before finding his place in the Railways team. He shifted from Varanasi to Lucknow to hone his skills under coach Saurabh Dubey, though he couldn’t quite break into the senior Uttar Pradesh set-up. But once he landed a Railways job, Ravi’s career finally stoked some steam. “After playing well for the under-23 side, I was called to the National Cricket Academy [now Centre of Excellence]. The Syed Mushtaq Ali and Vijay Hazare tournaments went quite well for me. Some of those matches were broadcast and the selectors at a higher level watched them. I was called for IPL trials, and, after seven or eight years of not playing anything [significant], things suddenly started falling my way,” Ravi said at the MAC Stadium on Saturday, two days ahead of the Ranji game against Tamil Nadu. Ravi was picked up by Rajasthan Royals for ₹95 lakh in the IPL 2026 auction. 5dac272ab23fd7c8.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Need help with your subscription? Published - October 24, 2026 08:14 pm IST - Kolkata The CPI(M), CPI(ML) Liberation, SUCI (Communist), and other Left parties have a decades-old tradition of setting up book stalls during the Durga Puja festivities. Credit: Facebook/CPI(M) West Bengal The book stalls affiliated with the Communist Party of India (Marxist) witnessed record sales in West Bengal during Durga Puja. They sold books worth over ₹1 crore even as many of their stalls faced repeated attacks. The CPI(M), CPI(ML) Liberation, SUCI (Communist), and other Left parties have a decades-old tradition of setting up book stalls during the Durga Puja festivities. “The people have shown immense resistance against the hooliganism and attacks on the book stalls. Published - October 24, 2026 08:14 pm IST - RAMANATHAPURAM Director General of Police and Head of Police Force Mahesh Kumar Aggarwal along with Ramanathapuram SP G. Chandeesh and other officials at the Muthuramalinga Thevar memorial ahead of Thevar Jayanthi in Ramanathapuram on Saturday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement A total of 480 high-definition cameras, mobile CCTV cameras and specialised drones would be deployed for real-time monitoring in and around Pasumpon in Ramanathapuram district through a Centralised Control Room. The Director General of Police (Head of Police Force) Mahesh Kumar Aggarwal, who visited the Pasumpon village on Saturday, took stock of the preparedness of the police force for the Thevar Jayanthi scheduled to be held on October 30. According to a press release, the camera systems are equipped with facial recognition and number plate recognition capabilities to strengthen surveillance and facilitate the timely identification of persons and vehicles, wherever required. Over 460 police patrol vehicles and quick reaction teams ( QRTs ) would be deployed for bandobust duties during the Jayanthi. The DGP inspected the commemoration venue, reviewed the preparations and interacted with the organisers to assess the arrangements and discussed operational requirements. Later, a review meeting was held at Kamuthi in which ADGP (Law and Order) T. S. Anbu Tamil Nadu, Inspector General of Police, (South Zone) Vijayendra Bidari, Commissioner of Police, Madurai City, S. Rajendiran, DIGs of Police, Abhinav Kumar (Madurai Range) and Manivannan (Ramanathapuram Range) and Superintendents of Police G. Chandeesh (Ramanathapuram), Abishek Gupta (Sivaganga), Gautam Goyal (Virudhunagar), R. Shivaprasad (Thoothukudi) and Devanathan (Madurai) attended. The security would comprise seven DIGs of Police, 40 SPs and over 18,000 police

f5ed28e5f787aba0.title: APEPDCL puts 12 coastal districts on high alert for Cyclone Arnab
f5ed28e5f787aba0.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Need help with your subscription? Published - October 24, 2026 08:15 pm IST - VISAKHAPATNAM Andhra Pradesh Eastern Power Distribution Company Limited (APEPDCL) Chairman and Managing Director Immadi Prudhvitej on Saturday (October 24, 2026) instructed field officials across 12 coastal districts to maintain maximum operational readiness following IMD warnings of ‘Cyclone Arnab’ expected between October 26 and 28. Chairing a teleconference with Superintending Engineers and Executive Engineers, the CMD ordered division-wise control rooms to be set up in Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Parvathipuram Manyam, Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli, Alluri Sitarama Raju, Kakinada, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, East Godavari, West Godavari, Eluru, and Polavaram. To ensure uninterrupted power supply to critical services, field teams have been mobilised with emergency vehicles, replacement transformers, electric poles, and clearing equipment for immediate damage restoration. The distribution utility’s corporate headquarters will monitor grid stability around the clock. Consumers have been cautioned to avoid fallen electrical wires, damaged poles, and uprooted trees, and to report power disruptions through the toll-free helpline 1912 or district control rooms. a7b5a5be05d9f25f.title: TDB to set up food safety laboratory at Pampa for evaluation of FSSAI parameters in production of prasadam
a7b5a5be05d9f25f.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Need help with your subscription? Published - October 24, 2026 08:22 pm IST - KOCHI The Travancore Devaswom Board recently informed the Kerala High Court that a laboratory would be set up at Pampa for evaluation of prasadam as per Food Safety and Standards Authority of India parameters, including testing for pesticides and toxin levels, before the start of Sabarimala pilgrimage season. The Division Bench of Justices Raja Vijayaraghavan and K.V. Jayakumar was informed that the Food Safety department would identify requirements and prepare a time-bound implementation plan. A decision was also taken to obtain National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories accreditation simultaneously, the Board stated. Currently, the samples are sent to a laboratory in Thiruvananthapuram for evaluation. The Food Safety department had apprised the Board that the equipment for the laboratory would cost around ₹2 crore to ₹3 crore and the laboratory would require an air-conditioned space of about 1000 sq. ft.; these requirements were affirmed by the Board. The department also agreed to arrange qualified personnel to operate the equipment and conduct the tests. It would examine the possibility of deploying two existing, duly appointed food safety officers for statutory inspection and sampling at Sabarimala. Published - October 24, 2026 08:16 pm IST - HYDERABAD The Cyberabad police have invoked the Preventive Detention (PD) Act against a 29-year-old alleged property offender who has been involved in 14 criminal cases since 2017, including cases of cheating, kidnapping, robbery and extortion. Cyberabad Commissioner of Police M. Ramesh ordered the detention of Nagaraju Raghu Varma alias Nagaraju Karthikeya Raghu Varma alias Vamshi alias Alluri Vijaya Ram. He was lodged in Central Prison, Cherlapalli, Medchal district. According to the Cyberabad police, Varma is a native of Poduru mandal in West Godavari district of Andhra Pradesh who migrated to Hyderabad and initially worked as a driver. Police said he later turned to criminal activities in pursuit of easy money. “Varma impersonated a police officer and approached people claiming that criminal cases had been registered against them at various police stations. He allegedly threatened them with legal consequences and extorted money by promising to help them,” said the police, adding that he was also accused of kidnapping targeted persons and robbing them after threatening them with firearms. Between 2017 and 2026, he was involved in 14 cases relating to cheating, kidnapping, robbery, extortion, criminal intimidation and offences under the Arms Act, 1959, according to the police. This is the third time that the Cyberabad police have detained Varma under the PD Act. He was previously detained in 2021 and 2024. Police said he resumed criminal activities after both releases and was subsequently involved in four more cases involving kidnapping, extortion and robbery while allegedly impersonating a police officer. Updated - October 24, 2026 08:00 pm IST - Bengaluru Image for representational purposes only. | Photo Credit: Gettu Images A 25-year-old man from Bihar died after a car allegedly hit him and dragged him for nearly 100 metres following a confrontation over the vehicle’s speed in Pragathinagar, in Electronics City police station limits, in the early hours of October 21. The deceased has been identified as Ranjit Kumar Sahu, who worked as a cook at a paying guest accommodation in BTM Layout. He was undergoing treatment at a private hospital in Madiwala for serious injuries sustained in the incident but died, the police said. According to the complaint lodged by his friend, Nitish Mukhiya, Ranjit had come to Electronics City to celebrate the Dasara festival. After celebrating with friends, he was walking with them to the house of the complainant’s brother in Pragathinagar, where they planned to spend the night. While they were crossing the road, a white compact sedan car allegedly approached at high speed. When Ranjit and his friends signalled the driver to slow down, the occupants of the car reportedly became angry, took a U-turn and returned to confront them, the complaint stated. Following an altercation, Mr. Nitish alerted other friends, who arrived at the spot. A heated exchange reportedly broke out between the two groups. The occupants of the car then allegedly attempted to run the vehicle into the group. While the others managed to move aside, Ranjit was hit by the car. The car allegedly ran over his legs and dragged him for nearly 100 metres before the occupants abandoned him in the middle of the Hosur service road and fled the scene, according to the complaint. Published - October 24, 2026 07:56 pm IST Union Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh. File | Photo Credit: PTI The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC) has extended the tenure of Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh by one year, until October 31, 2027. Also read | Defence Secretary holds key meetings at Shangri-La Dialogue 2026, pushes for Indo-Pacific security cooperation His current tenure was scheduled to end on October 31, 2026. Mr. Singh will now serve in the role until October 31, 2027, or until further orders, whichever comes first, in relaxation of FR 65(d) and Rule 16 (1A) of the All India Service (Death-Cum-Retirement Benefits) Rules, 1958, the Centre said on Saturday (October 24, 2026). Mr. Singh took over as Defence Secretary at South Block on November 1, 2024 . He took over from Giridhar Aramane, a 1988-batch IAS officer of Andhra Pradesh cadre, who had retired from service October 31, 2024 after a two year stint. He is a 1989-batch IAS officer from the Kerala cadre and assumed the charge of the Officer on Special Duty (Defence Secretary-designate) on August 20, 2024. Published - October 24, 2026 07:59 pm IST - PALAKKAD Malabar Devaswom Board has ordered steps to evict Club-6, a partnership firm that operates a convention centre on 77.90 ares of temple land at Puthur, Palakkad, after declaring its 30-year lease invalid. In an order dated September 8, Devaswom Commissioner T.C. Biju rejected a request to retrospectively approve the lease, which was executed in 2017 without the prior sanction required under Section 29 of the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Act, 1951. The Commissioner directed the deputy commissioner to appoint a person to oversee the temple’s administration and expedite eviction proceedings. The order said the president of Ramanathapuram Grama Devaswom Society, which executed the lease, had failed to establish his legal authority to lease the property belonging to Ramanathapuram Devaswom. The society’s registration under the Societies Registration Act in 2022 did not confer the powers of a trustee under the HR&CE Act. The lease was granted to Club-6 for 30 years. The society’s president later sought retrospective approval, arguing that the arrangement was intended to generate income for the temple. The Commissioner rejected the plea, holding that the required sanction had to be obtained before the lease was executed and that the law did not permit the retrospective approval sought. The order also questioned the handling of rent payments. Records showed payments only from 2022, despite the lease having begun in 2017. The rent was deposited into accounts held in the society’s name, and the evidence did not establish that the proceeds had been properly accounted for by the legally authorised temple administration. Updated - October 24, 2026 07:29 pm IST - HYDERABAD Senior BJP leader Gudur Narayana Reddy on Saturday proposed a three-point action plan to help Telangana address water, agricultural and power challenges arising from El Niño conditions, stressing the need for coordination among the government, experts, farmers and local communities. Mr. Reddy said the government’s focus on safeguarding drinking water supplies and preparing for difficult conditions in the coming months was appropriate. He said the emphasis should now be on translating policy directions into localised, measurable and publicly accessible action. He proposed setting up a small, time-bound technical cell comprising officials from the Irrigation, Groundwater and Agriculture departments, along with independent hydrologists and agronomists from agricultural universities, research institutions and ICAR institutes to coordinate measures and address emerging challenges. His second suggestion was to expedite community-level groundwater recharge and water conservation works in the most water-stressed mandals. Desilting tanks and check dams, developing farm ponds and creating percolation pits should be prioritised before peak summer, he said. As a third measure, Mr. Reddy proposed a public monitoring dashboard that tracks three key indicators: reservoir releases, the movement of drinking water tankers, and the number of hours of electricity supply to agricultural feeders. efeb08d6a3ab8a72.title: MCC-Murugappa Gold Cup: Hockey Karnataka rallies to hold PNB
efeb08d6a3ab8a72.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Updated - October 24, 2026 07:36 pm IST - CHENNAI: Gursimran Singh firing in Punjab National Bank’s second goal against Karnataka on Saturday. | Photo Credit: R. RAGU Hockey Karnataka fought back from a two-goal deficit to hold Punjab National Bank (PNB) to a 2-2 draw in a Pool-A match of the 97th All-India MCC-Murugappa Gold Cup hockey tournament at the SDAT Mayor Radhakrishnan Stadium here on Saturday. PNB dominated with its raids in the first half, but Karnataka showed greater purpose after the break to claw its way back into the contest. Neeraj put PNB ahead in the 14th minute with an impressive individual effort. Winning the ball from an opponent near the left sideline, he beat and dribbled past two Karnataka players and closed in on goal before slotting the ball past goalkeeper K.K. Tharun Ganapathy. Gursimran Singh doubled PNB’s lead in the 16th minute, converting a penalty corner with a drag-flick. Though Tharun intercepted the effort, he could not keep it out. Karnataka began its recovery in the 32nd minute through a well-coordinated move. Maji Ganesh found Bhrath Mahalingappa Kurtakot, who directed the ball for C.J. Rahul to finish. G. Vishwas completed Karnataka’s comeback in the 52nd minute. The side had chances to snatch victory, winning two penalty corners in the final three minutes, but failed to convert either. The results: Pool-A: Punjab National Bank 2 (Neeraj 14, Gursimran Singh 16-pc) drew with Hockey Karnataka 2 (C.J. Rahul 32, G. Vishwas 52). Pool-B: Indian Navy 5 (Rajat Sharma 15, Ashis Topno 35-pc, Nitesh 38, Sundra Pandi 58, K. Selvaraj 60) bt SAI-NCOE Bhopal 2 (Mohammed Zaid Khan 26, Bhrat Kaushik 59). Updated - October 24, 2026 07:40 pm IST - TIRUCHI The National Platform for Domestic Workers (NPDW) has urged the government to regulate the domestic service sector and provide better working conditions for its employees. At a press meet held here on Saturday, P. Clarammal, State coordinator, Tamil Nadu Domestic Workers Association, said that women formed a large section of the household service sector and they often had to work in unsafe conditions. “We urge the government to formulate laws that will ensure the personal safety of domestic workers and prevent exploitation by employers,” she said. The body focused on the enactment of comprehensive central legislation for domestic workers, and the ratification of the International Labour Organisation’s C.189 (Decent Work for Domestic Workers) convention by the Union government. The KFDC has opened a Kurinji trek for enthusiasts to relish the spectacular sight. Meeshapulimala, one of the Munnar region’s highest peaks, is witnessing the blooming of Neelakurinji and will open to tourists starting Monday (October 26). The peak falls under the jurisdiction of the Kerala Forest Development Corporation (KFDC) in Munnar. KFDC Munnar Manager Akhil Das said visitors will have the opportunity to view the blooms at higher elevations. “The KFDC has arranged multi-utility vehicles (MUVs) for the 30-kilometre journey from Munnar to Meeshapulimala at a fare of ₹1,250 per person. Tourists will be picked up from the Munnar KFDC office and transported in these specially arranged vehicles. The package includes a snack box and drinking water,” he said. KFDC District Manager Sujith P.K. stated that the corporation, in association with the Wildlife Trust of India (WTI), has launched the ‘Kurinji’ mobile application for online bookings. Visitors can reserve slots and make payments directly through the app. “The key attraction at Meeshapulimala is the Neelakurinji bloom alongside sightings of the endangered Nilgiri tahr. KFDC plans to provide a unique ecotourism experience here,” Mr. Sujith said. Officials added that the Kurinji mobile app lets users easily find locations and other travel details. Updated - October 24, 2026 07:41 pm IST - KOCHI Image for representational purpose After grappling with a rise in influenza cases for months, Ernakulam has reported relatively fewer cases in October. According to the health authorities, influenza activity may be declining even as the district braces for monsoon-related diseases such as dengue and leptospirosis. A health official said the dip in influenza cases was expected. “Influenza is a seasonal outbreak, and the disease is in the declining phase now. But with intermittent rains, we are expecting an increase in dengue cases. We have to intensify precautionary measures against dengue and other monsoon-related communicable diseases. This can be done by focussing on source-reduction activities, which need to be strengthened,” the official said. A total of 335 influenza cases were reported until October 23, according to the Health department. The district registered a total of 588 dengue cases during the month, including 168 confirmed and 420 suspected cases. It also reported 31 cases of leptospirosis, including 24 confirmed and seven suspected cases, and two deaths due to the disease. A total of 212 Domestic Breeding Checkers (DBC) have been engaged in door-to-door inspections across 60 wards of the corporation to identify mosquito larvae in water storage tanks, drums, flower pots, coconut shells, discarded tyres and other potential breeding sites. Larvicides are being applied and mosquito control activities are being carried out to prevent mosquito breeding. In addition to routine cleaning activities, intensive cleaning operations are being undertaken on a war footing to remove stagnant rainwater, garbage and other potential mosquito breeding sources from vacant plots, open spaces, parks and public spaces within the corporation limits. Fogging operations are also being carried out across all wards using four vehicle mounted fogging machines and 20 handheld pulse fogging machines to control mosquito population. Published - October 24, 2026 07:29 pm IST - SIVAGANAGA In view of upcoming memorial observances, District Collector P. Akash has announced holidays for schools and colleges across seven unions in the Sivaganga district on October 27 and 30, alongside temporary closures for the district’s prominent archaeological site. The closure on October 27 marks the memorial day of Marudu Pandiyar brothers, which is observed in Kalaiyarkovil. Following this, schools and colleges will shut down again on October 30 for the birth anniversary and memorial day of freedom fighter and leader Muthuramalinga Thevar, a major annual event held at Pasumpon in the neighbouring Ramanathapuram district. The holiday directives apply to all schools and colleges situated within seven designated unions: Sivaganga, Devakottai, Tirupattur, Thiruppuvanam, Manamadurai, Kalaiyarkovil, and Ilayangudi. Additionally, as part of the safety and crowd management measures surrounding the Pasumpon Thevar Jayanthi celebrations, the district administration has announced a two-day closure for the Keeladi Site Museum in Sivaganga district, which will stay shut for visitors on October 29 and 30. The holiday directives apply to all schools and colleges situated within seven designated unions: Sivaganga, Devakottai, Tirupattur, Thiruppuvanam, Manamadurai, Kalaiyarkovil, and Ilayangudi. Additionally, as part of the safety and crowd management measures surrounding the Pasumpon Thevar Jayanthi celebrations, the district administration has announced a two-day closure for the Keeladi Site Museum in Sivaganga district, which will stay shut for visitors on October 29 and 30. Updated - October 24, 2026 07:10 pm IST - MYSURU A new book titled ‘Who are the Kodavas (Coorgs)?’ written by journalist and author P.T. Bopanna has been launched. A statement by the author said the book, which decodes the mystery of the origin of the Kodavas, is based on the first genetic study of the community. The credit for providing these early scientific leads to the puzzle should go to Coorg-born Professor Buttiyanda Kuttapa Thelma, widely known as B.K. Thelma, whose team comprised scientists from the University of Delhi South Campus and the Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology, Hyderabad, the statement said. “The genetic study of Kodavas has not only attempted to resolve the question around the origin of Kodavas, but has also thrown insight into Indian population genetics, demonstrating that even small, tight-knit communities may harbour vast genetic complexities, shaped by centuries of migration, isolation and social customs,” the statement added. Annamalai speaking at a programme in Udupi on Saturday. | Photo Credit: UMESH S. SHETTIGAR Former IPS officer and founder of ‘We The Leaders’ K. Annamalai said on Saturday that politics in Karnataka needs to become more responsible than limiting to a style of politics that seeks votes by promising freebies. Speaking at the State-level retailers’ convention of the All India Mobile Retailers Association (AIMRA) in Udupi, Mr. Annamalai said that political parties should focus on providing good governance to the State. Karnataka deserves better governance. It is not enough for development to be concentrated solely in Bengaluru, he said. “Karnataka should not remain a State dependent solely on Bengaluru, but rather achieve development across all its regions,” he said. Mr. Annamalai said that a change in the political system is possible only when competition between political parties is based on developmental projects. The government’s achievements should serve as the benchmark for political rivalry. Such a responsible and competitive political system can lead to improvements in governance, he said. Mr. Annamalai said that politics should not be limited merely to a “poster culture”. Instead of putting up posters announcing the arrival of a Chief Minister or a former Chief Minister, there should be posters that inform the public about the contributions the government. MOORTHY The current spell of rain over the past few days has battered many key roads in the city, causing hardship to commuters and motorists. Since the onset of the northeast monsoon on October 15, Tiruchi has been getting rainfall. The rainfall was not heavy in the city up to Thursday and it received only light showers. However, it received heavy rain in different parts on Friday.The continuous rainfall has damaged many arterial roads and interior roads. Uneven road surfaces and potholes have become common sights on major stretches, with the top layer eroded in many places. The damaged patches have led to frequent skidding incidents, particularly affecting two-wheeler riders. Anna Nagar roads, Karur bypass, old Madurai road, West Boulevard Road, Major Saravanan Road and important stretches around the Central Bus Stand, such as Rockins Road, McDonalds Road, VOC Road, and Williams Road, have suffered significant deterioration. Similarly, stretches around the Chathiram Bus Stand were also damaged. Similar issues have cropped up around the Gandhi Market, Palakarai, Varaganeri and others. With heavy vehicle movement continuing through these roads, the loose surface material has begun to dislodge, worsening driving conditions. Recently patched up roads too have also suffered the damage. Motorists say the situation has grown increasingly unsafe, especially during nighttime travel. “We encounter many deep potholes and eroded stretches on the city roads. a7a625e6948fe0cc.title: TN coach Murray wants the players to develop a cohesive style of play
a7a625e6948fe0cc.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription Additional Subscription Benefits Need help with your subscription? Published - October 24, 2026 07:18 pm IST - CHENNAI William Murray. | Photo Credit: R. RAGU William Murray, Hockey Unit of Tamil Nadu’s (HUTN) high-performance coach, wants the State team to be more than just a winning unit. The Englishman, who joined the Sports Development Authority of Tamil Nadu (SDAT) in May on a two-year contract, wants his players to develop an exciting, cohesive style of hockey that draws crowds. An FIH coach educator, Murray first came to India this year to conduct Level 3 coaching courses for Hockey India (HI) in Rourkela and Hyderabad before taking up the role of coaching the Tamil Nadu men’s team. He has worked in Hong Kong and Belgium, and coached England’s u-18 and Scotland’s u-21 teams. Murray believes the lack of early exposure to artificial turf has influenced Indian players’ technical and tactical development. “Too often, it’s very individualised here. Even things like pushing (push pass), since it’s not done in the same way on gravel, grass, or dirt pitches, there’s a desire to get the ball off the floor as much as possible. Whereas on astro, you want the ball on the floor, where it moves quickly but smoothly. That allows the whole team to stay connected up the pitch and work together. “I’m trying to implement some quite rigorous tactical concepts, which will take time. I want us to be exciting - to play fast, with style and swagger, but also in a connected way,” he said. The coach is also keen to strengthen the State’s hockey pipeline. “More than just focusing on one team, for me it’s about making sure the whole ecosystem is rich, so that any young player, whatever their background, if they’re good enough, gets the opportunity and understanding to be nurtured and grow to their potential,” he said. Updated - October 24, 2026 07:08 pm IST - Hyderabad Researchers found traces of West Eurasian and Steppe-linked maternal lineages among some Konkani-speaking communities, offering fresh insights into the region’s complex population history. | Photo Credit: Jaison Sequeira Ancient migrations into South Asia may have involved women as well as men, according to a new genetic study of Konkani-speaking communities along India’s west coast. Comparisons with ancient DNA suggested that prehistoric migrations into South Asia were more complex than previously understood. Researchers from the CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CCMB), Hyderabad, and Mangalore University found traces of West Eurasian and Steppe-linked maternal lineages among some groups, offering fresh insights into the region’s complex population history. The findings of the study led by CCMB’s K. Thangaraj and Mangalore University's M.S. Mustak challenge the notion that Bronze Age migrations into the subcontinent were driven predominantly by males. The Konkan region, stretching from Daman in the north to the Gangavalli River and Karwar in the south, is known for its rich cultural, linguistic and social diversity. Although Konkani is spoken across the region, its speakers belong to several communities with distinct histories and traditions. To trace their maternal origins, researchers analysed maternally inherited mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) from 295 Konkani-speaking individuals. The population was broadly classified into Sarasvata and non-Sarasvata groups, based on oral traditions regarding ancestry linked to the ancient Sarasvati region. Observed from October 26 to 31 under the aegis of the Association of Indian Management Schools (AIMS-New Delhi), the initiatives reflect a simple yet meaningful belief: building a better city is a shared responsibility. During the week, students will engage with communities at more than 30 identified waste hotspots across Coimbatore. By promoting waste segregation at source and responsible disposal, they will encourage everyday practices that protect the environment and improve neighbourhoods for everyone. The initiative will also highlight the connection between unmanaged waste and street dogs. Discarded food and other waste can attract dogs to public spaces, increase the risk of conflict and create unhealthy conditions for people and animals. Students will also conduct rabies awareness activities across 30 identified locations in the city in association with the Humane Animal Society (HAS), to promote rabies prevention, safe interactions with street dogs and humane animal care. 40b7e4fba524fcb4.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription Additional Subscription Benefits Need help with your subscription? Published - October 24, 2026 04:41 pm IST - MUMBAI A man walks past the Kotak Mahindra Bank branch in New Delhi | Photo Credit: Reuters Kotak Mahindra Bank reported a 26% year-on-year (YoY) increase in net profit to ₹5,645.38 crore for the quarter ended September, beating analysts’ estimates based on LSEG data but falling short of domestic brokerages’ projections of 27-32% growth. The lender’s total income rose 18% YoY to ₹29,426.88 crore. Other income increased nearly 25% to ₹9,571.01 crore. However, sequentially, total income and other income declined 2.1% and 18.3%, respectively. Net interest income (NII) grew 16% YoY to ₹8,459 crore. Net interest margin (NIM), however, contracted to 4.31% from 4.54% in the preceding quarter. The bank attributed the decline to deposits mobilised under the Reserve Bank of India’s special window for foreign currency non-resident bank (FCNR-B) accounts, through which it raised ₹55,344 crore. Asset quality improved, with gross non-performing assets (GNPA) declining to 1.04% from 1.39% a year earlier. Net NPA fell to 0.24% from 0.32%. Provisions declined 15% YoY to ₹803 crore. Operating expenses rose 14% YoY to ₹5,271 crore, partly offsetting the gains from higher income and lower provisions. For the first half of FY27, net profit stood at ₹11,125.84 crore. As of September 30, net advances grew 25% YoY to ₹5,77,295 crore, while deposits increased 23% to ₹6,51,491 crore. Sindhu in action. | Photo Credit: Shiv Kumar Pushpakar Two-time Olympic medallist P V Sindhu advanced to her second Super 750 final of the year with a thrilling win over Japan’s Hina Akechi at the French Open in Paris on Saturday. The 31-year-old Indian, who won the Japan Open Super 750 in July, displayed immaculate temperament to register a 21-10, 20-22, 21-16 win over world No. 22 Akechi in an hour and 13 minutes. The 21-year-old Japanese, who beat Wang Zhi Yi and Putri Kusuma Wardani earlier in the week, used deceptive strokes and quality defence to trouble Sindhu, but the Indian held her nerve to emerge victorious. Sindhu will face Korea's world No. 1 An Se Young in the summit clash. The opening game was closely contested initially, with the players locked at 4-4 and 8-8 before Sindhu took an 11-9 lead into the interval. She then took charge, winning 11 of the last 12 points to seal the game 21-10 in 18 minutes. Sindhu, a former world champion, fell four points behind in the second game but raised her pace to draw level at 7-7. Her round-the-head cross-court attack produced winners as the players stayed neck and neck until 10-10, before Akechi edged ahead. The world No. 11 Indian stayed close at 14-14 and later caught up at 16-16 with a cross-court smash before moving ahead with a deceptive return. The Japanese kept pace and earned a game point. Sindhu saved it at 20-20 after a net exchange, but Akechi secured another opportunity and converted it when the Indian hit wide. Sindhu made a 5-3 start in the decider, but Akechi fought back to lead 6-5. bcfc461a8cec3809.title: Air pollution alert: 3 Punjab cities among world's top 10 most polluted; Check AQI
bcfc461a8cec3809.summary: Amritsar, Bathinda and Faridkot in Punjab were among the five most polluted cities in India, according to real-time Air Quality Index (AQI) rankings. Amritsar recorded an AQI of 392, followed by Bathinda at 368 and Faridkot at 360. Meerut in Uttar Pradesh and Fatehpur rounded out the top five, with AQI readings of 355 and 354, respectively. Meanwhile, Delhi continued to record ‘poor’ air quality on Friday, with an AQI of 230. The capital’s air quality is expected to remain in the ‘poor’ category over the next nine days, according to the Air Quality Early Warning System. These rankings are time-sensitive and can change as pollution levels and weather conditions fluctuate. Delhi recorded an AQI of 230 on Friday, placing it in the ‘poor’ category. According to data from the Central Pollution Control Board ’s (CPCB) Sameer app, three of the capital’s 56 monitoring stations recorded ‘very poor’ air quality. Pusa recorded the highest AQI among the monitoring stations, at 324. Meanwhile, 36 stations reported ‘poor’ air quality, while the remaining 17 recorded ‘moderate’ conditions. The Air Quality Early Warning System has forecast that Delhi’s air quality will remain ‘poor’ from October 23 to October 26 and is likely to stay in the same category for the following six days. Weather conditions are expected to remain unfavourable for the dispersal of pollutants. According to the forecast, a ventilation index below 6,000 square metres per second, combined with an average wind speed of less than 10 kmph, can hinder the dispersion of pollutants. Such conditions can allow pollutants to accumulate near the surface, prolonging periods of poor air quality. According to the Decision Support System for Air Quality Management in Delhi, developed by IITM Pune, the transport sector accounted for 20.3% of the capital’s air pollution. Published - October 24, 2026 05:20 pm IST Rajinikanth in ‘Jailer 2’. | Photo Credit: Sun Pictures/YouTube In a rare development, Tamil star Rajinikanth watched his latest blockbuster, Jailer 2 , with fans. Production house Sun Pictures posted on X (Formerly Twitter) that the superstar watched his film in a theatre with fans after four decades. “For the first time in 40 years, Superstar Rajinikanth joins fans to witness Jailer 2 on the big screen,” wrote Sun Pictures. Directed by Nelson, the Tamil movie hit the screens on October 15, 2026. With music composed by Anirudh Ravichander, the sequel to the 2023 hit has become a major blockbuster. beb21fd12844965c.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription Additional Subscription Benefits Need help with your subscription? Updated - October 24, 2026 05:20 pm IST Kumaran Nagar bus terminus on October 20, 2026. This has turned the terminus slippery and flyblown, and it smells bad. Kumaran Nagar bus terminus in Kolathur is unhygienic with cow dung all over the place. Commuters say that the bus services operated from the terminus are very poor, and hence the terminus remains vacant for most of the day; also, commuters hardly wait here for the buses. So, all these have provided a conducive environment for cows to occupy the terminus. Alcohol bottles found at the terminus point to misuse of the terminus for consumption. It may be noted this terminus was redeveloped and inaugurated early this year but the facility fell into a state of neglect within a few weeks. The toilets are also unhygienic due to the erratic water supply. The room meant for lactating mothers is kept under lock-and-key. Further, there is no timekeeper here. Commuters are clueless when the next bus would arrive. Though there is a room dedicated for the timekeeper, it also remains locked. Services operated from the terminus need to be improved. There are buses only to Guindy and Anna Square. Further, the frequency is also very poor and not reliable. So commuters rely on share autorickshaws to access Paper Mills Road. From there, they go to the Retteri junction or the Perambur bus terminus or the Thiru Vi Ka Nagar terminus to access buses to other places. This is quite inconvenient. Where is the need to redevelop a bus terminus which receives poor patronage? N. 7851e78b35628447.title: India's forex reserves decline $5 billion to $721 billion: RBI data
7851e78b35628447.summary: India's forex reserves dropped by USD 5.011 billion to USD 721.016 billion during the week ended October 16, the Reserve Bank of India said on Friday. In the previous reporting week, the kitty declined by USD 8.578 billion to USD 726.027 billion. The reserves touched an all-time high of USD 785.706 billion for the week ended September 4, driven by heavy greenback inflow as part of a special concessional swap for deposits from the diaspora through which banks raised a record nearly USD 133 billion but have been on a declining trend ever since. Experts attribute the sharp decline in the kitty to deployment of FCNR(B) resources and currency defence put up by the RBI through dollar sales. For the week ended October 16, foreign currency assets, a major component of reserves, decreased by USD 5.758 billion to USD 591.847 billion, according to the data released by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). ed7d9cd2c46fa5d0.summary: The government will share the cost of high-risk deepwater oil and gas exploration with energy companies under the Rs 84,084-crore Samudra Manthan scheme, offering to pay part of the cost of risky exploration wells, fund seismic mapping of offshore basins and help build shared production facilities. The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas issued operational guidelines for the Samudra Manthan programme, which aims to improve the economics of exploring India's deepwater and ultra-deepwater basins, where high drilling costs and uncertain geological prospects have constrained investment. 1df76ae7afa31607.title: CG Power and Industrial Solutions Q2 profit jumps 44% to ₹409 crore
1df76ae7afa31607.summary: CG Power and Industrial Solutions on Friday posted 44 per cent jump in consolidated net profit at Rs 409.09 crore for September quarter FY27, supported by higher revenues. The Mumbai-headquartered entity had clocked a profit after tax (PAT) of Rs 284.44 crore in the year-ago period, it said in an exchange filing. During the quarter, the company's total income increased to Rs 3,883.25 crore from Rs 2,988.89 crore in Q2 FY26. From power systems segment, the revenue was Rs 1,766.76 crore as against Rs 1,254.49 crore in the year-ago quarter. The industrial systems business contributed a revenue of Rs 1,868.61 crore in the quarter as against Rs 1,533.33 crore in July-September FY26. The company's board approved enhancing capex investment for the GIS brownfield project at Vilholi, Nashik, from Rs 35.17 crore to Rs 44.62 crore. It also gave nod to invest Rs 15.31 crore to enhance EHV (extra high voltage) circuit breaker manufacturing capacity by 3,600 units (annually) at S3 Unit-II ...

Operating revenue increased by 29.8 per cent to Rs 17,014.06 crore during the quarter under review from Rs 13,106.34 crore in Q2 FY26, it said. 0404e1873c16f985.title: Petronet LNG, Gruner Renewable float JV to develop compressed biogas plants
0404e1873c16f985.summary: Petronet LNG and Gruner Renewable Energy have formed a 50:50 joint venture to develop a portfolio of compressed biogas (CBG) plants across India, which entails an initial investment of about Rs 1,200 crore. This model is first of its kind in India, where the JV partner is undertaking sourcing of feedstock, EPC, operations and maintenance and offtake of organic manure, thus integrating the CBG value chain, a statement said. The proposed partnership envisages the development of 10 CBG plants, each with a designed capacity of 18 metric tonnes per day, taking the planned aggregate capacity to approximately 180 metric tonnes per day. The combined investment for the proposed portfolio is estimated at around Rs 1,200 crore, it informed. The partnership brings together Petronet LNG's established position in India's LNG and natural-gas infrastructure ecosystem with Gruner Renewable Energy's experience in CBG project development, engineering, feedstock mobilisation and plant operations. 791461cc61bd7ae8.summary: Bharat Coal Gasification and Chemicals Ltd (BCGCL), the joint venture of Coal India Ltd (CIL) and BHEL, has started ground construction activities for its Rs 25,000 crore coal gasification project in Odisha, with most of the tenders awarded, its Managing Director Peeyush Kumar said on Thursday. The development assumes significance in the wake of the country's push to build 100 million tonne of coal gasification capacity by 2030 under the National Coal Gasification Mission, aimed at converting coal into chemicals and bringing down the import dependence on products such as LNG, urea, ammonia and methanol. "We are going ahead with the joint venture of BHEL and Coal India, which is BCGCL....I am happy to share that we have started ground construction activities... Most of the tenders have been awarded and construction has started," Kumar said during the 17th Edition of Gasification India 2026 organised by Mission Energy Foundation. d7d7f7c06453556f.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Bank on Thursday reported a 10.6 per cent rise in net profit to Rs 546.36 crore for the second quarter ended September 30, driven by earnings growth and improvement in asset quality. The bank earned Rs 494.11 crore net profit in the year-ago period. Sequentially, its profits surged 28.8 per cent from Rs 424.18 crore in the first quarter of the current fiscal year, a bank spokesperson said. The bank announced the financial results after its Board of Directors reviewed and approved the quarterly and half-yearly figures at a meeting held at its corporate headquarters here on Thursday. Its net interest income rose 5 per cent during the quarter to Rs 1,502 crore. The lender's other income more than doubled to Rs 314.90 crore from Rs 153.76 cr a year ago. For the first half of the current fiscal year, the bank's operating expenditure grew 1.5 per cent, and its operating profit rose over 15 per cent to Rs 1,492 crore. Total income, including other income, increased 1.32 per cent to Rs 8,022.73 crore in the financial year ended March 31, 2026, according to financial data accessed through business intelligence platform Tofler. Sony India, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Japanese technology major Sony Corporation, had reported a profit of Rs 157.03 crore and revenue from operations of Rs 7,851.08 crore in FY25. b603c52963c725a4.title: Essar Ports wins ₹2,276 crore Tuna Tekra terminal project at Kandla
b603c52963c725a4.summary: Essar Ports has secured a letter of award from Deendayal Port Authority to develop an 18.33-million-tonne-a-year multipurpose cargo terminal at Tuna Tekra in Gujarat's Kandla port, marking a renewed push by the group to expand its ports business. The project carries an estimated cost of Rs 2,276.06 crore, including an investment of Rs 1,552.57 crore by Essar Ports and Rs 723.49 crore by the port authority, the company said in a statement. The terminal will be developed under a 30-year build-operate-transfer concession through the public-private partnership route, with Essar emerging as the highest bidder in a global competitive bidding process. The project will add capacity for handling dry and other multipurpose cargo on India's western coast, as the country seeks to expand port infrastructure to accommodate growing trade and improve logistics efficiency, it said. The proposed facility will have four berths, each measuring 300 metres, providing a total berth length of 1,200 metres

8e00001f3b35f80a.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio met Adani Group chairman Gautam Adani and Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran in Mumbai on Wednesday morning before heading to Jamnagar in Gujarat to visit Reliance Industries' giant oil-refining complex, the world's largest single-site refinery, along with Vantara and giga factories being developed by the conglomerate. Rubio, who arrived in Mumbai on Tuesday afternoon, first met Adani, followed by a meeting with Chandrasekaran, sources said. Neither side released details of the meetings. Adani heads one of India's largest conglomerates, with interests spanning ports, airports, energy, logistics and infrastructure. The group has also been expanding its renewable-energy and manufacturing businesses, sectors that are central to India's ambitions to strengthen domestic supply chains and attract global investment. Chandrasekaran, who leads Tata Sons, the Tata Group's holding company, oversees a sprawling business empire with interests in automobiles, .

The country's GDP registered modest growth alongside an increase in per capita income in dollar terms, reflecting a sluggish pace of recovery in the country's overall output compared with the previous year, the government said. In May 2026, the government had projected the economy to grow by 3.70 pc in FY26, revising its earlier estimate of 4 pc. The downward adjustment now indicates that the country fell short of its GDP target, a Dawn report showed. The revised growth rates in agriculture, industry and services in FY26 are 3.50pc, 3.34pc and 3.81pc, respectively, compared with earlier growth rates of 2.89pc, 3.51pc and 4.09 pc. Paralympics medallist Bhavina Patel, Sonalben Patel, Prachi and Sahana all went down to accomplished Paralympic medallists in their respective women's singles semifinals, while Jehan Madan bagged a bronze medal in the men's singles class 1 event by virtue of finishing fourth in a five-paddler field. The haul also took India past its medal tally from the previous edition, where it had won two bronze medals in para table tennis. Sahana and Prachi's bronze were particularly significant as they became the first Indians to win medals in the standing category at the Asian Para Games. Paralympics medallist Bhavina Patel, Sonalben Patel, Prachi and Sahana all went down to accomplished Paralympic medallists in their respective women's singles semifinals, while Jehan Madan bagged a bronze medal in the men's singles class 1 event by virtue of finishing fourth in a five-paddler field. The haul also took India past its medal tally from the previous edition, where it had won two bronze medals in para table tennis. Sahana and Prachi's bronze were particularly significant as they became the first Indians to win medals in the standing category at the Asian Para Games. Tamil Nadu's Sahana went down 8-11, 2-11, 4-11 to five-time Paralympic gold medallist Mao Jingdian of China in the Class 9 semifinal. Class 9 in para table tennis is a standing .

5d3d056af94e4cda.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Tuesday announced that India will host the first Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum by the end of this year and invited all member countries to participate in it. 129317366508a5c6.title: Shafali Verma reprimanded for breaching ICC Code of Conduct in 2nd T20I
129317366508a5c6.summary: India vice-captain Shafali Verma was on Tuesday handed an official reprimand for throwing the ball to the ground in frustration after dropping a catch during the second T20I against Zimbabwe. The 22-year-old was found to have breached Level 1 of the ICC Code of Conduct during India's nine-wicket victory in Raipur on Sunday. Verma was found to have breached Article 2.2 of the ICC Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel, which relates to "abuse of cricket equipment or clothing, ground equipment or fixtures and fittings during an International Match," an ICC media release said. In addition to this, one demerit point has been added to Verma's disciplinary record, for whom it was the first offence in a 24-month period. The incident occurred in the 12th over of Zimbabwe's innings when Verma, after dropping Chipo Mugeri-Tiripano at mid-off off Shree Charani's bowling, threw the ball to the ground in frustration. ccbf19cc8b4c46a4.title: Grocery to overtake mobiles as India's online retail market to cross $90 bn
ccbf19cc8b4c46a4.summary: India's online retail market is projected to cross USD 90 billion in 2026, registering an annual growth of 22-24 per cent, its fastest expansion in five years, driven by everyday consumption categories like grocery rather than mobile phones, Redseer Strategy Consultants said in a report. According to the analysis, e-commerce gross merchandise value (GMV) expanded roughly 25 per cent year-on-year to about USD 38 billion in the first half (H1) of 2026, marking its strongest H1 performance in four years. While online retail accelerated, mobile sales remained flat at 0 per cent growth during the first half and are projected to grow by just 2-3 per cent across the full year due to sharp price increases curbing sales volumes. Consequently, the grocery segment is poised to overtake mobile phones as the second-largest category in Indian e-commerce, behind fashion. bd7479f5fd8b87f5.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday said all institutions and political parties of the country should unite for national interest and fight together against the enemies of the country. Participating in Dussehra celebrations here, Modi also said that no matter how big or difficult a crisis may be, no one should sit back relying on others and recognise their own strength. "May our thoughts be aligned, and may... all the institutions of the nation, all political parties, stand together for national interest. We must proceed with this very spirit and we must fight together against the enemies of the country," the PM said. Underlining that his government's goal is to make India self-reliant, the prime minister said, "We must have faith in our resources. We must turn our resolve into power and find solutions through our own hard work. Because Lord Shri Ram taught us that the difficulties cannot stop our journey." He said in 'Ram Rajya', there is no discrimination against anyone and .

8fb74366d3fdbad4.summary: Vice President J D Vance declined to endorse Israeli President Benjamin Netanyahu for reelection a day after President Donald Trump endorsed the embattled Israeli leader. "The president has the most influential endorsement in American or international political history," Vance said on Monday during an interview with journalist Mark Halperin. "I endorse American candidates, and that's where I'm focused on the midterms," Vance said, while travelling to campaign for Republican Senate nominee Michael Whatley of North Carolina. "So, I'm not getting involved in Israeli elections." Vance has campaigned for a foreign leader -- then-Hungarian prime minister Viktor Orban -- last spring before the right-wing leader's party lost that country's parliamentary election. 6dc6053bbb569952.title: Just Dial Q2 profit declines 9.73% to ₹107.8 cr despite 13% revenue growth
6dc6053bbb569952.summary: Just Dial Ltd, a leading local search engine, has reported a decline of 9.73 per cent in its consolidated net profit to Rs 107.8 crore in the September quarter of FY27, on a year-on-year basis. It had posted a net profit of Rs 119.44 crore in the July-September quarter a year ago, according to a regulatory filing. However, Just Dial's revenue from operations was up 13.11 per cent in the September quarter at Rs 342.82 crore, compared to Rs 303.07 crore in the corresponding quarter a year ago. Just Dial's total expenses stood at Rs 262.81 crore, up 14.6 per cent YoY in the September quarter. The company, owned by Reliance Retail Ventures, the retail arm of billionaire Mukesh Ambani-led Reliance Industries Ltd, reported a 5.6 per cent rise in total income to Rs 397.38 crore in the second quarter of FY27. Share of Just Dial Ltd on Monday settled 2.82 per cent higher at Rs 732.55 apiece on the BSE.

20bf7e85d649d76c.title: PM Modi greets people on Vijayadashami, wishes happiness and prosperity
20bf7e85d649d76c.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday greeted people on the occasion of Vijayadashami and prayed that the festival would enrich everyone's life with happiness, prosperity, and success. "Heartiest greetings of Vijayadashami to everyone. May this festival of victory, filled with joy and faith, empower everyone's resolve with renewed strength," Modi said in a post on X in Hindi. "May every life be enriched with happiness, prosperity, and success-this is my sincere wish," he added. The festival celebrates Lord Rama's vanquishing the 10-headed demon king Ravana, and symbolises the triumph of good over evil. It is celebrated across the country with revellers coming out in large numbers to witness the burning of Ravana effigies, marking a culmination of 10 days of festivities filled with rituals, songs, dance and processions.

5cb2e7ba575b3eac.title: UN food agency cuts aid to Palestinians in Gaza, West Bank amid fund crunch
5cb2e7ba575b3eac.summary: The United Nations has cut food assistance to 5,00,000 Palestinians in Gaza and 2,00,000 in the West Bank due to a serious funding shortage, the head of the UN food agency said. Carl Skau, acting head of the World Food Program, on Monday urged the international community to provide USD 450 million so the agency could restore the cut assistance and provide hot meals and food parcels in Gaza and the West Bank for the next six months. Because of the money shortage, the number of people receiving assistance was reduced this month from 1.6 million to 1.1 million in Gaza and from 4,00,000 to 2,00,000 in the West Bank, he said. Skau, who had just visited both territories, told UN correspondents in a video briefing from Jerusalem that life in Gaza remains "absolutely brutal" and incredibly dangerous, with UN teams recording about 50 attacks per day in the past week. Nonetheless, he said that since last October's ceasefire between Israel and Hamas, "we have been able to push back on famine"

7219997d9a65701c.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat on Tuesday cautioned that regime-change agitations do not resolve fundamental problems, warning that protests could become instruments of political interests and fuel divisions in society rather than delivering solutions. Addressing the annual Vijayadashami gathering here, Bhagwat cited recent upheavals in Bangladesh, Nepal, France, and Albania, asserting that forces pursuing their own interests use regime change as a means to alter political circumstances, rarely achieving intended results. "They claim that changing a regime will change the situation, but that has never really happened," he said. Bhagwat claimed that a stronger India would constrain such forces, making the country a target of attempts to weaken and divide it. While some global powers want India to develop, they do not want it to become too powerful, as it could challenge their dominance, he added. Higher output in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan will likely largely offset crop losses in Maharashtra, according to the association's first crop estimate report. The data was shared during the concluding session of SOPA's international soybean conference in Indore on Saturday. Soybean is a key oilseed crop that provides domestic cooking oil and a protein base for the livestock and poultry industries. Overall production is estimated to decline by 2.11 per cent from the previous season, the association said. It attributed the losses in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Telangana to prolonged dry spells and moisture deficiency during critical stages of crop growth. 5cd516c86434f6f3.title: Delhi sets up DITI on lines of NITI Aayog, to act as premier advisory body
5cd516c86434f6f3.summary: Delhi government has set up Delhi Institute for Transformation and Innovation (DITI) on the lines of NITI Aayog, for policy-making under its goal of "Viksit Dilli by 2047", officials said on Saturday. DITI will function as the Delhi government's premier advisory body for public policy, development strategy and institutional reforms, an official notification said. DITI replaces the Dialogue and Development Commission (DDC) that previously served as the think tank of the city government under AAP rule. Chief Minister Rekha Gupta had announced the constitution of DITI in Delhi's budget presented in March. a722e6aae76e6979.title: Hybrids, CNG may contribute 50% of sales in 2-3 years: Renault India CEO
a722e6aae76e6979.summary: As French carmaker Renault pushes multifuel powertrain strategy in India, Renault India CEO Stephane Deblaise said hybrid and CNG technology can possibly account for almost half of the automaker's powertrain mix in its sales over the next 2-3 years. His comments came as the company bets big on hybrid and CNG technology in its India strategy. The automaker on Saturday launched its first strong hybrid offering on the Duster SUV, and plans to launch factory-fitted CNG models in the future. When asked how Renault India's powertrain mix could look over the next 2-3 years, Deblaise told PTI: "It is possible, 50 per cent is possible from hybrid and CNG, but we do not have a target." India's car market is increasingly seeing multiple powertrain technologies develop alongside each other, including hybrids, CNG and electric vehicles, rather than one single technology replacing another immediately. Automakers see hybrid technology as a practical bridge as the electric vehicle ecosystem evolve

ed44f33125f40768.title: India to keep Russian oil imports near current levels after Trump waiver
ed44f33125f40768.summary: India is expected to keep importing Russian crude at close to current levels after US President Donald Trump waived sanctions and tariffs mandated by a new law on major buyers of Russian oil, analysts said. Trump issued an executive order late on Friday waiving the "sanctions, restrictions, and duties" under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, a day before a 30-day deadline for enforcement expired. He signed the law on September 18. The law authorised tariffs of up to 100 per cent on goods from the five largest importers of Russian crude and gas, and sanctions on Russia's shadow fleet of tankers. The waiver is not specific to India and could also benefit China. The order lets the administration reconsider it later. India is the largest importer of Russian seaborne crude, averaging 1.8 million barrels per day this year, ahead of China at 1.2 million, ship tracking data showed. Italy, Turkey and the Netherlands completed the top five. India took about 1.82 million

1c694b3357c62887.title: Delhi Police files multiple FIRs over CJP's 'Lehra Do Tiranga' protest
1c694b3357c62887.summary: Delhi Police has registered multiple FIRs in connection with alleged violation of prohibitory orders in Connaught Place ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party's 'Lehra do Tiranga' protest a day ago, sources said on Saturday. "Despite repeated announcements asking people to disperse, a crowd gathered in and around Connaught Place on Friday, prompting the police to initiate legal action," said the source. The prohibitory orders, issued under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, banned mass gatherings in Connaught Place and adjoining areas. Hundreds of CJP supporters and student activists staged a series of flash protests across Connaught Place amid a massive police deployment on Friday, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

244a544fe652c0b2.title: Puja pandal stampede: PM announces ₹2 lakh ex gratia, Shah to visit injured
244a544fe652c0b2.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday said the stampede in Kolkata is extremely distressing and announced an ex gratia of Rs 2 lakh to the next of kin of each deceased and Rs 50,000 for the injured. At least 10 people are feared dead in a stampede following a crowd surge at a community Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata on Saturday evening. "The stampede in Kolkata is extremely distressing. My thoughts are with those who have lost their loved ones. May the injured recover at the earliest," Modi said in a post on X. The prime minister said the local administration is providing all possible assistance to those affected. Modi announced that an ex gratia of Rs 2 lakh will be given from the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund to the next of kin of each of those who lost their lives and Rs 50,000 to each injured person.

7df0f8c7e7e0d7b1.title: Centre revises Ladakh hill council rules, allows 7-24 elected members
7df0f8c7e7e0d7b1.summary: The Centre has amended the legal terminology, administrative structure and electoral provisions governing the Autonomous Hill Development Councils in Ladakh to align them with the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019, which led to the creation of the Union territory of Ladakh. Under the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils (Amendment) Regulation, the number of elected seats in each Council will be determined by the Ladakh administration, with a minimum of seven and a maximum of 24 seats. The administration can nominate up to four members from among women and "unrepresented communities", subject to the one-sixth limit of the population, the regulation states. The sitting Lok Sabha MP representing Ladakh will be an ex-officio member of the Councils constituted for each district. Each Council will have a term of five years from the date appointed for its first meeting, unless dissolved earlier. The term can be extended if holding elections is considered impracticable. Th
